An operating discipline of continuous human ownership of AI systems across their lifecycle, with named owners, decision rights and escalation authority to pause or retire AI behavior. Described in the episode as the complement that turns AI governance principles into enforceable decisions.
AI upskilling is role-based training that teaches employees to apply AI inside specific recurring tasks and workflows, measured by changes in the work rather than by course completion.
AL is Microsoft's programming language for Dynamics 365 Business Central, used to build extensions with tables, pages, codeunits, reports and business rules, usually in Visual Studio Code.
Alberto Ferrari is a co-founder of SQLBI, a Microsoft MVP and co-author of The Definitive Guide to DAX.

Algorithmic bias describes systematic and repeatable errors in computer systems, including AI models, that produce unfair outcomes, often by reproducing biases contained in training data, for example in hiring or policing.
The Altair 8800 is a 1975 microcomputer by MITS, programmed through front-panel toggle switches and widely seen as the first commercially successful personal computer.

As used in this m365.fm episode, Altera stands for an execution layer that operationalizes the autonomy boundary through an execution contract, turning a goal, allowed actions and evidence rules into a controlled sequence of tool calls that completes the work or escalates.
Amazon Bedrock is an AWS service for building generative AI applications and agents on foundation models.
Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3) is an object storage service from Amazon Web Services that stores data as objects in buckets; Microsoft Fabric can reference S3 data through OneLake shortcuts.
Amazon's public cloud platform offering compute, storage, networking, database and many other services. In Microsoft contexts it often appears as part of hybrid and multi-cloud environments.
AI researcher and influential voice on working with large language models, described in the episode as the person most associated with articulating the LLM Wiki pattern.

Anomaly detection identifies rare items, events or observations that deviate from expected behavior; the episode recommends dynamic baselines, for example via AI Builder, over static thresholds to reduce false positives.
A design pattern that places a translation layer between a legacy system and a new system so each keeps its own model and contracts during a migration.
Software that detects and blocks malware, traditionally by matching files against signatures of known threats.
Open-source distributed event streaming platform from the Apache Software Foundation, used for high-throughput event streams, data pipelines and analytics with the ability to replay past events.
Open-source, column-oriented file format optimized for analytics; Azure Open Datasets stores its curated public data as Parquet files.
An open-source distributed processing engine that splits large data workloads across many machines; it began at UC Berkeley and is maintained by the Apache Software Foundation.
API-first architecture designs business capabilities as stable, callable APIs before any user interface, so that user interfaces, workflow engines and AI agents consume the same operations.
An API gateway is a single entry point between clients and backend services that centrally handles routing, authentication, rate limiting, load balancing and request/response transformation.
Customizable website that is part of an Azure API Management instance, where API consumers discover APIs, read documentation, obtain subscription keys and try API calls in the browser.

Configurable rules in Azure API Management that change API request and response behavior in the gateway, for example authentication, rate limiting, caching and transformation, without changing backend code; they run in inbound, backend, outbound and on-error sections.
Extensibility model in which Copilot calls a live external API at runtime, typically to perform actions such as creating a ticket or updating a record; the data is not indexed into Microsoft 365.

An application registration in Microsoft Entra ID is the global definition of an app, describing its name, redirect URIs, token settings and requested permissions; it is used to create service principals in tenants.
The uncontrolled growth of applications in an organization, often low-code apps, without clear ownership or lifecycle management, leading to unused apps, licensing waste and a larger attack surface.
An applicant tracking system (ATS) is software that manages recruiting and hiring electronically, including searching and screening applications by keywords.

Exchange Online policies, managed with cmdlets such as New-ApplicationAccessPolicy and Test-ApplicationAccessPolicy, that restrict an app holding Microsoft Graph or EWS application permissions to a defined set of mailboxes, typically a mail-enabled security group.

Opt-in deployment model for Azure Application Gateway v2, enabled by registering a subscription feature flag, that keeps Azure management traffic off the public internet so gateways can run with a private IP only, blocked outbound internet access and custom DNS.
The application performance monitoring feature of Azure Monitor. It tracks request rates, response times, exceptions and dependency calls of applications.
Application lifecycle management (ALM) covers managing software from requirements through development, change management, continuous integration and release; the episode applies it to Power BI work.
The application server tier of Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations that runs business logic and batch jobs; heavy integration traffic through custom code adds load to the AOS.
Azure feature that groups virtual machine network interfaces by function, such as web servers, so network security group rules can reference the group instead of individual IP addresses.

Architectural debt is a form of technical debt caused by architectural decisions or uncontrolled growth, such as duplicate logic across many unmanaged apps and flows, that makes a system harder to govern and change.

The growth of possible system states, configurations and dependencies across identity, productivity and infrastructure that makes system behavior unpredictable; described in the episode across state, configuration, interaction and organizational dimensions.
An open-source, CNCF graduated GitOps continuous delivery tool for Kubernetes that compares the live cluster state with Git and offers a web UI for sync status, health and history.
A JSON file that defines Azure infrastructure and configuration for deployment through Azure Resource Manager; Bicep files are translated into ARM templates before deployment.
ASP.NET Core is Microsoft's cross-platform framework for building web apps, web APIs and backend services on .NET.
Microsoft's server-side web application framework on .NET, with programming models such as Web Forms, MVC and Web API built on a shared request pipeline of HTTP modules and handlers.
An industrial standard for the digital description of an individual asset; it complements OPC UA device data and can be linked into product and process context.
A message delivery guarantee in which a message is not silently lost but may be delivered more than once, so consumers must handle duplicates idempotently.
A Nordic and Baltic IT infrastructure and services company headquartered in Norway, where Christoffer Besler Hansen leads AI Workplace.
Analysis of possible routes an attacker could take from a weak point to a sensitive resource, including choke points where one fix closes several paths.
A Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 feature that sends realistic simulated phishing to users and assigns follow-up training based on their behaviour.
Rules in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint that block risky software behaviors commonly abused by malware, such as macros in Office files downloaded from the internet.

An access control model that grants or denies access by evaluating attributes of the user, the resource and the environment, such as role, device health and location, against policies at request time.
Audience targeting in SharePoint shows navigation links, news, pages and supported web parts only to specified Microsoft 365 or security groups, so content reaches the people it is relevant to.

The ability of an organization to produce defensible, retained evidence that its controls existed, were active and worked over time, quickly enough to answer auditors and regulators without manual reconstruction.

Authentication strength is a Microsoft Entra Conditional Access control that specifies which combinations of authentication methods, such as phishing-resistant methods, a user must use to access a resource.
The cognitive bias of giving more weight to an output or opinion because it appears authoritative; with AI, fluent and complete-looking answers can end debate without being right.
The most common OAuth 2.0 flow for user sign-in: the browser receives a short-lived, single-use code that the app exchanges server-side for an access token.
Auto capture in Dynamics 365 Sales finds emails and meetings related to customer records and suggests them to the seller for review and tracking in the CRM.

Auto-labeling applies or recommends Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels automatically, either client-side in Office apps while content is created or service-side through policies that scan SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange; service-side policies run in simulation before they are enforced.

desc.fr: Framework open source de Microsoft Research pour orchestrer plusieurs agents IA qui collaborent et se passent des tâches.

desc.en: A technique that tries many algorithms and settings on a dataset in parallel and returns the best-performing model for a defined prediction target.
A Microsoft Defender XDR capability that uses high-confidence signals to automatically contain compromised devices or accounts and stop an attack in progress, such as ransomware, before it spreads.
Automation bias is the tendency of people to over-rely on outputs from automated systems and to trust them more than their own judgment, especially under time pressure.
An AI agent that runs on its own in response to triggers or schedules rather than in a conversation with a user, for example in Copilot Studio; it can use reasoning to decide its next steps.

An architectural pattern described in the episode in which a Microsoft 365 tenant acts as a unified control plane, with Entra ID for identity policy, Dataverse for business state, Power Automate for orchestration and Copilot Studio for intent, so that processes run deterministically without human operators in the data flow.

The autonomy boundary is the explicit decision line between recommendation and action, where an AI agent stops producing text, options and plans and starts changing systems, for example through Graph calls, configuration changes or closing tickets.
An Azure feature that logically groups virtual machines inside one datacenter across fault domains and update domains so they do not all fail or restart together.
Physically separate locations within an Azure region, each with its own power, cooling and networking, used to spread workloads so a failure in one zone does not take down every instance.
Available to promise is planning logic that checks whether a quantity can be committed to a customer on a given date based on inventory and planned supply.

A host pool in Azure Virtual Desktop is a collection of Azure virtual machines registered as session hosts; host pools are either pooled, shared by multiple users, or personal, with a dedicated machine per user.
AWS Direct Connect is an Amazon Web Services offering that provides a dedicated private network connection from on-premises or colocation facilities to AWS without traversing the public internet.
AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) controls access to AWS resources through users, roles and policies; IAM Identity Center adds single sign-on and MFA across AWS accounts.

Azure Active Directory B2C, Microsoft's earlier customer identity service for consumer-facing apps, configured with user flows or XML-based custom policies and succeeded by Microsoft Entra External ID.
Azure AD Graph is the legacy Microsoft directory API that Microsoft deprecated and retired in favor of Microsoft Graph. It did not provide API-level activity logging.

Azure Advisor is a free, built-in Azure service that analyzes resource configuration and usage and gives personalized recommendations across cost, security, reliability, performance and operational excellence.

desc.ru: Сервис Azure для фильтрации вредоносного, непристойного и оскорбительного контента во входящих запросах и ответах моделей ИИ.

desc.en: A Microsoft AI service that takes documents, images and other content and returns structured results based on fields defined in a schema, so business processes can use the extracted information.

Azure AI Document Intelligence, formerly Azure Form Recognizer, is a cloud AI service with prebuilt and custom models that extract text, key-value pairs, tables and structure from documents through REST APIs and SDKs.
Microsoft family of prebuilt AI APIs on Azure, formerly Azure Cognitive Services, covering vision, speech, language and decision capabilities that apps and flows can call.
Azure API Center is an Azure service for building a central inventory of an organization's APIs and MCP servers, so that they can be registered, described, governed and discovered for reuse.
Managed Azure service that centralizes application settings and feature flags as key-value pairs so multiple applications can share and update configuration.

The set of compute resources an Azure App Service app runs on; it defines the operating system, region, number and size of instances and the pricing tier, and all apps in a plan share and scale with it.
Layer 7 web traffic load balancer in Azure that understands HTTP and HTTPS, routes requests by web rules and can handle TLS termination before traffic reaches back-end servers.
Microsoft service that connects servers and Kubernetes clusters running outside Azure, for example on-premises or at the edge, to Azure management.
The Azure DevOps package management service that hosts private feeds for NuGet, npm, Maven, Python and Universal packages and can proxy public upstream sources.

Azure Automation State Configuration is a configuration management service based on PowerShell Desired State Configuration (DSC) that keeps machines in a defined desired state and reports their compliance; Microsoft is moving this capability to Azure Machine Configuration.

Azure capability that automatically adds or removes instances, for example in a virtual machine scale set, based on metric rules, schedules or predictive patterns within a defined minimum and maximum.
Azure Backup protection that keeps deleted backup items and recovery points in a soft-deleted state for a retention period, so they can be restored instead of being lost immediately.

Azure Backup is Microsoft's managed cloud backup service that protects Azure VMs, databases, file shares, blobs, disks and on-premises servers, storing recovery points in a vault with policy-based retention.
Microsoft's object storage service for unstructured data, offering hot, cool, cold and archive access tiers that trade lower storage charges for higher access costs or rehydration delays.
The Azure DevOps service for planning and tracking work with work items, backlogs, sprints, queries, dashboards and Kanban boards.

desc.de: Azure-Dienst, bei dem Bots und Agenten registriert werden; er terminiert Kanalprotokolle und leitet Aktivitäten aus Teams, Webchat oder Copilot Studio an einen einzigen Endpunkt weiter.

desc.en: The Azure command-line tool used to sign in to Azure and create and manage Azure resources from a terminal, including inside WSL.
Azure Cloud Shell is an interactive, authenticated, browser-accessible shell for managing Azure resources with Bash or PowerShell, with Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell preinstalled.
Azure service that provisions large pools of virtual machine capacity in one request by mixing several acceptable VM sizes and Spot and standard (on-demand) pricing models.
Azure Compute Gallery is a library for approved virtual machine images that organizes image definitions and versions and can replicate image versions to the Azure regions where they are used.

The lightweight agent installed on servers outside Azure to connect them to Azure Arc. It connects outbound over HTTPS, handles extensions and reports inventory so the machine appears as an Azure resource.
Azure Container Apps is a fully managed, serverless container platform built on Kubernetes, KEDA, Dapr and Envoy, where Microsoft runs the underlying cluster and apps can scale to zero.
Azure Container Storage is a volume management and orchestration service for containers on Kubernetes, including AKS. Version 2 uses local NVMe disks of the cluster nodes as backing storage.
Specialized agents in Azure Copilot for migration, deployment, optimization, observability, resiliency and troubleshooting that reason over Azure resources and act only with approval.
A fully managed Azure service (ADX) for fast analysis of large volumes of log and telemetry data, queried with Kusto Query Language; KQL databases in Fabric share its Kusto engine heritage.

Microsoft's cloud-based data integration service for orchestrating data movement and transforming data at scale with pipelines, activities, linked services, datasets, integration runtimes and triggers. Data Factory in Microsoft Fabric is described by Microsoft as its next generation.
Azure Data Lake Storage is a set of capabilities on Azure Blob Storage for storing large volumes of data for analytics workloads.

name: Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server

desc.en: A fully managed Azure database service built on the community PostgreSQL engine, offering Burstable, General Purpose and Memory Optimized compute tiers.
A first-party managed Apache Spark analytics service on Azure, built by Microsoft and Databricks, for data engineering, analytics and machine learning on data kept in your own storage.

Azure DDoS Protection is an Azure service that defends Azure resources against distributed denial-of-service attacks at the network layer, complementing application-layer protection such as Azure Web Application Firewall.

An Azure service that reserves an entire physical server in an Azure datacenter for one subscription, on which the customer places compatible virtual machines with host-level isolation and maintenance control.

A deployment stack is an Azure resource that manages a group of resources defined in a Bicep or ARM template as one unit, tracking what it owns and deleting or detaching resources removed from the template; deny settings can block changes outside the stack.
The Azure Developer CLI (azd) is an open-source command-line tool that provides a consistent workflow to create environments, provision Azure resources and deploy application code.

An Azure service that represents connected devices and industrial assets as Azure resources, so they can be registered, discovered and governed across edge and cloud, for example with Azure IoT Operations.

An Azure platform service for building a live graph of digital twins, defined with DTDL models, that represents entities and relationships of a real environment and can be queried and routed as events.
An Azure-specific DNS record that points a name directly at an Azure resource, such as a load balancer or CDN endpoint, and updates automatically when the resource's IP address changes.

Azure Elastic SAN is a managed storage area network service in Azure that provides pooled high-performance block storage, organized into volume groups and volumes that workloads connect to over iSCSI.

Azure Event Grid is a fully managed publish-subscribe service in Azure that routes events from publishers such as Azure services or custom apps to subscribed handlers over HTTP or MQTT, with push and pull delivery.
Azure File Sync caches files from Azure Files on local Windows servers, giving on-premises users local performance while Azure Files remains the source of truth.

Azure Firewall is a cloud-native network firewall service that protects Azure virtual network resources by inspecting addresses, ports and protocols; it is a different service from Azure Web Application Firewall.

Global Azure service that combines content delivery and layer 7 load balancing at Microsoft edge locations, with a built-in web application firewall; it is often placed in front of regional Application Gateways.

Serverless hosting plan for Azure Functions that bills only for executions and execution time (GB-seconds) while functions run, with a monthly free grant. Functions on this plan have a default timeout of five minutes and a maximum of ten.

Triggers define the event that starts an Azure Function, and every function has exactly one trigger. Optional input and output bindings declaratively connect a function to data sources and services without writing SDK connection code.
Azure HorizonDB is Microsoft's managed, PostgreSQL-compatible database service built for AI workloads, with vector search, embeddings and AI functions available directly in SQL.
Azure Hybrid Benefit is a licensing benefit that lets organizations bring eligible on-premises Windows Server and SQL Server licenses with Software Assurance to Azure for reduced rates.
Azure Image Builder is an Azure service that creates customized virtual machine images from a set of instructions you define, using HashiCorp Packer behind the scenes.

Azure Integration Services is Microsoft's collection of Azure services for enterprise integration, including Azure Logic Apps, API Management, Service Bus, Event Grid and, depending on the definition, Azure Functions.

Azure IoT Edge is a feature of Azure IoT Hub that runs containerized modules on edge devices, managed from the cloud. It supports offline operation and synchronizes telemetry and configuration when connectivity returns.

name: Azure IoT Hub Device Provisioning Service (DPS)

desc.en: An Azure helper service for IoT Hub that verifies a device's proof of identity against enrollment rules on first boot and assigns it to an IoT hub using an allocation policy, enabling zero-touch provisioning.
Azure IoT Hub is a managed Azure service that acts as a central message hub between IoT applications and devices, with device identities and device-to-cloud and cloud-to-device messaging.
Microsoft edge data platform that runs on Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes and provides OPC UA connectivity, a local MQTT broker and data flows for industrial sites.
Azure Kubernetes Service is Microsoft's managed Kubernetes offering: Microsoft runs the control plane, while customers choose and pay for the worker node virtual machines that run their containers.
An Azure service that lets a service provider or enterprise manage resources in other Azure tenants through delegated resource management, without accounts in those tenants.
Layer 4 Azure load-balancing service that distributes TCP and UDP traffic across virtual machines or scale set instances and uses health probes to send traffic only to healthy instances.

Azure Machine Learning is a Microsoft cloud service for managing the machine learning lifecycle, including training jobs, experiment tracking, model registration and managed batch and online endpoints.

A management group is a container above Azure subscriptions that lets organizations arrange many subscriptions into one hierarchy; access and policies assigned there are inherited by every subscription underneath.

Cloud-based geospatial service suite in Microsoft Azure; in Power BI the Azure Maps visual replaces the deprecated Bing Maps-based map and filled map visuals and must be enabled in the tenant settings.

Microsoft's open-source implementation of the Model Context Protocol for Azure, letting MCP-compatible AI agents and clients work with Azure resources such as Storage, Cosmos DB, Azure Monitor and App Configuration through natural language.

Azure Migrate is a free Microsoft service and hub that discovers on-premises servers, databases and web apps, assesses their readiness, sizing and cost for Azure, maps dependencies and helps carry out the migration.

A lightweight agent installed inside Azure, on-premises or other-cloud machines that collects guest OS metrics and logs for Azure Monitor using data collection rules. It replaces the retired Log Analytics agent.
Interactive reports in Azure Monitor that combine text, metrics, logs and parameters into custom dashboards.
Azure's monitoring service that collects metrics and logs from cloud and on-premises resources; its log half is Log Analytics.
Azure GPU virtual machine series built on NVIDIA Grace CPUs and Blackwell GPUs for deep learning training, generative AI and HPC workloads.

A collection of Azure Policy definitions grouped into a single assignable object (also called a policy set), used for example to apply regulatory frameworks such as ISO 27001 or NIST at a management group scope.
Azure Policy is the Azure service for defining rules (policy definitions, bundled as initiatives) that are assigned to a scope and inherited downward, to audit, deny, modify or deploy resources.
The Azure portal is Microsoft's web-based console for creating and managing Azure resources and subscriptions through a graphical interface.

Azure Private 5G Core is an Azure service for deploying and managing 5G core network functions on Azure Stack Edge as part of an on-premises private mobile network. Microsoft Learn lists its retirement for September 30, 2025.
An Azure DNS zone whose records resolve only inside the Azure virtual networks linked to it, optionally with automatic registration of virtual machine records.
Microsoft's cloud quantum computing service in Azure, which includes the Quantum Development Kit and the Azure Quantum Resource Estimator.

A simple message queue service inside an Azure Storage account that decouples application components; messages are small (up to 64 KB) and are typically processed asynchronously by background workers.
Azure RBAC is the authorization system built on Azure Resource Manager that grants access to Azure resources through role assignments combining a security principal, a role definition and a scope.
Pairs of Azure regions, usually in the same geography, used for geo-redundant storage replication, staggered platform updates and prioritized recovery; pairing alone is not a disaster recovery plan.

Azure Relay is an Azure service that exposes services in a private network to the cloud without opening inbound firewall ports; the on-premises data gateway uses it to pick up queued requests over outbound connections.
The Azure DevOps service for Git-based version control, with branches, pull requests and code review linked to work items.
A commitment-based purchase option that lowers the price of eligible Azure services, including Fabric capacity, in exchange for committing to specific usage for a one- or three-year term.

Azure service that lets you query resources across subscriptions at scale using a subset of the Kusto Query Language. It extends Azure Resource Manager with its own index of resource data and is used by Resource Graph Explorer in the Azure portal.

A resource group is a logical container in Azure Resource Manager that holds related resources sharing the same lifecycle, permissions and policies; every Azure resource belongs to exactly one resource group.
Management locks in Azure Resource Manager protect subscriptions, resource groups or resources from accidental deletion (delete lock) or modification (read-only lock), regardless of user permissions.
The deployment and management layer of Azure that accepts commands to create, update and delete resources and keeps track of what you own.
Tags are key-value metadata pairs attached to Azure resources, resource groups and subscriptions to organize them and to group costs by project, department, environment or owner.

Routing preference in Azure lets customers choose whether traffic is routed over the Microsoft global network (cold potato routing) or handed off to transit ISPs over the public internet (hot potato routing).
A commitment discount where you commit to a fixed hourly spend on eligible Azure compute or database services for one or three years; unused hourly commitment does not roll over.

Microsoft-managed labels, such as Internet, VirtualNetwork or AzureLoadBalancer, that represent groups of IP address prefixes and can be used in network security group rules; Microsoft updates the underlying ranges automatically.

Azure Site Recovery (ASR) is Microsoft's managed disaster recovery service that continuously replicates whole servers to a secondary location so workloads can fail over and fail back during an outage.
Azure virtual machines that run on unused Azure capacity at a discount and can be evicted when Azure needs the capacity back, suited to interruption-tolerant workloads.
Microsoft's managed relational database service in Azure.
A group of Azure SQL databases that share one fixed set of resources for one price, suited to databases with low average use and short, non-overlapping spikes.
A managed Azure database option with close to full SQL Server compatibility, recommended by Microsoft for most migrations of existing SQL Server applications.

Azure Stack Edge is a Microsoft-supplied edge appliance that brings Azure compute, storage, networking and hardware-accelerated machine learning to on-premises and edge locations. It is managed through the Azure portal.
The top-level Azure resource that provides a globally unique namespace for storage data such as blobs, with its own performance tier, redundancy setting and access keys.

The replication options for Azure Storage data: locally redundant storage (LRS) keeps three copies in one datacenter, zone-redundant storage (ZRS) spreads them across availability zones, and geo-redundant options (GRS, GZRS) add a copy in a secondary region.
Fully managed real-time analytics service in Azure that analyzes and processes fast-moving streams of data, for example from Azure Event Hubs, using a SQL-based query language.

An Azure subscription is the logical container in which Azure resources are created; it is the unit for billing, quotas and access or policy assignments and is linked to exactly one Microsoft Entra tenant.

Azure analytics service that combines data warehousing and big data analytics; its serverless SQL pool can query files such as public Azure Open Datasets directly with OPENROWSET without provisioning storage.
A schemaless NoSQL key-value store in Azure Storage for structured data, where entities are looked up by partition key and row key.
The Azure DevOps service for planned manual and exploratory testing, organizing test cases into test suites and test plans with bugs linked back to Azure Boards.

Azure-native service that assesses, schedules, installs and tracks operating system updates for Windows and Linux servers in Azure, on-premises and other clouds via Azure Arc. It replaces Azure Automation Update Management.
A Microsoft-backed initiative that defines quality standards for infrastructure-as-code modules and publishes supported Bicep and Terraform modules for deploying Azure resources.
Azure service for running and managing a group of identical or flexible, load-balanced virtual machines whose instance count can grow or shrink with demand or on a schedule.
Azure's infrastructure-as-a-service offering for renting virtual computers in Microsoft's cloud with a chosen size, operating system and configuration.

Azure Virtual Network Manager is a centralized Azure service for grouping, configuring and managing virtual networks across subscriptions, covering IP address management, connectivity, security admin rules and routing.
The fundamental building block for private networks in Azure; you assign it a private address range and carve subnets from it, with Azure reserving five addresses in every subnet.

Azure security service (WAF) that inspects web requests and blocks common attacks such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting; it can run on Azure Application Gateway or Azure Front Door in detection or prevention mode.
Microsoft's design guidance for building quality Azure workloads, with explained design patterns such as circuit breaker that help make solutions resilient, available and recoverable.
Business-to-business collaboration in Microsoft Entra that adds external users to a directory as guest objects so they can access apps and resources.
Microsoft Azure MVP from the Netherlands whose observations on cloud rollouts, landing zones and policy are referenced in this episode.
Reading printed barcodes or QR codes with a camera or scanner to capture data in a structured way instead of typing it manually.
BCC, The Business Collaboration Company, is a software vendor that provides tools for governance, security and automation in Microsoft 365.

A BI or analytics Center of Excellence is an internal team of technical and business experts that sets standards, mentors users and guides governance for self-service and enterprise BI, as described in the Microsoft Fabric adoption roadmap.
A Bicep file called from another Bicep file as a reusable building block, passing values between modules through parameters and outputs.
A deployment preview that compares a Bicep file with the resources already in Azure and shows what would be created, modified or deleted, without making any changes.
A bill of materials lists the components, raw materials and other inputs, with quantities, that are needed to make a product; together with the routing it tells planning what an operation consumes.
Billennium is a Polish IT services company headquartered in Warsaw and a Microsoft partner; in this episode it is named as the employer of guest Edyta Gorzoń.
Microsoft web mapping service whose technology powered the classic Power BI map and filled map visuals; the episode explains its deprecation in Power BI and the move to Azure Maps.
BitLocker is the full-volume drive encryption feature built into Windows. On a dev box the disk is already encrypted, so enabling BitLocker manually can lock users out.
Blazor is Microsoft's ASP.NET Core framework for building interactive web UIs from strongly typed components in C#; the episode pairs it with OpenAPI contracts to keep front end and back end aligned.
A SharePoint and OneDrive site policy that lets users view files in the browser while preventing them from downloading, printing or syncing the content.
BM25 (Okapi BM25) is a classic sparse ranking function that scores documents by exact term overlap with a query; it is commonly combined with vector search in hybrid retrieval.
The standard routing protocol for exchanging routing and reachability information between networks; ExpressRoute gateways and circuits use it to share routes automatically.
A network of compromised internet-connected devices controlled remotely by attackers, commonly used to launch DDoS attacks.

The resource or process step that limits how much work can pass through a production system in a given period; after a disruption the bottleneck can shift to another machine, inspection step, tool or person.
Bring your own device (BYOD) is the practice of employees using personally owned phones, tablets or laptops for work, which requires separating and protecting corporate data on those devices.

Broken object level authorization is an API vulnerability in which a user can access another user's records by changing an object ID in a request because no per-object authorization check is enforced.

Germany's federal agency for information security (Bundesamt für Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik). Its requirements and standards define what auditors expect from Microsoft 365 deployments in critical infrastructure and government.
A resilience design pattern that isolates resources such as connection pools, worker capacity or queues per dependency or workload, so a failure in one part cannot exhaust resources needed by others.
Occupational burnout is a state of exhaustion and disengagement resulting from chronic workplace stress that has not been successfully managed.
Agent Designer is a capability in Dynamics 365 Business Central for creating custom AI agents from plain-language instructions, an assigned profile and permissions, initially in sandbox environments.
Separate installable apps, written in AL, that add fields, pages, actions, rules and integrations to Dynamics 365 Business Central without modifying the standard base application.
A fraud attack in which an attacker impersonates or takes over a trusted mailbox to trick people into moving money, for example by changing bank details or approving payments.
A business process flow is the process bar shown across a Dynamics 365 record that guides users through defined stages, such as qualify, develop, propose and close for sales opportunities.
The bystander effect is a social psychology phenomenon in which individuals are less likely to act when other people are present, because responsibility is diffused across the group.

Caching keeps frequently accessed data in fast memory so repeated queries do not have to read from slower storage; in analytics platforms such as Microsoft Fabric it is a key lever for query performance.
A calculated column is a column added to a Power BI table using a DAX formula; its values are computed row by row and stored in the model, increasing model size and refresh work.
Calculation groups are a tabular model feature that applies reusable DAX calculation items, such as time intelligence, to many measures and so reduces redundant measures.
A deployment technique that routes a small percentage of production traffic to a new version, compares it against the stable version and gradually increases the share or rolls back automatically.

CAPA (corrective and preventive action) is a formal quality process that addresses the cause of a nonconformance so it does not recur (corrective action) and addresses potential problems before they occur (preventive action).

Capable to promise is an order promising approach in which the delivery date is derived from what the factory can currently do given material, routing, resource, labor and shipping limits, rather than from a static lead time.
A capacity profile in Dynamics 365 unified routing sets the amount and type of work an agent can handle at the same time, such as a number of concurrent chats or emails.
A team game in which each side defends its own flag while trying to capture the opposing team's flag; used in the episode to expose communication gaps under time pressure.

Carbon removal (carbon dioxide removal) takes CO2 out of the atmosphere through deliberate human activity and stores it durably, for example via afforestation, soil carbon or direct air capture; companies buy removal credits to counterbalance residual emissions in net claims.
In Power BI data modeling, cardinality describes how often values can repeat on each side of a relationship: one-to-many, many-to-one, one-to-one or many-to-many.
Cash flow forecasting estimates a business's future cash inflows and outflows over a period so that finance teams can anticipate liquidity problems and plan decisions.
A trusted entity in a public key infrastructure that issues and signs digital certificates; a root CA typically anchors trust while an issuing CA signs certificates for devices and users.
Chain-of-thought reasoning is a technique in which a language model works through intermediate reasoning steps, such as outlining and evaluating options, before producing its final answer.
A group of trained employees who carry adoption of a new platform such as Microsoft 365 or Copilot into their own teams through peer support and real workflows.
Chaos engineering is the practice of deliberately injecting controlled failures into a system to test hypotheses about its resilience and to find weaknesses before real outages occur.

Character drift is the loss of a character's visual identity (face, proportions, outfit) across frames or shots in AI-generated video, typically caused by inconsistent references, prompts or excessive motion.
A FinOps practice of actually billing each team or cost center for the technology costs allocated to it through an internal budget transfer.
Charles Lamanna is a Microsoft executive who has led Business Applications, Power Platform and Business & Industry Copilot.
The list of accounts used in a company's general ledger, each typically with a name and number, that categorizes money movements such as sales income, rent or supplier debt.
A chatbot is a conversational interface that answers user questions by retrieving or generating responses, typically used for FAQs and support ticket deflection.

The senior executive responsible for an organization's information security strategy and program; in Microsoft 365 design discussions the CISO's need for strong controls must be balanced with compliance and user productivity.
Child flows in Power Automate are reusable flows called from a parent flow, used to encapsulate shared logic such as error classification, context enrichment or logging.
Chunking is the practice of splitting documents into smaller, coherent pieces before embedding and indexing them for retrieval, which strongly influences the precision of RAG answers.
Churn prediction uses AI models to estimate how likely a customer is to stop buying, cancel or disengage, as a signal for where a team should look first.

A CI/CD pipeline is an automated, fixed sequence of steps (trigger, build, test, artifact, deploy) that runs the same way every time software changes, combining continuous integration with continuous delivery or deployment.
CI/CD combines continuous integration, testing every change as it is made, with continuous delivery, automatically shipping the tested result to where it needs to go.

An IP address allocation and notation method introduced by RFC 1519 in 1993 that replaced fixed address classes, allowing blocks of any power-of-two size written as an address plus a slash prefix length.
A resilience design pattern in which an application stops repeatedly calling a dependency that is already failing, preventing one problem from spreading through the rest of the workload.
A business user without a professional development background who builds apps or automations, for example with Power Platform, close to the processes they know; Microsoft also calls them makers.
Partner Center model in which partners submit claims, backed by proof of execution, to associate themselves with customers whose purchase or usage of Microsoft products they influence.
Anthropic's agentic coding tool; named in the episode as one of the platforms that can run portable agent skills alongside GitHub Copilot and Copilot Studio.
Claude is a family of large language models developed by Anthropic; in the episode it is described as strong for developer tasks and deeper reasoning.

A software design approach associated with Robert C. Martin (Uncle Bob) that splits a system into decoupled modules with clear interfaces and a single purpose each; it applies to low-code solutions as well as pro-code.
An SAP extension approach that avoids modifying SAP standard code and instead extends the system through released APIs and side-by-side apps so upgrades stay predictable.

OAuth 2.0 grant in the Microsoft identity platform that lets a confidential client such as a background service authenticate with its own identity (secret or certificate) and application permissions instead of impersonating a user.

A client secret is a password-like credential an application uses to prove its identity to Microsoft Entra ID; it should be treated as an exception and replaced by managed identities, federation or certificates where possible.
Client-side evaluation is when Entity Framework Core runs parts of a query in application memory instead of translating them to SQL, which can pull large amounts of data and hurt performance.

An operating approach in which planning, shop-floor execution, measurement, learning and replanning form a continuous feedback loop, so schedules are revised from the current production state instead of staying static after release.

The CLOUD Act (Clarifying Lawful Overseas Use of Data Act) is a 2018 US law that lets US law enforcement compel US-based technology providers, via warrant or subpoena, to produce data in their possession, custody or control even when it is stored outside the United States.

A central team of cloud experts that defines standards and governance for cloud adoption. The episode warns that a CCoE without real workloads or enforcement authority becomes documentation rather than a control plane.
The ongoing practice of reducing cloud waste, for example by rightsizing or scheduling idle resources to shut down, funded as a recurring activity rather than a one-time phase.

Feature of Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps that finds the cloud apps in use across an organization, either continuously via Defender for Endpoint or from uploaded firewall and proxy logs, and rates them against the app catalog.
Egress is data leaving a cloud provider's network, region or zone boundary; unlike most inbound traffic it is commonly billed per gigabyte.

As used in the episode, cloud erosion is the gradual drift between the intended and the actual state of a cloud environment as an organization scales, driven by velocity, complexity and policy exceptions.
A Power Automate workflow that runs on Microsoft's servers, starts from a trigger and connects apps and services through connectors.
Power Automate flows that run in Microsoft's cloud and connect services to each other through connectors, as opposed to desktop flows that drive a machine's screen.
A Windows Hello for Business trust model in which the cloud account system hands out Kerberos tickets directly, so no certificates are needed; Microsoft recommends it for typical hybrid deployments.
Moving workloads, data and applications from on-premises systems into a cloud platform; the episode argues it is a continuous process rather than a project with an end date.
Continuous assessment of cloud resource configurations to find exposures such as weak network rules, missing encryption or excessive access.

The Cloud Solution Provider (CSP) program lets Microsoft partners resell Microsoft cloud services such as Microsoft 365, Azure and Dynamics 365 and manage billing, support and provisioning for their customers, either as direct-bill partners or as indirect resellers through a provider.
A single ready-made PowerShell command named with a verb-noun pattern, such as Get-MgUser.

CMMC is a US Department of Defense certification program that checks whether defense contractors can protect controlled unclassified information; CMMC 2.0 requires level 2 compliance based on NIST SP 800-171 controls.
A computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) holds work orders and maintenance history and supports organizing and documenting maintenance work.

Microsoft's supported model in which a Windows device is managed by Configuration Manager and Microsoft Intune at the same time, with workload sliders deciding which tool is the authority for each management area.
Co-sell is Microsoft's partner motion in which eligible partner solutions are made visible to and recommended by Microsoft's sales teams and other partners, managed through Partner Center.
A self-contained, reusable custom control built with the Power Apps component framework, defined by a manifest and lifecycle methods and packaged in a Dataverse solution.
Code interpreter is a setting for prompts in Copilot Studio and Power Platform prompt builder that lets a prompt generate and run code, for example for data analysis and chart creation.

name: Code Interpreter (Azure AI Foundry Agent Service tool)

desc.te: Azure AI Foundry ఏజెంట్లకు అందుబాటులో ఉన్న టూల్; సురక్షిత శాండ్‌బాక్స్‌లో Python కోడ్‌ను నడిపి లెక్కలు, డేటా విశ్లేషణ, చార్ట్‌లు మరియు ఫైళ్లను రూపొందిస్తుంది.

desc.en: A software quality practice in which people other than the author examine source code changes, typically pull requests, before they are merged.

A Microsoft toolkit for Power Platform Centers of Excellence that collects inventory data about environments, apps and flows to support governance; in the episode it is described as no longer receiving updates.
The mental effort placed on working memory by a task; cognitive load theory distinguishes intrinsic, extraneous and germane load.
The extra delay when a serverless platform that has scaled down to zero must rebuild the environment before it can handle the next request.
Dataverse feature that secures individual columns and grants read, create or update on them through column (field) security profiles assigned to users or teams; unauthorized users see masked values.
A command-line interface lets users interact with software by typing text commands in a terminal, which favors precision, scripting and repeatability over discoverability.

The Commerce Scale Unit hosts the headless commerce engine of Dynamics 365 Commerce, applying the same business logic for all channels through APIs; it can run as a Microsoft-managed cloud service or as a self-hosted unit closer to a store.
Commoditization is the process by which a once specialized, differentiated capability becomes standardized and interchangeable, so that buyers compare providers mainly on price.

Public reference system that assigns identifiers to publicly known software security vulnerabilities. A CVE says a weakness exists in certain software versions but not how urgent it is for a specific organization.
Comms vNext is a community-run conference in Denver focused on unified communications and Microsoft Teams, co-founded by Microsoft MVPs including Josh Blalock.

desc.es: Solución de Microsoft Purview que analiza comunicaciones, incluidos prompts y respuestas de Copilot, para detectar contenido inapropiado o posibles conductas indebidas.

desc.en: The practice of expressing compliance requirements and controls as machine-readable code that is version-controlled, tested and enforced automatically, so drift is detected and remediated continuously instead of through manual reviews.
A grouping of controls from one regulation, standard or policy in Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager, with its own score, status and exportable report.

A solution in Microsoft Purview that helps organizations assess and manage compliance across cloud services through assessments, regulatory templates, improvement actions and a risk-weighted compliance score.

A percentage in Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager built from points earned by completing risk-weighted improvement actions, including actions Microsoft manages; it tracks progress and is not a certificate of compliance.
The appearance of control without the substance of enforcement: policies, labels and DLP rules that exist on paper but are not applied, deployed or monitored in the tenant.

In RevoScaleR, the compute context defines where R computations run, for example locally or inside a SQL Server instance. Running in the SQL Server compute context keeps processing next to the data instead of moving rows over the network.

A computer-using agent is an AI agent that reads a graphical user interface and operates it like a human by clicking, typing and navigating, which lets agents work with legacy systems that have no API.

A machine learning term for changes over time in the underlying definition or distribution of what a model is trying to predict, which erodes model accuracy unless the model is monitored and retrained.
Condition monitoring measures physical indicators of equipment health, such as vibration or temperature, to detect changes that may point to a developing fault.

Authentication context is a Microsoft Entra Conditional Access feature that applies step-up requirements, such as a fresh MFA challenge, to specific sensitive actions or resources instead of a whole app, for example each PIM role activation.

Report-only mode is a Conditional Access policy state in Microsoft Entra ID in which policies are evaluated at sign-in and their results logged, but not enforced, so administrators can assess impact before turning them on.

Excel feature that automatically changes the appearance of cells based on rules about their values, for example to highlight outliers; Copilot in Excel can create such rules from natural-language prompts.
An estimate attached to an individual AI extraction result that indicates how sure the system is about that value; it is not a guarantee that the value is correct.

Confidential computing protects data in use by processing it inside hardware-based, attested trusted execution environments (TEEs), so that code outside the TEE, including host administrators and the cloud operator, cannot read or alter it.
Configuration drift is the gradual gap between the intended, documented state of infrastructure and its actual running state, typically caused by manual changes made outside infrastructure as code.
Microsoft's on-premises device management product. In co-management with Intune, workload sliders decide which system owns Windows Update policies.
Atlassian's web-based corporate wiki; in the episode an on-premises Confluence is indexed with Azure AI Search as a knowledge source for a Copilot Studio agent.
Copilot Studio capability in which a separately published agent can be called by other (parent) agents during orchestration, with its own lifecycle, settings and authentication configuration.
Partner organizations declared in Microsoft Entra entitlement management by domain or identity provider, whose users may request specific access packages under a policy.

desc.ar: مراجع داخل حلول Power Platform تربط التطبيقات والتدفقات باتصالات الموصلات، ويجب إعادة تعيينها في كل بيئة مستهدفة عند الاستيراد.

desc.en: Consent management is the process of obtaining, recording and respecting a person's permission for the collection and use of their data, for example for marketing communications by channel, brand or purpose.

A production scheduling approach that places each operation on a real resource and time slot only when hard constraints such as machine capability, tooling, labor skills, material release and precedence are met, then compares feasible options against business objectives.
A read-only, layered template that holds an application, its files and its start instructions; containers are the running instances started from an image.

Container labels are sensitivity labels applied to Microsoft Teams, Microsoft 365 groups and SharePoint sites; they set workspace rules such as privacy, guest access, external sharing and access from unmanaged devices, but do not label the files inside.
A service that stores container images so they can be pushed, shared and pulled by others; registries can be public or run privately.
A software container packages an application together with everything it needs to run and shares the host operating system, so it runs the same way on a laptop, a server or in the cloud.
SharePoint Premium capability that generates documents or content from templates filled with metadata fields, such as image cards built from tagged library columns.
An evaluation of stored content that goes beyond mapping by examining its structure, actual usage behavior and business context to decide what to keep, improve or archive.
A content delivery network is a geographically distributed set of servers that caches static content close to users to reduce latency and load on the origin.
Endorsement lets owners promote Power BI and Fabric items such as semantic models and lets authorized reviewers certify them as official, trusted content.
Content explorer is a Microsoft Purview tool that shows where sensitive and labeled content is stored across Microsoft 365 locations such as SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange.
Managing documents through defined stages of creation, review, archiving and deletion, with owners, review dates and expiration rules so outdated content does not linger.

Web security standard that controls which script sources a browser may execute. In SharePoint Online, CSP enforcement blocks inline scripts and external scripts that are not registered as trusted sources.
Context& is a consulting company that implements project and portfolio management solutions on Microsoft technology and offers Projectum xPM. Guest Erik van Hurck works there as a consultant.
Context engineering is the practice of deliberately designing and managing the information, instructions and memory an AI model receives, going beyond writing individual prompts.

desc.pt: Recurso do Microsoft 365 Copilot que usa o Microsoft Graph para trazer o contexto de trabalho certo (arquivos, e-mails, reuniões, pessoas) para os prompts.

desc.en: The amount of text (tokens) a large language model can take into account at once, including instructions, data and conversation; as it fills up, reasoning quality tends to degrade.

Continuous access evaluation is a Microsoft Entra capability that lets services revoke or re-evaluate access tokens in near real time when critical events such as a rising user risk occur, instead of waiting for the token to expire.
Continuous delivery keeps software always in a releasable state so it can go live on demand; continuous deployment goes further and releases every change that passes the pipeline automatically.
An ongoing effort to improve products, services or processes incrementally over time; applied here to cloud operations where monitoring signals trigger funded, owned actions.
Continuous integration is the practice of merging everyone's work into a shared main copy at least daily, with an automated build and tests checking every change.
A management layer where administrators see and steer systems centrally without doing the work itself; Microsoft describes Agent 365 as a control plane for AI agents.

In governance architecture, a control surface is the specific point in a workflow, such as creating a team, sharing a file or granting an agent permissions, where controls shape behavior at the moment of action.
Conversation intelligence in Dynamics 365 Sales analyses recorded sales calls to surface topics, tracked keywords, questions, competitor mentions and sentiment for review and coaching.

A built-in Copilot Studio system topic that runs when no authored topic matches a user question and uses generative answers to respond; without grounded knowledge sources it can fall back to generic model knowledge.
The observation that the structure of a system mirrors the communication structure of the organization that builds it.
Agent Builder is the no-code experience in Microsoft 365 Copilot for creating declarative agents from instructions, knowledge and a limited set of tools.

desc.ar: أداة من Microsoft ضمن Viva Insights لقياس استخدام Microsoft 365 Copilot وتبنيه وأثره على الأعمال والعائد على الاستثمار.

desc.en: App Builder is an agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot that generates small personal or team apps from natural-language prompts, storing data in Microsoft Lists (SharePoint lists) rather than Dataverse.

desc.te: Microsoft 365 అడ్మిన్ సెంటర్‌లో Copilot మరియు ఏజెంట్లను నిర్వహించడానికి, భద్రపరచడానికి, వాటి వినియోగాన్ని కొలవడానికి Microsoft అందించే నియంత్రణలు మరియు సాధనాల సమాహారం.

desc.en: Microsoft one-year, pay-up-front purchase option for Copilot Credits with tiered volume discounts; unused credits expire at the end of the term.
The options for extending Microsoft 365 Copilot beyond its built-in experience, for example with agents, connectors, APIs and custom orchestration, to connect it to business data and processes.

Flex routing is a Microsoft 365 Copilot setting that allows LLM inferencing for EU and EFTA tenants to run outside the EU Data Boundary during peak demand; admins can disable it in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

The step in which Microsoft 365 Copilot gathers relevant work context such as files, emails and meetings via Microsoft Graph before answering, turning a generic answer into one about the user's actual work.

The generative AI assistant built into Microsoft Fabric that helps with data work such as writing queries, fixing notebook code and drafting Power BI report pages. It runs on paid Fabric capacities and consumes capacity compute.
AI assistant built into Power Apps that generates app structures from natural-language descriptions and lets users ask questions about, summarise and visualise data inside running apps.

The generative AI assistant built into Power BI Desktop and the Power BI service that drafts DAX measures, creates report pages, answers data questions and writes narrative summaries based on the semantic model.

desc.nl: Personalisatiefunctie van Microsoft Copilot die alleen feiten en voorkeuren onthoudt die de gebruiker expliciet opgeeft; zichtbaar via de melding 'geheugen bijgewerkt', door de gebruiker te bekijken, te bewerken of uit te schakelen en voor beheerders controleerbaar via Microsoft Purview eDiscovery.

desc.en: Copilot Notebooks are Microsoft 365 Copilot workspaces based on Loop that collect pages, files and links on a topic so Copilot can reason over that content, for example to create summaries or audio overviews.

Copilot Pages is a Microsoft 365 Copilot capability that turns Copilot chat results into a shared, editable page built on the Loop framework, so colleagues can collaborate on the content with Copilot.
A category of Windows 11 PCs with a neural processing unit (NPU) capable of more than 40 TOPS, which is required for on-device AI features such as Recall and Click to Do.
A catalog of suggested and saved prompts inside Microsoft 365 Copilot; organizations can now add their own custom prompts, for example sorted by department.
A built-in agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot that performs multi-step research across work data and the web and returns source-backed answers.

desc.it: Esperienza di ricerca di Microsoft 365 Copilot che trova contenuti in tutte le app di Microsoft 365 e in fonti di dati di terze parti collegate; la ricerca trova, Copilot Chat spiega.

desc.en: Copilot Service workspace, formerly Dynamics 365 Customer Service workspace, is the multisession agent app for Dynamics 365 Customer Service that keeps each customer issue in its own session with tabs, an inbox, a productivity pane and Copilot assistance.
A toolkit for Copilot Studio for testing and evaluating agents and tracking conversation KPIs; in the episode it is used to measure agent business value and support governance.
Designed portions of a Copilot Studio agent conversation with steps, questions and conditions, used for answers that must be exact; requests outside the topics can fall back to generated answers.

desc.nl: Functie van Microsoft Copilot die op verzoek van de gebruiker in real time meekijkt naar het scherm of de camera; sessiegebaseerd en opt-in, beelden en audio worden na de sessie gewist, alleen het teksttranscript kan in de chatgeschiedenis blijven.

desc.en: The setting that lets Microsoft 365 Copilot reference public web content alongside internal data; admins can allow, block or selectively enable it and should test its effect in their tenant.

Corporate social responsibility (CSR) describes how a company accounts for the social and environmental impact of its business decisions, commonly framed as people, planet and profit and grouped into environmental, ethical, philanthropic and economic responsibility.
Cost to serve is a business metric for the total operational effort and expense required to run a process or deliver a service, including manual handling, rework and exception management.
Credential Guard uses virtualization-based security to isolate secrets such as NTLM hashes and Kerberos tickets from the LSASS process memory.

Accounts receivable capabilities in Dynamics 365 Finance for managing customer credit limits and credit holds and for carrying out collection activities on overdue balances, such as reminders, promises to pay and disputes.
A logical grouping of the same important field, such as a customer ID, across different tables so it can be governed with the same rules everywhere.
A scheduling method that identifies the chain of dependent tasks with no float that determines the earliest possible completion date; tasks on that chain delay the whole plan when they slip.

Aspects of a program, such as logging, authentication, validation and telemetry, that affect many modules and do not belong inside business logic. They are typically centralized with middleware, decorators or filters.
Cross filter direction is the Power BI relationship setting that determines whether filters travel only from the one side to the many side (single) or in both directions (bidirectional).
Microsoft Entra settings that control inbound and outbound collaboration with other Entra organizations, including trust for their MFA and device claims.

The capability to discover, replace and evolve cryptographic algorithms across systems without destabilizing critical services. The episode frames it as a permanent operational discipline rather than a one-time migration.
C# is a general-purpose, multi-paradigm programming language from Microsoft and the primary language of the .NET platform.
EU directive that makes sustainability reporting mandatory for in-scope companies under common reporting standards.

desc.pt: Plataforma e toolkit da NVIDIA para computação paralela em GPUs, base de runtimes de inferência.

desc.en: A custom connector wraps a REST or SOAP API, typically described with OpenAPI, so that Azure Logic Apps, Power Automate, Power Apps and Copilot Studio can call it like a built-in connector with typed actions and configured authentication.

A custom engine agent is a Microsoft 365 Copilot agent type in which the developer chooses the model and orchestrator, for example built with the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit, as opposed to declarative agents that run on Copilot's own orchestrator.
Custom pages are a page type in Power Apps model-driven apps that brings canvas-app design and Power Fx into a model-driven app, for full pages, dialogs or side panes.
A customer asset in Dynamics 365 Field Service is a record of a specific machine, unit or device installed at a customer site, holding its exact location and service history.

The Customer Intent Agent is an AI agent in Dynamics 365 Contact Center that uses generative AI to discover customer intents from past service interactions and support self-service and assisted service.

Customer-managed keys (CMK) are encryption keys that a customer creates and controls, typically in Azure Key Vault or Managed HSM, to protect the keys that encrypt their data in a cloud service, instead of relying on provider-managed keys.
A customer segment is a group of customers selected by rules based on profile details, activities and measures, which updates automatically as customer data changes.

Custom services in Dynamics 365 finance and operations apps expose business logic written in X++ to external systems as SOAP and JSON (REST) endpoints, complementing OData data entities for rule-driven or multi-table operations.
Dapr is an open-source runtime for microservices that runs as a sidecar and provides building blocks such as state management, pub/sub messaging and service discovery.
Dark data is information an organization collects and stores but does not use for insight or decision-making, often because it cannot be found, classified or governed.
Visual displays that bring key information and metrics together on one screen, often built in tools such as Excel or Power BI.
SharePoint admin reports (DAG) that show which sites are overshared, where permissions do not match policy and where sensitive content may be exposed.

The practice of identifying and categorizing data by sensitivity or business value, for example with sensitive information types and labels, so that protection policies such as DLP can target what matters.
A written, versioned agreement that defines what a data signal means, how its records are formed and what receiving systems should do when records do not meet the agreement.
The gradual degradation of data quality over time, showing up as duplicates, outdated records and conflicting versions of the truth across systems.
Data gravity describes how large accumulated data sets attract compute, tools, copies and teams, making the data increasingly hard to move.
A data historian is an industrial system that records process measurements over time and offers an interface to retrieve that history.
The trail of where data came from and how it moved and changed between systems.
The ability of people across an organization to ask precise questions of data and to read, interpret and question the answers they get.

The data import/export framework (DIXF) in Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations for bulk import and export of data through data entities; well suited for master data and batch loads, not for real-time integration.
A data architecture approach in which ownership of data is distributed to business domains while a platform team provides shared infrastructure and governance.
Data partitioning splits a table or data set into separate segments, for example by date or region, so queries only scan the relevant slices, improving performance and manageability.
The layer of a system that executes operational requests at scale, such as user interactions, flow runs and data transactions, as opposed to the control plane that defines policy and configuration.

A data processing agreement (DPA) is the contract between a data controller and a data processor that governs how personal data is processed on the controller's behalf, including sub-processors, security measures and breach notification, as required by GDPR Article 28.
A bundle of related data assets, such as tables, files and Power BI reports, packaged for a defined use case with owners and a business description, so others can discover and request access to it.

name: Microsoft Products and Services Data Protection Addendum (DPA)

desc.pl: Umowa Microsoft (Data Protection Addendum, DPA) określająca zobowiązania dotyczące przetwarzania danych, prywatności i RODO, w tym dla Microsoft 365 Copilot; Microsoft działa w niej jako podmiot przetwarzający dane.

desc.en: The default assessment in Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager, available at every subscription level, built from controls of common standards and regulations such as NIST, ISO, FedRAMP and GDPR.

Assessment required under the GDPR when processing is likely to create a high risk to people's rights, documenting the processing, its necessity and proportionality, the risks and the mitigating measures.
The documented history of a data asset's origin, custody and transformations, used to validate and audit where data came from and how it changed.
The degree to which data is complete, consistent, accurate, fresh and unique; in Microsoft Purview it is measured with rules and scores that roll up from columns to assets, data products and domains.
Data residency refers to requirements about the geographic location where data is stored and processed, often driven by regulations such as GDPR.
Data silos are isolated collections of data maintained separately by different teams or systems, leading to duplication, diverging versions and coordination failures.

Data sovereignty is the principle that data is subject to the laws and control of a particular jurisdiction or owner, which shapes where data may be stored and processed and who can compel access to it.

A data steward is a role responsible for maintaining accurate metadata, mapping business glossary terms, monitoring data quality and supporting access governance and compliance for a set of data assets.
A data transfer object is an object that carries data between processes or layers and has almost no behavior beyond storing and retrieving its own data.
The practice of structuring a relational data model to remove redundancy and improve data integrity, for example keeping one customer record instead of several copies.
A Microsoft Fabric item that uses Power Query to connect to, clean and shape data through a visual, low-code editor.
Alternate keys in Dataverse define uniqueness on business columns in addition to the GUID primary key, so imports and integrations can find, upsert and link rows without knowing their GUID.

Dataverse business skills is a preview Dataverse feature that lets business users write procedures as natural-language instructions in Dataverse, which agents can discover through the Dataverse MCP server without the agent being rebuilt or redeployed.
Security boundaries in a Dataverse environment arranged as a tree under a root unit; together with security roles they define which rows a user can reach.

A Dataverse custom API is a developer-defined message that exposes a named operation in Dataverse; it can be backed by a plug-in or used without one to define business events that subscribers such as Power Automate react to.

Elastic tables are a Dataverse table type backed by Azure Cosmos DB that scale horizontally for high-volume, append-heavy workloads such as logs, telemetry and audit events. Each record carries a partition ID and can expire automatically through a time-to-live value.
Dataverse security model that extends a manager's access to rows owned by their reports, based on either the manager hierarchy or a position hierarchy with a configurable depth.

desc.de: Indizierung in Microsoft Dataverse: automatische und benutzerdefinierte Indizes bestimmen, wie schnell Abfragen, Ansichten und Filter Datensätze finden, verursachen aber zusätzlichen Schreibaufwand.

desc.en: Custom server-side code registered in the Dataverse event pipeline that runs when data operations occur, used in Dynamics 365 for transactional validation and calculations.
A Dataverse column type whose value is generated by an AI prompt that references other columns of the same record, with the result stored on the record for use in apps, flows and reports.
Granting a specific user or team rights on an individual Dataverse row outside the role and business unit structure; each share is stored as an entry in the principal object access (POA) table.
Sets of privileges in Dataverse, such as create, read, write, delete, append, append to, assign and share, each defined per table with an access level or depth; roles are additive.

Dataverse table relationships connect tables through lookup columns as one-to-many or many-to-many relationships, with configurable relationship behavior (such as parental, referential or restrict) that decides what happens to related rows when a parent row is deleted or reassigned.
Teams in Dataverse that hold security roles or own rows: owner teams, access teams for record-level collaboration, and Microsoft Entra group teams whose membership follows a directory group.
Tables in Microsoft Dataverse whose definition lives in Dataverse while the records stay in an external system and are fetched at runtime through a data provider; formerly called virtual entities.
A date table is a dedicated calendar dimension in a Power BI semantic model with one row per date over a continuous range, used for filtering, grouping and time intelligence calculations.

ADDCOLUMNS is a DAX table function that adds calculated columns to a table or table expression, evaluating each expression for every row. The episode uses it to materialize a metric once per entity inside a UDF.
CALCULATE is a DAX function that evaluates an expression in a modified filter context, letting authors add, override or remove filters; it underpins time intelligence and comparisons.
Context transition is the DAX behavior that turns the current row context into an equivalent filter context, performed by CALCULATE and implicitly when a measure is evaluated in a row context.
DAX time intelligence functions such as TOTALYTD, SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR and DATEADD compare and aggregate data over time periods and require a table marked as a date table.
DAX user-defined functions let modelers package DAX logic once and reuse it like a built-in function in measures, calculated columns and other functions.
DCSync abuses the directory replication rights (DS-Replication-Get-Changes and Get-Changes-All) to request password hashes from a domain controller as if it were another domain controller.
A distributed denial-of-service attack floods a website, API or service with traffic from many devices at once so that legitimate users can no longer reach it.
Dead-lettering is a messaging safety net that parks events or messages that cannot be delivered in a separate store, so they can be inspected and replayed later instead of being dropped.

Decision debt is the accumulated inconsistency that arises when multiple agents or systems solve the same problem differently, with different assumptions and toolchains, producing contradictory outcomes and rework.
The decline in decision quality after making many consecutive decisions; the episode argues that letting Copilot pre-sort tasks reduces it.

Decision latency is the cumulative delay between an event happening, the organization understanding what it means and actually acting on it, often hidden in waiting, clarification and re-approval steps.

Decision rights define who in an organization is allowed to make, approve and override which decisions; in cloud governance they are often captured in a decision rights matrix covering standards, security, funding, exceptions and lifecycle ownership.
A leadership metric for the total time it takes to go from a business question to a trusted, logged and actionable decision, proposed as an alternative to measuring time saved by AI.

A declarative agent customizes Microsoft 365 Copilot with instructions, knowledge sources and actions while running on Copilot's own orchestrator and models and inheriting its security and compliance.
A software design pattern that wraps an existing object or service to add behavior, such as logging or validation, without changing its core implementation.

A credential type in the Azure Identity client libraries that tries several authentication methods in turn, using a managed identity when running in Azure and developer credentials when running locally.
The shared Power Platform environment that every user in a tenant can access by default; without governance it tends to fill up with mixed, unmanaged apps and flows.

Microsoft's email and collaboration security service that adds Safe Links, Safe Attachments and impersonation protection (Plan 1) plus investigation, response and attack simulation tools (Plan 2) on top of Exchange Online Protection.
Defense in depth is an information security approach that layers multiple independent security controls so that a single failed control does not leave systems or data exposed.
Compaction merges many small files of a Delta Lake table into fewer, larger files to reduce metadata overhead and read latency.

An open-source storage layer that extends Parquet files with a transaction log to provide ACID transactions, schema enforcement and table versioning; it is the default table format in Azure Databricks.
A Delta table is a table stored in the open Delta Lake format, Parquet files plus a transaction log, which is the default table format for lakehouses in Microsoft Fabric.
