Dependency analysis observes which servers communicate with each other and groups them into applications, so connected workloads can be migrated together instead of being split by accident.
A software engineering technique that supplies an object's dependencies from outside, typically through interfaces, producing loosely coupled and replaceable components.
Live copies of an Azure App Service app with their own address, used to deploy and test a new version and then swap it into production; available from the Standard tier.
An unplanned trail worn by people taking a shorter or easier route than the official one; used as a metaphor for repeated workarounds that reveal where a designed workflow does not fit real work.
A Power Automate for desktop automation that runs on a Windows machine and drives the user interface through mouse and keyboard actions, used to automate apps that have no API or connector.
Container-based development environments defined in a devcontainer.json file, so that every developer, VS Code instance and CI pipeline runs the same runtimes, tools and extensions.
The quality of the tooling, workflows and conventions developers work with in a code base or organization, with a focus on removing friction.

name: Device code flow (OAuth 2.0 device authorization grant)

desc.en: The OAuth 2.0 device authorization grant lets users sign in on input-constrained devices by entering a short code on another device. Attackers abuse it in device code phishing to obtain tokens without a password.

Device compliance means devices must meet rules set in Microsoft Intune compliance policies, such as secure boot or antivirus; the resulting compliance status is passed to Microsoft Entra ID and used by Conditional Access to grant or block access.
A persisted cloud document attached to an IoT Hub device identity that holds metadata, desired properties written by the cloud and reported properties written by the device.

desc.ar: منهجية وثقافة عمل تجمع بين التطوير والعمليات لتسليم البرمجيات وتشغيلها بشكل مستمر وموثوق عبر الأتمتة والمراقبة والتحسين المستمر.

desc.en: A mathematical framework that bounds how much any single record can influence a model's output, using techniques such as gradient clipping and calibrated noise, quantified by epsilon and delta parameters.
The accumulation of unverified and unmanaged digital artifacts, such as AI-generated drafts, summaries and automations, that grows faster than people can validate it and slows down decisions.
An extension of digital literacy that treats technology use as a life skill: using tools correctly, efficiently, effectively and responsibly, including AI.
The ability to find, evaluate, use, create and communicate information with digital tools in a purposeful and responsible way.

A digital signal processor (DSP) processes audio signals, for example mixing, echo and reverb reduction and noise removal; in conference rooms it can run as onboard software in microphones and room systems instead of a separate device.

The connected context that links product information across the lifecycle, from engineering through planning, production, quality, maintenance and service, while each system keeps ownership of its own records.
A preview item in Microsoft Fabric Real-Time Intelligence for modeling real-world assets and their relationships as an ontology on a low-code semantic canvas, with twin data stored in OneLake.
A maintained digital representation of a physical resource, its relationships and its operating conditions, kept up to date from observations.
A JSON-LD based language for describing digital twin models with properties, telemetry, components, commands and relationships, used by Azure Digital Twins and IoT Plug and Play.
Direct Lake is a storage mode for Power BI semantic models in Microsoft Fabric that reads Delta tables directly from OneLake instead of importing a copy or querying the source on every click.

A Teams Phone connectivity option in which the organization connects its own certified session border controller and chosen carrier trunks to Microsoft's SIP proxies, owning routing, certificates and operations.
DirectQuery is a Power BI storage mode in which no data is copied into the model; every report interaction queries the source database directly, so data is always live.
Policies, tools and procedures for restoring IT systems and data after a major outage or disaster, typically derived from a business continuity plan.

DiskANN is a graph-based approximate nearest neighbor search algorithm from Microsoft Research that keeps a compressed navigation layer in RAM and the full-precision graph on SSD. It is used in services such as Azure Cosmos DB and SQL Server vector search.
The immediate shop-floor instruction that tells a person or machine which operation to run next given the current situation, as opposed to a broader plan or detailed schedule.
Microsoft Purview process in which designated reviewers decide whether content that has reached the end of its retention period can be permanently deleted.

Distributed order management in Dynamics 365 Commerce uses business rules to choose a suitable store or warehouse to fulfill an order, based on available stock, delivery promise and fulfillment locations.

Transactions that must commit or roll back atomically across multiple services or databases, classically coordinated with a two-phase commit; in .NET 7 and later this support is Windows-only and must be explicitly enabled.
A static mail-enabled group in Exchange Online whose membership only changes when an administrator or owner adjusts it.
An email authentication method in which the sending server signs messages with a private key whose public key is published in DNS, proving integrity and origin.
Mode in Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention in which a policy runs as if it were enforced but without blocking anything, so admins can review matches and tune rules before enforcement.
An email authentication standard published in DNS that checks whether SPF or DKIM results align with the visible From domain and tells receivers to do nothing, quarantine or reject failing mail.
Docker's default public registry for finding, storing and sharing container images.
A set of tools that package and run applications in portable containers; Docker Desktop on Windows runs on top of WSL 2.
A plain-text file that lists the instructions for building a Docker image, one instruction per line, with each step producing a layer.
A server that runs Active Directory Domain Services for a Windows domain, authenticates users and computers and holds the group policy that domain members download.

The Domain Name System is the internet's public directory for domain names; email authentication records such as SPF, DKIM and DMARC are published there as DNS records that any receiving server can read.

The software delivery metrics from the DevOps Research and Assessment (DORA) program: deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change failure rate and time to restore service, which measure delivery throughput and stability.

Microsoft's opinionated, cloud-ready stack for building observable, distributed applications; it orchestrates services and dependencies for local development and ships a dashboard for logs, health and traces.
.NET Multi-platform App UI (.NET MAUI) is a cross-platform framework for building native mobile and desktop apps with C# and XAML from a single code base.

name: Data Security Posture Management for AI (DSPM for AI)

desc.es: Función de Microsoft Purview que detecta contenido compartido en exceso y datos sensibles que Copilot y otras IA podrían exponer, y propone políticas de corrección.

desc.en: A design for resisting prompt injection that separates a privileged LLM with tool access from a quarantined LLM that processes untrusted content, with regular software mediating between them.
In dual-write, a table map defines which finance and operations table connects to which Dataverse table and which fields belong together, and whether changes flow one way or both ways.
An extension of Azure Functions for building stateful, long-running workflows in a serverless environment using orchestrator, activity and client functions.
A Dutch community founded by Femke Cornelissen that connects women working in technology and promotes diversity and inclusion in Dutch workplaces.
In cybersecurity, dwell time is how long an attacker stays inside an environment before being detected; the episode presents it as a more meaningful SOC metric than MTTR.
An Exchange Online mail-enabled group whose membership is calculated from recipient attributes and rules, such as department or office, instead of a fixed member list.
The Accounts receivable module of Dynamics 365 Finance, used to track customer invoices, incoming payments, settlement and the money customers owe the business.
Maintenance management capability within Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management that tracks physical equipment, functional locations, maintenance plans, work orders, costs and service history.
The Dynamics 365 Customer Service capability that keeps each customer issue in one case record with customer details, activities, routing, service level targets and a recorded resolution.

Dynamics 365 Commerce is Microsoft's omnichannel commerce application that connects back office, in-store, call center and digital selling around shared product, pricing, inventory, order and customer data; it builds on Dynamics 365 Retail.

Microsoft's cloud contact center service for handling customer conversations across voice calls and digital channels from one agent workspace, with AI agents, routing and Copilot assistance. It can work alongside Dynamics 365 Customer Service or other CRM systems.

Copilot in Dynamics 365 is the set of generative AI capabilities built into Dynamics 365 apps such as Sales, Customer Service, Finance and Operations and Business Central. It summarizes records, answers questions about business data the user can access and prepares drafts for human review.

Customer Insights - Data is the customer data platform part of Dynamics 365 Customer Insights that brings customer information from separate systems together into unified profiles, segments and predictive insights.
Customer Insights - Journeys is the part of Dynamics 365 Customer Insights that uses customer profiles and audiences to send emails, text messages and other planned communications.

Microsoft's Model Context Protocol server for Dynamics 365 finance and operations apps that lets MCP-compatible agents, for example from Copilot Studio or VS Code, use ERP data and business logic under the connected user's security permissions; an initial static version with a fixed tool set was followed by a dynamic server that exposes forms and actions.
Microsoft Dynamics 365 application for planning and completing on-site service work, such as sending technicians to install, repair or maintain equipment at customer sites.

The add-in in Dynamics 365 Finance for creating, maintaining and viewing financial statements such as income statements and balance sheets from general ledger balances, using row, column and report definitions and reporting trees.

Dynamics 365 Fraud Protection is a Microsoft service for assessing transactions and account activity for fraud that can integrate with Dynamics 365 Commerce; Microsoft no longer sells it and its support ended in February 2026.

Dynamics 365 Guides is a Microsoft mixed reality application that shows step-by-step holographic instructions on HoloLens where the work happens; Microsoft set December 31, 2026 as its end-of-availability date.
Microsoft's cloud-based HR application in the Dynamics 365 family that centralizes employee records, organization structure, leave and absence, benefits, compensation and HR workflows.
A Dataverse-based Dynamics 365 application that orchestrates orders from capture through fulfillment and billing across Microsoft and third-party systems using orchestration flows and providers.
The inventory management capabilities of Dynamics 365 that keep one shared record of stock quantity, location, status, ownership and cost as items are received, moved, reserved, shipped and counted.
Knowledge management in Dynamics 365 Customer Service gives support teams one place to create, review, approve, publish, search and improve help articles for agents and self-service customers.
Omnichannel capabilities for Dynamics 365 Customer Service bring chat, voice, SMS and social messaging conversations into one agent workspace with routing, customer history and supervisor dashboards.

The procurement and sourcing capabilities of Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management, covering requisitions, RFQs, vendors, purchase orders, receipts, invoice matching and vendor payment in one source-to-pay process.
Microsoft Dynamics 365 application for project-based service businesses that connects project sales, resourcing, project management, time and expense tracking, billing and project financials.
In Dynamics 365 Customer Service, a shared work list for a team where cases wait for an owner; routing rules can send cases to the right queue.
Dynamics 365 Remote Assist is a Microsoft mixed reality application for remote expert support; like Dynamics 365 Guides, it is no longer available after December 31, 2026.
Guided selling workspace in Dynamics 365 Sales that gives sellers a prioritized work list of leads and opportunities, repeatable follow-up sequences and customer context.
Dynamics 365 Sales Insights is a set of AI-powered capabilities in Dynamics 365 Sales that turns sales activity into guidance through prompts, predictive scores and relationship signals.
Microsoft's Dynamics 365 ERP application for supply chain, warehouse, inventory and manufacturing processes.
The transportation planning capability inside Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management that connects orders, warehouse work, carriers, routes, rates, loads and freight costs.

The warehouse management capabilities of Dynamics 365 that guide physical warehouse work such as receiving, put-away, picking and loading, for example with mobile scanning, barcodes and license plates.
Easy Auth is the built-in authentication and authorization feature of Azure App Service and Azure Functions that signs in users and handles tokens with little or no application code.

A zero-click prompt injection vulnerability in Microsoft 365 Copilot (CVE-2025-32711) in which a crafted email could cause Copilot to exfiltrate data; the episode describes it as an LLM scope violation.
Edge computing places compute and storage near the data source, for example inside the plant, to handle protocols, buffering, filtering and local inference before data moves to the cloud.
A device or service close to industrial equipment that reads machine protocols and signals, buffers and filters data and forwards it to upstream systems without taking over machine control.

Working collections in Microsoft Purview eDiscovery where authorised reviewers examine, tag and filter collected content before exporting it; review sets and advanced review tools depend on licensing.

A prioritization framework that sorts tasks by urgency and importance into four quadrants: do now, schedule, delegate or ignore. The episode shows how Microsoft 365 Copilot can apply it automatically.
The electronic exchange of invoices; in many countries outside the US, invoices must be registered with the tax authority before they are sent, which ERP localizations have to support.
A data integration pattern that loads raw source data into the destination platform first and transforms it there, keeping the original data available.
Forging the sender address of an email so that it appears to come from a trusted person or domain; email authentication standards such as SPF, DKIM and DMARC help detect it.
A Dynamics 365 Customer Service capability that automatically creates or updates case records from incoming emails using automatic record creation and update rules.

Embedded analytics places reports and dashboards directly inside the business applications where people work, such as Power BI reports embedded in Dynamics 365 forms, instead of in a separate analytics tool.

Numeric vectors produced by machine learning models that represent the meaning of text, images or other content, so that similar content lies close together and can be compared by distance in vector search.

Highly privileged emergency admin accounts kept outside Conditional Access policies and protected with long passwords and phishing-resistant MFA, so administrators can regain access to a tenant if they are locked out.

A conversion rate that links an activity, such as a kilowatt hour of electricity or a mile driven, to the amount of greenhouse gas it produces; activity data multiplied by the factor gives the emissions.
The ability to perceive, understand and manage one's own and others' emotions; a broad set of skills such as empathy and active listening.

An HR approach in which employees and managers handle routine tasks themselves, such as updating personal details, checking leave balances and submitting or approving requests, instead of going through HR by email.
EN 16931 is the European standard defining the semantic data model of the core elements of an electronic invoice, with syntax bindings such as UBL and CII.
Microsoft field-led funding program that pays qualified partners to deploy, migrate and drive adoption of Microsoft cloud solutions at customer sites.
A software testing practice, often called front-end or UI testing, that simulates a real user in a browser to confirm complete workflows such as logging in or checking out actually succeed.
A security approach that continuously monitors endpoints, detects behavior that looks like an attack and responds to it, rather than only blocking known malicious files.
The Microsoft Purview capability that applies DLP policies on onboarded Windows and macOS devices, covering activities such as copying to USB, uploading to cloud services, printing and clipboard use.
Power Apps canvas component feature that adds function, event and action properties to components, letting the host app inject logic into a component through its declared properties.
The Intune setup screen shown during Windows Autopilot provisioning that blocks access to the desktop until required policies, certificates and apps in the device and user phases are installed.

The Microsoft Enterprise Agreement is a volume licensing program for large organizations, generally with at least 500 users or devices, that license Microsoft software and cloud services for a multi-year term.
Enterprise content management (ECM) is the discipline and set of systems for capturing, organizing, governing and retaining an organization's documents and records across their lifecycle.

Enterprise data protection is the set of Microsoft controls and commitments that applies to prompts and responses in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat for users signed in with a work account; this data is not used to train foundation models.

A framing used in the episode for Microsoft 365 as the shared operating environment in which identity, data, collaboration, compliance and automation layers interact and the business actually runs, rather than a bundle of separate tools.
Business software that connects purchasing, inventory, orders and related transactions across an organization.
Microsoft Entra ID Governance feature for requesting and granting access through catalogs and access packages with approval policies, expiry and extensions, including for external users.
Entity Framework Core (EF Core) is Microsoft's object-relational mapper for .NET that translates LINQ queries into SQL through a layered query pipeline and materializes the results as objects.

Entity resolution (also called record linkage) is the process of determining when records from different systems refer to the same real-world entity and merging them into one canonical representation, for example in a knowledge graph.
Entra Connect Health is the monitoring layer for Entra Connect that watches the sync connection and alerts IT about stopped sync services, failed syncs, server issues or sign-in problems.
Microsoft's customer identity and access management (CIAM) platform in the Microsoft Entra family for external users such as customers, partners and guests; it is the successor to Azure AD B2C.

Identity governance offering in Microsoft Entra that combines entitlement management, access reviews, lifecycle workflows and privileged identity management; sold as an add-on on top of Entra ID P1 or P2.

Microsoft Entra Internet Access is the identity-centric secure web gateway (SWG) part of Global Secure Access, applying organizational security policies to traffic for websites, SaaS apps and other internet destinations.

Microsoft Entra Private Access is the Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) part of Global Secure Access, giving users identity-based access to specific private apps and resources without broad VPN network access.

Microsoft Entra Workload ID covers the identities used by software such as applications, services, scripts and containers, including app registrations, service principals and managed identities, and the tools to secure them.
A way to organize managed Power Platform environments into groups and apply the same rules to all member environments at once. An environment can belong to only one group.
A Power Platform tenant setting that automatically routes makers away from the default environment into their own personal developer environments, which are created on the fly if needed.

desc.ar: قيم قابلة للتهيئة داخل حلول Power Platform مثل نقاط النهاية والمفاتيح وسلاسل الاتصال، يمكن تبديلها لكل بيئة عند النشر دون تعديل التطبيق أو التدفق.

desc.en: The capacity of people to direct their own inquiry and own how they come to know something; in AI-mediated work, the risk is that teams consume AI outputs instead of building their own understanding.

Equinix is a US-based data center and interconnection company whose carrier-neutral colocation facilities host meet-me points where cloud private circuits such as ExpressRoute and Direct Connect terminate.

Framework of environmental, social and governance factors that organizations measure and disclose; in this episode treated as a system of record whose numbers must be auditable like financial reporting.

A data integration pattern that extracts data from sources, transforms (cleans and shapes) it and loads it into a target such as a data warehouse. The variant ELT loads the data before transforming it.

desc.es: Compromiso de Microsoft de almacenar y procesar los datos de clientes de la UE dentro de la Unión Europea; también se aplica al procesamiento de Microsoft 365 Copilot.

desc.en: Event-based retention in Microsoft Purview starts a retention label's retention period when a defined event occurs, such as a contract expiring, a project completing or a case being resolved, instead of when content is created or labeled.

Event-driven architecture is a design approach in which systems react to notifications that something has happened instead of repeatedly polling for changes, decoupling the components that announce changes from those that react to them.

desc.de: Consumergruppen sind unabhängige Sichten auf denselben Event-Hubs-Datenstrom, sodass mehrere nachgelagerte Anwendungen dieselben Ereignisse im eigenen Tempo lesen können.
Partitionen sind die geordneten Datenspuren eines Azure Event Hubs: Innerhalb einer Partition bleibt die Reihenfolge der Ereignisse erhalten, mehr Partitionen ermöglichen mehr parallele Verarbeitung.

desc.en: An item in Microsoft Fabric Real-Time Intelligence that serves as the container for real-time event data work; it holds one or more KQL databases, which hold the tables where events land.
A Microsoft Fabric Real-Time Intelligence item that connects to event sources, applies transformations such as filters or aggregations, and routes the data to destinations such as an eventhouse.
Built-in SharePoint and Microsoft 365 claim that includes every internal user of a tenant; granting it access to sites or libraries makes content broadly visible inside the organization.
A Microsoft Purview detection method that compares content against a hashed table of real sensitive values, such as customer account numbers, to reduce false positives compared with pattern matching.
PowerShell module (ExchangeOnlineManagement, also called EXO) for managing Exchange Online mailboxes, mail rules and distribution groups.
The baseline filtering service included with every Exchange Online mailbox, covering spam, malware, connection filtering and core anti-phishing with spoof protection.
Microsoft's on-premises email and messaging server, which can be connected to Exchange Online in a hybrid configuration; the episode notes that Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 are out of support.
Exchange Web Services (EWS) is the older API developers used to work with Exchange mailboxes and calendars; in Exchange Online it is being retired in favor of Microsoft Graph.

An execution contract is a concrete definition of what an autonomous agent may do and under which constraints, covering allowed tools, scopes and boundaries, evidence requirements, thresholds, and escalation and kill behavior.
The plan a SQL query optimizer chooses to execute a query, including access methods, join algorithms and sorts; estimated plans show the optimizer's intent and actual plans add runtime details.

As used in the episode, the ability of an organization to trace and prove with evidence how an automated outcome was produced: what triggered it, which rules and data applied and who changed the logic.

The time a risky condition, such as an oversharing event or an unprotected sensitive file, stays unresolved before a control contains it; used as a metric for how close governance controls sit to the point of action.
Open-source back-end web application framework for Node.js, used to build web applications and APIs.
Expression trees represent code as a data structure that can be examined at run time; Entity Framework Core uses them to analyze LINQ queries before translating them to SQL.
Routing domains configured on an Azure ExpressRoute circuit: private peering connects to Azure virtual networks, while Microsoft peering connects to Microsoft public services such as Microsoft 365.

A Microsoft program that delivers security patches for out-of-support products such as Windows Server 2012 and SQL Server 2012. With Azure Arc they can be received on-premises without migrating to Azure.
A separate Microsoft Entra tenant, isolated from the workforce tenant, that holds customer identities for consumer-facing apps in Microsoft Entra External ID.
A shared pool of Microsoft Fabric compute measured in capacity units (CUs) that workspaces and items draw from; consumption is smoothed over time and sustained overuse can lead to throttling.
A Data Factory item in Microsoft Fabric that copies data from a source to a destination without building a pipeline, with built-in batch and incremental (change tracking) patterns.

The data integration experience built into Microsoft Fabric for moving and transforming data with pipelines, Dataflow Gen2, copy jobs and mirroring; Microsoft positions it as the successor to Azure Data Factory.

The orchestration feature of Microsoft Fabric that chains activities such as copy data, dataflows and notebooks into a scheduled or triggered workflow with success, failure, retry and timeout handling.

name: Deployment pipelines (Microsoft Fabric and Power BI)

desc.en: A Fabric and Power BI feature that promotes workspace content through stages such as development, test and production, with full or selective deployment and REST APIs for automation.
Domains in Microsoft Fabric group workspaces by business area (for example sales or finance) to define ownership and governance boundaries in a data mesh style setup.
The Microsoft Fabric container for real-time event analysis, holding KQL databases that store time-stamped events for fast queries over recent machine states, alarms and condition data.

Fabric IQ is a Microsoft Fabric workload, in preview, that brings unified data and semantics together, including an ontology and Power BI semantic models, to give AI agents context about business entities and data.
A Microsoft Fabric item for storing and analyzing large amounts of structured and unstructured data, organized into a Tables folder and a Files folder.
A managed Microsoft Fabric capability that continuously replicates external databases, or their metadata, into OneLake as Delta tables in near real time without building pipelines.
A Microsoft Fabric capability for modeling business entities and their relationships on top of existing data and semantic models, which data agents can use to answer questions.
The Microsoft Fabric workload for streaming and event data, combining eventstreams, eventhouses with KQL databases, real-time dashboards and Activator alerts.

Tenant-level settings in the Microsoft Fabric admin portal that control which features, such as creating warehouses, lakehouses or notebooks, sharing and exporting, are available to which users in an organization.

Warehouse snapshots in Microsoft Fabric provide a read-only, transactionally consistent view of a warehouse as of a point in time and can be rolled forward on demand while consumers keep the same connection.
Microsoft Fabric relational data warehouse for preparing and querying well-defined tables with SQL.
Microsoft Entra Verified ID feature that compares a live selfie with the photo stored in a Verified ID credential for higher-assurance checks.
Facilitator is a Microsoft 365 Copilot agent in Teams meetings that takes notes and answers questions visibly for all meeting participants.

A controlled model of how work moves through part of a factory, using current operating rules, resources, orders and normal variation, so a proposed change such as an extra shift, new machine or smaller buffer can be tested before it is made.
Groups of hardware in an Azure datacenter that share power and network equipment; spreading hosts or VMs across fault domains reduces the risk of a single rack-level failure affecting all of them.
Feature engineering is the process of transforming raw data into input variables (features) for machine learning models, for example through cleaning, aggregation and encoding.

Copilot connector model in which Microsoft 365 Copilot queries an external system in real time, via the Model Context Protocol, instead of indexing its content into Microsoft 365; each user authenticates with the source system.
Training models collaboratively across multiple organizations, business units or locations without sharing raw data; only model updates, such as LoRA adapter matrices, move across the network.
The industry association that develops and promotes the FIDO authentication standards behind passkeys.
The open authentication standard, including WebAuthn and CTAP, that defines how passkeys and security keys work.
Figma Make is Figma's AI prompt-to-app feature that generates working prototypes and code from a description.
In DAX, filter context is the set of filters active at the moment a measure is evaluated, coming from slicers, visuals, the page and rows, which determines which data a measure sees.
The recurring period-end process in which a finance team reconciles accounts, posts adjustments, validates results and reports the financial statements for the month or year.
The accounting process of combining the financial results of multiple legal entities into one consolidated view, including the elimination of intercompany transactions.
Additional labels in Dynamics 365 Finance, such as department, cost center, location or project, attached to ledger entries to add detail beyond the main account.
The ease with which users can locate the content they need, influenced by structure, metadata, search behavior and navigation.
Fine-tuning further trains a pre-trained model on additional data; for keeping AI answers current with company data it is often compared with retrieval-augmented generation.

Finite capacity scheduling plans production operations onto real resource calendars, treating each machine, person or station as limited, so conflicts between orders become visible instead of being left to the shop floor.
A nonprofit project of the Linux Foundation that maintains the FinOps Framework, its principles and phases, and publishes the annual State of FinOps survey.
A serverless hosting plan for Azure Functions that Microsoft recommends for new serverless apps. It builds on pay-for-what-you-use billing and can scale out to as many as one thousand instances.
A flow metric that divides the time work is actively being handled by its total elapsed time, showing how much of a work item's life is spent waiting in queues.
Microsoft's UI framework and component library for building user interfaces that look and behave like Microsoft 365 and SharePoint.

An open-source GitOps operator and CNCF graduated project that runs as Kubernetes controllers and continuously reconciles a cluster with the state defined in Git; it is the built-in GitOps option on AKS and Azure Arc.
Focus time is protected calendar time for uninterrupted work; Microsoft Viva Insights lets users book focus blocks during which Teams notifications can be silenced.

A forecast category is a label on a Dynamics 365 Sales opportunity (pipeline, best case, committed, omitted, won or lost) that decides which forecast column includes its amount and signals confidence.

The forecast grid is the main forecasting view in Dynamics 365 Sales, showing rows for sellers, teams, products or territories with quota and forecast amounts that can be drilled into the underlying opportunities.
A psychological model, originating with Hermann Ebbinghaus, describing how newly learned information is lost over time without reinforcement or practice.
Forrester Research is a market research and advisory firm. Its Total Economic Impact (TEI) studies model the costs, benefits and ROI of technology investments such as Microsoft Power Platform.

Foundry IQ is a Microsoft Foundry capability that provides shared knowledge bases for grounding AI agents with permission-aware, cited retrieval. Agents, including Copilot Studio agents, can connect to it via an MCP connector.
The catalog in Microsoft Foundry for discovering, comparing, testing and deploying models from Microsoft and partners such as OpenAI, Meta, Mistral and Cohere.

An isolated workspace inside a Microsoft Foundry resource for one AI solution, holding its own model deployments, agents, knowledge stores, evaluations and monitoring while sharing the resource's security boundary.
A feature in Microsoft Foundry that gathers tools once, exposes them through a single connection and lets many agents reuse them with shared sign-in and controls.
Freelancing is self-employed work for multiple clients without a long-term commitment to a single employer, common in IT consulting and the Microsoft partner ecosystem.
The process of comparing a carrier's freight invoice with the expected transport charge, rate and shipment details recorded during planning before the invoice is paid.
Frequency capping limits how many times the same person receives a message or ad within a defined time window, to prevent fatigue and over-contacting.
A small metadata section at the top of a file, such as a skill file, that summarizes it (for example name, domain and purpose) so a system can judge relevance without loading the whole file.
The Frontier program is Microsoft's early access preview program through which organizations can enable new Microsoft 365 Copilot features before general availability.

Microsoft profile technology that stores Windows user profiles in containers (virtual disks) and attaches them at sign-in, giving users a consistent profile across session hosts in virtual desktop environments.
A domain name that specifies a host's exact location in the DNS hierarchy; firewall rules based on FQDNs allow traffic to named services instead of changing IP ranges.
A capability of language models to request a specific function by name with structured inputs, letting frameworks such as Semantic Kernel run application code and return the result to the model.

The organizational side of Microsoft 365 governance: how sites and teams are created, which templates are used, how data is archived or deleted across its lifecycle and how guest users are managed, as opposed to technical governance such as device and conditional access configuration.
In Dynamics 365 Asset Management, the place where an asset does its job, such as a site, building or production line, organised in a parent-child hierarchy that also carries cost details.

An approach in which fusion teams of business experts, low-code makers, IT professionals, architects and professional developers build solutions together on a shared platform such as Power Platform, each contributing at the appropriate abstraction level.
Fuzzy matching is a technique that identifies and links non-identical records by calculating a similarity score, for example with character-based edit distance or semantic similarity.

Gamification applies game design elements such as points, challenges, progress indicators, competition and social features to non-game contexts like business apps and adoption programs to increase engagement and motivation.

GCC High is Microsoft's isolated government community cloud environment for Microsoft 365, used by US defense contractors that handle controlled unclassified information; moving there from commercial Microsoft 365 requires a re-tenanting migration.
The main bookkeeping record of a company that collects all financial transactions by account; in Dynamics 365 Finance it is the official home for every posted money movement.
Artificial intelligence that generates text, images or other content in response to natural-language prompts.
The practice of improving content so that it is referenced and cited in answers generated by AI systems such as ChatGPT, Copilot or Perplexity.
Orchestration mode in Microsoft Copilot Studio in which a large language model chooses which tools, topics or knowledge to use for a request, guided by their names and descriptions.
Open-source AI tooling by Alan Buscaglia under Gentleman Programming, described in the episode as a collection of harnesses and ways of thinking and reasoning for coding agents.
Spanish-speaking developer community and content channel created by Alan Buscaglia, covering programming, software architecture and AI-assisted development across YouTube, Twitch, Discord and GitHub.
Ghost agents are AI agents that keep running, consuming tokens and holding access after their project has ended and their owner has moved on, creating cost and security risk.
A branch is a separate line of work in a version control system such as Git that starts from an existing version and is later merged back.
A commit is a deliberate, named checkpoint in a Git repository that records a selected set of changes together with a short message.
A distributed version control system that records changes to project files over time so teams can compare versions, revert changes and collaborate on the same code.

A Git branching model published by Vincent Driessen in 2010 that uses two permanent branches, master and develop, plus feature, release and hotfix branches. It suits software that ships in numbered versions.
GitHub's security offering for repositories, including code scanning, secret scanning and dependency checks that alert developers to leaked secrets and vulnerable packages.

A mode of GitHub Copilot in which you hand it a goal instead of a question; it decides which files to open, makes the edits and runs commands to check its own work until the task is finished. Changes still need to be reviewed by the developer.
GitHub Copilot CLI brings GitHub Copilot to the terminal as an agent that takes natural-language tasks, plans the steps and runs commands in the local environment.
GitHub Copilot coding agent works asynchronously on tasks such as assigned GitHub issues in a cloud environment and delivers its changes as a pull request for human review.

GitHub Copilot for Azure is a GitHub Copilot extension that lets developers use natural language to learn about Azure, deploy resources and diagnose problems, including generating infrastructure-as-code scaffolding.

The GitHub Copilot SDK lets developers embed the agent runtime behind GitHub Copilot CLI into their own applications, with custom tools and MCP server integration; the episode highlights its built-in session persistence.
A lightweight, branch-based workflow in which anything on the main branch is deployable and work happens in short-lived feature branches merged through pull requests.
An operating model in which environments, deployments and releases are managed declaratively through a Git repository.

The most privileged built-in administrator role in Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft 365, with access to all administrative features and data in a tenant. Microsoft recommends limiting its use and assigning it to as few people as possible.

Microsoft Entra Global Secure Access is Microsoft's cloud-delivered Security Service Edge (SSE) solution and the umbrella name for Microsoft Entra Private Access and Microsoft Entra Internet Access, securing access to private apps and internet resources based on identity and policy.
A shared business word with a definition that is attached to data; in Microsoft Purview Unified Catalog, terms live in governance domains and can carry policies.

A custom, preconfigured virtual machine image that bundles the operating system, updates, applications and customizations and is captured as the template for deploying virtual desktops or session hosts; it has to be maintained and updated over time.
An approved, repeatable route in an internal developer platform that turns code into a running service for a common job, with sensible defaults instead of setup from scratch.
A golden ticket attack forges Kerberos ticket-granting tickets with a stolen KRBTGT key, giving an attacker persistent, arbitrary identity in an Active Directory domain.
Cloud Interconnect is a Google Cloud service that provides high-availability, low-latency private connections between external networks, including other clouds, and Google's network.
Google's suite of public cloud computing services. In Microsoft contexts it often appears as part of multi-cloud environments managed alongside Azure.
Gemini, formerly Bard, is Google's generative AI assistant, which is also built into Google Workspace apps such as Google Sheets.
Google Sheets is the web-based spreadsheet application in Google's Docs Editors suite, known for real-time collaboration and compatible with Microsoft Excel file formats.

Governance debt describes the accumulating risk and cleanup effort that arise when AI agents and integrations are shipped without central identity, policy, logging and cost controls, trading short-term speed for long-term loss of control.
Boundary in Microsoft Purview Unified Catalog that groups data products and business concepts such as glossary terms and OKRs by business area for shared ownership, governance and discovery.
GRC is the combined discipline of governance, risk management and regulatory compliance; in Microsoft 365 it covers ownership, data protection, audit readiness and related controls.

desc.pl: Wcześniejszy model językowy OpenAI, na którym opierał się Microsoft 365 Copilot przed GPT-5.

desc.en: GPT-4o is a multimodal OpenAI model that can process and generate text, images and audio; its real-time API streams audio in and out for low-latency voice conversations.

desc.hi: समानांतर गणना के लिए बना प्रोसेसर, जिसका उपयोग AI मॉडल की ट्रेनिंग और इन्फ़रेंस को तेज़ करने के लिए एक्सेलरेटर के रूप में होता है।

desc.de: Browserbasiertes Werkzeug von Microsoft, mit dem man Anfragen an die Microsoft Graph API ausprobieren, Berechtigungen testen und Antworten wie Delta-Links prüfen kann.

desc.en: An open-source query language and runtime for APIs that lets a client request exactly the data it needs; Fabric apps expose their database through a GraphQL API.

GraphRAG is a retrieval-augmented generation technique from Microsoft Research that uses an LLM to extract a knowledge graph of entities and relationships from text and retrieves over that graph and its community summaries instead of flat text chunks.
A Microsoft Entra ID setting that gives Microsoft 365 groups a lifetime, emails owners renewal notices before it ends, auto-renews active groups and soft-deletes expired ones for 30 days.
Group managed service accounts are Active Directory service identities whose long, random passwords are rotated automatically by the domain, so no human knows the secret.
A tenant-wide Microsoft Entra ID policy that adds prefixes or suffixes, including user attributes, to Microsoft 365 group names and blocks listed words at creation.
Group Policy Preferences once stored passwords in SYSVOL XML files in a cpassword attribute encrypted with a publicly known AES key, so any domain user can recover them.
A Windows feature that lets administrators define settings once in group policy objects (GPOs) and have domain-joined Windows computers and users apply them automatically through Active Directory.
A Microsoft Entra synchronization feature that provisions cloud-authored groups back to on-premises Active Directory so legacy file servers and applications can still use them for access.
gRPC is an open-source remote procedure call framework originally developed by Google that uses Protocol Buffers to define services and messages across languages.
The ability to add people from outside the organization to Microsoft 365 groups and Teams as guest objects in Microsoft Entra ID, controlled at tenant, team and sensitivity-label level.
The Hadamard gate is a single-qubit quantum operation that puts a qubit from a basis state into an equal superposition of zero and one.
A device fingerprint built from details such as manufacturer, model and serial numbers that is uploaded to the Windows Autopilot service to register a device to an organization's tenant.
A security foundation built into a chip that verifies device identity and software integrity before any software loads, so that later security checks can be trusted.
An attack strategy in which adversaries collect encrypted traffic today and store it until a sufficiently capable quantum computer can decrypt it.
Packer is a HashiCorp tool that automates image creation; Azure Image Builder wraps it in an Azure-managed layer.
The software company that created Terraform, released in 2014. HashiCorp is now a subsidiary of IBM.
Headless commerce separates the selling engine and its business rules from the customer-facing screens, so websites, apps, kiosks or store devices all call the same engine through APIs.

A periodic TCP, HTTP or HTTPS check that a load balancer sends to each backend instance to decide whether it is healthy and should receive new traffic; Azure probes originate from the address 168.63.129.16.

Hierarchical partition keys (subpartitioning) in Azure Cosmos DB let a container use up to three levels of partition key, such as tenant ID, user ID and item ID, so that large tenants are spread across many logical partitions.
Higgsfield is a generative AI video platform that offers controllable cinematic camera presets, motion control and lip sync tools on top of multiple video models.
A system design goal of keeping services operational with minimal downtime, typically achieved through redundancy such as standby replicas.

A communication style in which much of the message is carried by context, timing and relationship rather than explicit words, as opposed to low-context communication where the meaning sits in the message itself.
High-performance computing runs massive parallel jobs such as simulations, rendering or financial modeling across many compute nodes that need shared, high-throughput, low-latency data access.
The US Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996, known in IT for its rules protecting the privacy and security of individually identifiable health information.

Hire-to-retire is the end-to-end HR lifecycle of a worker, from recruiting and hiring through transfers to termination or retirement; the episode argues it behaves less like one linear process and more like a stream of facts, obligations and identity changes across many systems.

HNSW is a graph-based approximate nearest neighbor algorithm that builds a multi-layer proximity graph for fast vector search. It keeps the whole graph in memory, which makes it fast but RAM-intensive at large scale.
Decoy user accounts with tempting names that have no legitimate use; in Microsoft Defender for Identity any authentication with such an account triggers an alert.
An agent type in Foundry Agent Service where you bring your own code and framework and Foundry runs it in an isolated session, scaling it and giving it its own identity.
HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) is the request-response protocol of the web; its methods such as GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE and its numeric status codes form the basis of REST APIs.

A federated governance operating model in which a central hub defines policies, baselines, standards and rollout criteria, while local spoke teams execute and remediate them within their own environments, for example individual Microsoft 365 tenants.
Network design in which a central hub virtual network hosts shared services such as a firewall or VPN gateway and is peered with many spoke virtual networks that hold individual workloads.
Hybrid cloud is an operating model that combines on-premises infrastructure with one or more public clouds under shared identity, policy and management.

Microsoft Entra hybrid join describes Windows devices that are joined to on-premises Active Directory and also registered in Microsoft Entra ID, giving them a cloud identity for access and management.
A retrieval architecture that routes simple queries to fast single-pass retrieval and complex or ambiguous queries to an agentic path with planning and iteration.

A Hybrid Runbook Worker is a Windows or Linux machine, for example an on-premises server connected via Azure Arc, that runs Azure Automation runbooks locally with access to its own network and resources.
Search approach that runs keyword (full-text) and vector queries together and merges the results into one ranked list, for example with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) in Azure AI Search.
Hybrid work is a working model in which employees split their time between working in the office and working remotely, which creates the need to coordinate who is in the office and when.
Hyper-V is Microsoft's hypervisor for running virtual machines on Windows hosts; Azure Migrate can discover, assess and replicate Hyper-V virtual machines.
Hyperconverged infrastructure is a software-defined design in which the same cluster of servers provides compute, storage and networking, instead of separate server and storage systems.

A property of an operation or deployment that produces the same result no matter how many times it is run; in infrastructure as code, re-running a deployment only changes what differs from the desired state.

Identity debt is the accumulation of non-human identities and entitlements, such as service principals, managed identities, app registrations, secrets and conditional access exceptions, that an organization depends on but can no longer explain.

Gradual loss of clear accountability when automations and AI agents run under maker credentials, shared service accounts or ambiguous connection contexts instead of dedicated, isolatable non-human identities.

Identity threat detection and response (ITDR) is a security discipline that detects compromised or misused identities from identity signals and contains them quickly, for example by revoking sessions or disabling accounts.

An illicit consent grant attack tricks a user into granting an attacker-controlled OAuth application permissions such as mail or file access, giving the app account-level access to data without stealing a password.
Immanuel Kant (1724-1804) was a German philosopher whose ideas on ethics, including the distinction between dignity and price, are frequently cited in discussions about AI and automation.
Immersive spaces are a 3D meeting view in Microsoft Teams, powered by Microsoft Mesh, in which participants join as avatars with spatial audio; a space holds up to 16 participants.
A backup stored in a write-once-read-many (WORM) state so that recovery points cannot be changed or deleted, even by administrators, until their retention period expires.
Write once, read many storage behavior, offered for Azure Blob Storage and ADLS Gen2 through time-based retention policies and legal holds, that prevents data from being modified or deleted.
Import is the Power BI storage mode that copies and compresses source data into the semantic model in memory, giving fast reports whose freshness depends on scheduled refresh.

Impossible travel is a risk detection that flags sign-ins by the same user from locations too far apart to be reached in the time between them, a common signal of compromised credentials or replayed tokens.
A psychological pattern in which people doubt their accomplishments and fear being exposed as a fraud, common among high achievers in tech.
Recommended tasks in Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager that can be assigned to owners, hold evidence and be tested manually or automatically, and that add points to the compliance score.

SharePoint Advanced Management site lifecycle policy that detects SharePoint sites without activity for a set period, notifies owners to confirm they are still needed and can make unclaimed sites read-only or archive them.
Incremental refresh is a data loading technique that processes only new or changed data since the last run instead of reloading the full data set, used in Power BI and Fabric Dataflow Gen2.
An independent software vendor is a software company that builds and sells an app for many customers of a platform, such as Business Central apps offered through Microsoft AppSource.
Pieces of evidence on a network, device or in email, such as malicious IP addresses, domains or file hashes, that suggest an intrusion has happened.

A shared set of rules that describes the objects that matter in a factory, such as products, orders, operations, resources and states, with stable identities and the relationships between them across systems like ERP, MES and maintenance.

A separate network zone between plant (OT) and enterprise (IT) networks that hosts selected services under controlled access rules, so exchanges pass through distinct, separately permitted connections.
The use of connected sensors, controllers and gateways in industrial settings to capture physical machine and process signals and pass them to digital systems.
A rough-cut planning approach that loads demand into time buckets without limiting it to the actual capacity of resources; useful for seeing load build up, but not an executable shop-floor schedule.
Microsoft InfoPath is a legacy Microsoft tool for designing electronic forms, often used with SharePoint; Power Apps is commonly seen as its successor.
Inforcer is a company focused on Microsoft 365 security configuration management for managed service providers and their clients. Guest Jonathan Hope works there as an M365 solutions architect.
The deliberate structuring of sites, content, metadata and navigation so that information can be found and managed; described in the episode as the biggest pain point in SharePoint implementations.

A situation in which one party holds information that the other cannot access. The episode uses it to describe AI agents whose decision paths are opaque to the managers accountable for their outcomes.
Microsoft Purview compliance solution that restricts two-way communication and collaboration between defined groups or segments of users in Microsoft Teams, SharePoint and OneDrive.
A threat intelligence technique that follows shared details such as registrars, certificates, name servers or IP addresses to expand one indicator into a map of related attacker infrastructure.
Insecure deserialization is a vulnerability in which an application deserializes untrusted data without validation, which can let attackers run arbitrary code or read private data.
Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management is a compliance solution that correlates activity signals to detect, investigate and act on potentially risky behavior inside an organization.
A REST endpoint at the non-routable address 169.254.169.254 that is reachable only from inside Azure resources and, among other things, issues access tokens for managed identities.
The compute infrastructure in Azure Data Factory that runs activities, acting as the bridge between an activity and a linked service. It comes in three types: Azure, self-hosted and Azure-SSIS.
A retired dedicated hosting option for Azure Logic Apps that placed workflows inside a private network; Microsoft recommends Logic Apps Standard with VNet integration as its successor.
A software testing practice that verifies components work together with the real services they depend on, such as queues, databases, authentication and configuration.

Intelligent document processing combines optical character recognition, natural language processing and machine learning to classify documents and extract structured data such as dates, amounts or parties from forms, invoices and contracts.

Intelligent recap is a Microsoft Teams Premium feature that generates AI notes, suggested tasks, chapters and personalized highlights from a transcribed meeting; intelligent call recap is also available with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
Automatic version history setting in SharePoint and OneDrive that caps versions per file and thins older versions over time while preserving recent ones; retention overrides trimming.

A design artifact for AI agents that defines one intent with its allowed actions, required inputs, systems it may touch and the evidence it must produce, serving as a machine-enforceable authorization boundary.

Microsoft's internal carbon fee, in place since 2012, charges its business groups a price per metric ton of carbon emissions tied to their operations and uses the proceeds to fund carbon reduction, renewable energy and related sustainability investments.
A self-service platform built by a platform team that gives developers curated tools, templates and workflows to build and deploy applications within organizational guardrails.
The network of physical devices such as sensors, appliances and industrial controllers that connect to the internet to collect and exchange data.
A private company website or network for internal information such as news, policies and tools; classic static intranets suffered from low engagement and poor mobile access.
A security capability that monitors network traffic for malicious activity using signatures of known attack patterns and can alert on or block it; in Azure it is a feature of Azure Firewall Premium.

An Intune policy type that bundles Windows Update for Business settings such as quality and feature update deferrals, deadlines, grace periods and restart behavior, assigned to groups of devices for staged rollouts.
In Dynamics 365, inventory dimensions are the labels that distinguish stock records: storage dimensions such as site, warehouse and location, and tracking dimensions such as batch and serial numbers.
A Dynamics 365 service that gives a central, near real-time view of inventory across locations, legal entities and data sources and supports reservations.
IOPS (input/output operations per second) measures how many read or write requests a storage system can handle each second.

name: Azure IoT Hub Device Provisioning Service (DPS)

desc.en: Azure service that lets devices enroll through a repeatable provisioning process; it authenticates a device and assigns it to an IoT hub based on defined enrollment rules.
State synchronization feature of Azure IoT Hub with desired properties written by the cloud and reported properties written by the device.
Azure IoT Hub feature that evaluates rules on message properties to send device-to-cloud messages to built-in or custom endpoints such as Event Hubs, storage or Fabric eventstreams.

An international standard model for manufacturing that describes levels from physical process and control through manufacturing operations management to enterprise planning, used to place responsibilities and interfaces.
iSCSI (Internet Small Computer Systems Interface) is a protocol that carries SCSI storage commands over IP networks, giving servers network access to block storage.
The international standard published by ISO and IEC that specifies requirements for an information security management system (ISMS); organizations can be certified against it.
Business Central data storage for key/value pairs that is isolated per extension, so other extensions cannot read the stored values; often used for secrets in development and test scenarios.

Microsoft program for software companies that build B2B applications on the Microsoft Cloud and publish them to Microsoft Marketplace; per the episode it includes Marketplace Rewards with marketing support, technical resources and Azure sponsorship.

IT service management (ITSM) covers the activities an organization performs to design, deliver, operate and control IT services for its customers, typically through processes such as incident, request and change management.
Jamf Pro is Jamf's enterprise device management platform for Apple devices such as Mac, iPhone and iPad; it can integrate with Microsoft Intune to share compliance signals.
Java is a general-purpose, object-oriented programming language compiled to bytecode for the Java virtual machine. The episode covers upgrading a Java 8-era Spring application to Java 21.
The programming language of the web platform, used for front-end and back-end development.
Atlassian's IT service management product built on Jira, used to receive, route and resolve service requests and incidents; it can be integrated with Microsoft Teams.
JSON-RPC is a lightweight remote procedure call protocol encoded in JSON. Version 2.0 is the message format used by the Model Context Protocol (MCP) between clients and servers.
JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) is a plain-text data format of label-value pairs, objects and lists that almost every modern web API uses to exchange data.

A hardened server, also called a jump server or jump host, that administrators connect to first and then hop from to other machines in a private network; as a regular VM it needs patching, monitoring and an exposed management port.

Just Enough Administration (JEA) is a Windows PowerShell security technology that lets organizations delegate only specific administrative tasks, such as restarting certain services, instead of full administrator rights.
An access model in which elevated permissions are granted only when needed and for a limited time, then expire automatically instead of remaining permanently assigned.
A lean practice of small, practical improvements made close to the work, often run as short kaizen events or workshops by the people who run the process.
KEDA is an open-source Kubernetes component that scales workloads based on events such as queue length or HTTP request rate, including scaling down to zero.

A key performance indicator is a measure used to judge how well an organization, process or activity is meeting its objectives. The episode argues that a KPI should act as a decision rule with an owner, a trigger and a pre-committed action.
An operational risk where critical process knowledge or capability is concentrated in one or a few individuals, creating a single point of failure when they are absent or leave.
Traditional lexical search that matches the exact words of a query against documents, often ranked with the BM25 algorithm; precise for exact terms but blind to meaning.
A reviewed support answer stored in the Dynamics 365 knowledge base that agents can search while working on a case and customers can read through a self-service portal.
A data model that represents entities and typed relationships explicitly so software can traverse connections, for example across production stages in a genealogy investigation.
The organized process by which an organization creates, shares, uses and maintains its knowledge and information; the episode applies it to SharePoint as a company knowledge platform.
KRBTGT is the Active Directory account whose key the Key Distribution Center uses to sign Kerberos tickets; rotating its password twice invalidates forged tickets.
KRITIS is the German term for critical infrastructure, such as energy, health or public administration, whose operators face stricter IT security and compliance requirements.
Open-source container orchestration software that places packaged applications on computing resources and manages their execution.

The key-value cache that transformer-based language models keep in memory during inference to store attention state for previous tokens; it grows with context length and concurrent users and can become a hardware bottleneck for self-hosted LLMs.
LangChain4j is an open-source Java library for building LLM-powered applications, offering a unified API over model providers plus tool calling, agents and RAG.
LangGraph is an open-source framework from LangChain for building stateful, multi-agent LLM applications as graphs of nodes and edges, with checkpointing and human approval steps.
A type of AI model trained on large amounts of text that generates likely text from patterns in its input; it powers conversational assistants such as Copilot.
Lateral movement describes an attacker moving from one system to another inside a network after gaining an initial foothold.

An open, vendor-neutral application protocol for accessing and maintaining directory information over IP networks; older Windows applications use it to look up users and groups in Active Directory or Microsoft Entra Domain Services.
Software for delivering, tracking and managing courses and training; in the episode, EC Learn is presented as an LMS built on Dataverse and Power Pages.

Least privilege is the security principle of giving an identity the smallest role at the smallest scope for the shortest time that still lets it do its work, limiting what an attacker can reach if the account is compromised.

Older sign-in protocols such as IMAP, SMTP and older Exchange ActiveSync versions that do not support multifactor authentication and can therefore be used to bypass MFA; blocking them is a common baseline Conditional Access policy.
In warehouse management, a unique ID for a pallet, carton, tote or other container, so that scanning it identifies the container and its recorded contents.
Lift and shift, also called rehosting, is a cloud migration approach that moves applications and data to the cloud with little or no change to their architecture.
LinkedIn Sales Navigator is LinkedIn's sales tool that can add relationship context such as mutual connections and company updates to Dynamics 365 Sales.
LinkedIn is a professional networking and employment platform owned by Microsoft, widely used for recruiting, job searching and building professional visibility.
LINQ (Language Integrated Query) is a set of .NET language features that adds query syntax to C# and Visual Basic across data sources such as collections and databases.

desc.ar: لغة القوالب Liquid المستخدمة في Power Pages لعرض المحتوى الديناميكي وبيانات Dataverse داخل صفحات الموقع.

desc.en: Llama is a family of large language models released by Meta AI, with open weights that can be downloaded and run on local hardware.
Open-source data framework for ingesting, indexing and retrieving data for large language model applications such as retrieval-augmented generation.

A knowledge pattern in which an AI reads raw sources once and compiles them into a maintained, cross-linked set of wiki pages governed by a schema, updating pages and flagging contradictions as new sources arrive instead of searching raw documents on every query.
LLMLingua is a family of prompt compression methods from Microsoft Research that remove less important tokens from prompts so large language models can work with shorter, cheaper inputs.

LLMOps is the practice of operating large language model applications in production, covering prompt and configuration versioning, evaluation, approval gates, safety checks, monitoring and audit trails.

A configurable rule set in Dynamics 365 warehouse management that decides which location stock should be put away to or picked from, based on factors such as product, storage needs, zone and capacity.
Azure Monitor tool and workspace for collecting, storing and querying log data from Azure, other clouds, on-premises servers and applications using Kusto Query Language (KQL).

Log4j is an open-source Java logging framework from the Apache Software Foundation; a critical vulnerability in it, disclosed in 2021, forced organizations to search their environments for affected applications.

In Azure Logic Apps Standard, stateful workflows persist their state and run history to external storage so they can run for long periods, wait for approvals and resume after restarts, while stateless workflows run in memory for short, fast operations.

Shared spaces in Microsoft Loop that group the pages, components, tasks and files of a project or team in one place; they can also be created as a tab in a Teams channel, with membership following the channel.

A parameter-efficient fine-tuning method introduced by Microsoft researchers that freezes a base model and trains small low-rank matrices inserted into its layers, producing compact, swappable adapters.
Lotus 1-2-3 was the dominant spreadsheet program of the 1980s, released by Lotus Development in 1983 and later overtaken by Microsoft Excel.
An approach in which a program learns patterns from examples instead of following rules written by hand, and uses them to make predictions.

Magma is a multimodal foundation model for AI agents from Microsoft Research. It is a vision-language-action model that perceives text and visual input and generates grounded actions such as UI navigation and robotic manipulation.
In-house large language model family from Microsoft AI, built as a sparse mixture-of-experts model for deep, multi-step reasoning and offered as a cloud-hosted model.
An organization-wide Exchange Online rule, also called a transport rule, that checks messages in transit against conditions and exceptions and applies actions before delivery.

In Dynamics 365 Finance, the ledger account that states what an amount relates to, such as cash, sales revenue or rent expense; main accounts have account types and can be grouped into main account categories for reporting.
A mainframe is a large, centralized computer shared by many users through terminals, with workloads queued and scheduled on one host.
A suite of premium Power Platform capabilities that lets admins govern environments at scale, for example with usage insights, sharing limits and solution checking.
A managed identity is an identity for an application or Azure resource whose credentials Azure creates and rotates automatically, so no secret has to be stored in code or configuration files.
An outside company that a business hires to run and manage its IT or cloud environment on its behalf.

The two modes of a Power Platform solution: the unmanaged solution is the editable working copy used in development, the managed solution is the locked copy exported for deployment to test and production.
Shop-floor software that records production activity against work orders and operations, such as the actual material consumed at a station.

MAPI (Messaging Application Programming Interface) is a proprietary Microsoft messaging API and data model underlying Exchange and Outlook, whose legacy data structures still shape Exchange development.
Visually designed, no-code data transformations in Azure Data Factory that run as activities inside pipelines on Apache Spark clusters managed by the service.
Markdown is a lightweight markup language with plain-text formatting syntax; Copilot Studio and Copilot Cowork store skills as Markdown (.md) files.
Market development funds, also called co-op funds, are partner earnings that Microsoft sets aside for approved marketing and enablement activities and that must be spent within a set period.

Master planning in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management combines current demand and supply, calculates net requirements and suggests planned purchase, production and transfer orders for planners to review.
A planning calculation that works backward from demand through the bill of materials and creates planned supply signals where shortages appear.
Open-source React component library that implements Google's Material Design and ships prebuilt, styled UI components.
Searching through possible actions, such as schedules or resource assignments, to find options that satisfy stated constraints while improving a defined objective.
Graph problem of partitioning the nodes into two groups so that the total weight of edges crossing between the groups is maximal; it is NP-hard in general and a common benchmark for QAOA.
A proposed operational metric for agentic AI systems: the time it takes to explain why a system behaved the way it did, as opposed to mean time to repair (MTTR) for deterministic failures.
A data design pattern that organizes lakehouse data into bronze (raw), silver (cleaned) and gold (consumption-ready) layers.
Memory poisoning is an attack in which malicious instructions are planted in content an AI agent stores in its persistent memory, so they resurface and influence later decisions.

Intermediary software that accepts messages from senders, stores them reliably and delivers them to receivers when they are ready, decoupling applications from each other; Azure Service Bus is Microsoft's fully managed message broker.
A tool in the Exchange admin center that follows email messages through mail flow to show whether they were delivered, failed or quarantined.

Meta Quest is Meta's line of virtual reality headsets; Quest 3 and Quest Pro can join Teams immersive experiences via the Microsoft Teams immersive app, with device management through Meta Horizon managed services and Intune.
Defining and applying a simple metadata model, such as columns and tags on documents, so content can be classified, discovered and used by search and Copilot.
An attack, also called prompt or push bombing, in which an attacker who already has a password floods the user with MFA approval prompts until the user approves one.
A lightweight object-relational mapper that executes hand-written SQL and maps results to plain objects, without full features such as change tracking or relationship management.
A learning approach that delivers training in small, short units focused on a single task, so learners can apply knowledge immediately.
Microservices is a software architecture pattern that splits an application into small, loosely coupled services that can be developed, tested and deployed independently.

desc.de: Open-Source-Framework von Microsoft zum Bau von KI-Agenten für Teams, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Studio und Webchat – mit Identität, Zustandsverwaltung, Aktivitätsprotokoll und Kanaladaptern, unabhängig vom gewählten Modell oder Orchestrator.

desc.en: A Microsoft 365 plan for small businesses that, according to the episode, includes Defender for Business along with email protection, device management, identity protection and data protection tools.
Microsoft's enterprise subscription plan that bundles the Microsoft 365 apps and services with core security, compliance and device management; E5 adds more advanced security and compliance features.
A Microsoft 365 enterprise licensing tier above E3 that, as discussed in the episode, unlocks additional Defender and identity security capabilities.
A Microsoft 365 enterprise licensing tier that, according to the episode, adds AI capabilities on top of the lower tiers at a notably higher price.
Microsoft 365 F3 is a Microsoft 365 license plan for frontline workers that provides core communication and collaboration capabilities at a lower cost than the E3 and E5 enterprise plans.
The Microsoft 365 membership object behind every team, which provisions a SharePoint site, a shared mailbox and calendar, a plan and other connected resources under one membership list.
Lifecycle management in Microsoft 365 governance covers how Teams, groups, sites and guests are provisioned, reviewed, archived and deleted over time, often with automation and templates.
An admin portal that helps managed service providers onboard, monitor and manage Microsoft 365 customer tenants at scale; it is separate from Azure Lighthouse.

Microsoft 365 Local is a deployment model that runs Exchange Server, SharePoint Server and Skype for Business Server on Azure Local infrastructure under the customer's control, aimed at sovereignty and data residency requirements.
Area of the Microsoft 365 admin center where Microsoft announces upcoming changes, feature updates and required admin actions, tagged with categories such as security or admin impact.

The unmanaged accumulation of workspaces, sharing links, permissions, guest access, connectors and other assets in a Microsoft 365 tenant that outpaces governance and is amplified when AI such as Copilot uses that content.
Microsoft's open-source framework for building AI agents and multi-agent workflows, created as the successor to Semantic Kernel and AutoGen.

The Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program is Microsoft's partner program, formerly the Microsoft Partner Network and Microsoft Cloud Partner Program, through which partners get benefits, designations, specializations and incentives.

name: AI gateway in Azure API Management

desc.en: Set of Azure API Management capabilities for securing, routing, limiting and monitoring traffic to AI models, MCP tool servers, agents and business APIs through one managed control point.
A free Microsoft tool for software companies that scores marketplace listings, such as AppSource listings, and gives AI-powered recommendations for improving them.
Microsoft Applied Skills are scenario-based credentials that validate specific hands-on technical skills, complementing role-based Microsoft certifications.
Microsoft's authentication app for phones, which can hold device-bound passkeys for work accounts in Microsoft Entra ID.
Contractual commitment by a customer to spend a set amount on Azure over a period of time; purchases of eligible marketplace offers can count toward it.

Microsoft Bot Framework is a set of SDKs and services for building conversational bots. In Microsoft Teams, bots and action-based message extensions typically run behind a Bot Framework endpoint that receives user requests and returns cards.
Microsoft Certified Trainer is an annual Microsoft membership program for professionals who deliver training on Microsoft technologies.

Microsoft Clarity is a free behavioral analytics tool from Microsoft that provides session recordings, heatmaps, scroll depth and rage-click detection. It can be deployed to modern SharePoint as a tenant-wide extension.
