Microsoft platform built on Power Platform and Dynamics 365 that helps organizations record, report and reduce their environmental impact, including carbon emissions and wider ESG data.
Microsoft Commerce Incentives is Microsoft's partner incentive framework in which partners enroll in engagements such as deployment funds, assessments and other incentive programs.
Microsoft's suite of FinOps tools to analyze, monitor and optimize cloud costs, with cost analysis, budgets, alerts and exports; also known as Azure Cost Management.

name: Microsoft Defender External Attack Surface Management (Defender EASM)

desc.en: Microsoft security service that discovers and continuously maps an organization's internet-facing assets, such as domains, hosts, IP addresses and certificates, starting from known seeds to give an outside-in view of the attack surface.
An endpoint security offering from Microsoft for small and medium businesses with up to 300 users. It is available as a standalone subscription and is included in Microsoft 365 Business Premium.

Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps is Microsoft's cloud access security broker that discovers the cloud apps used in an organization, rates their risk and helps protect data and detect threats across them.
Microsoft's cloud security service that combines cloud security posture management and workload protection across Azure, on-premises, AWS and GCP environments.
Microsoft's enterprise endpoint security platform, offered in Plan 1 and Plan 2, covering preventive protection, endpoint detection and response, automated investigation and advanced hunting.

Microsoft threat intelligence platform (Defender TI), built on the RiskIQ acquisition, that combines finished intelligence such as threat actor profiles with raw internet data such as passive DNS and certificates; its capabilities are being folded into Microsoft Defender.

Microsoft Defender capability that continuously discovers devices and software, assesses weaknesses, prioritizes them by risk and context, and tracks remediation until devices no longer report the exposure.
A Microsoft 365 service built on Microsoft Graph that surfaced documents colleagues were working on and had shared; Microsoft retired it in December 2024.

Microsoft Dev Box is an Azure service that gives developers self-service access to preconfigured, cloud-hosted Windows workstations organised in dev centers, projects and pools. Microsoft stopped new sign-ups and is moving its capabilities to Windows 365.

desc.de: Webbrowser von Microsoft mit integrierter Copilot-Seitenleiste; Copilot verhält sich dort teils anders als in Office-Apps wie Word oder Teams, etwa bei Funktionsumfang und der Durchsetzung von DLP- und Compliance-Regeln.

desc.en: Microsoft Entra ID P2 is the premium Microsoft Entra ID license tier that includes ID Protection and risk-based Conditional Access; it is included in Microsoft 365 E5.

Microsoft Entra ID Protection detects, investigates and remediates identity-based risks by scoring sign-in risk and user risk, which Conditional Access policies can use to require MFA, a password change or block access.
Microsoft Entra Kerberos lets Microsoft Entra ID issue Kerberos tickets from the cloud, so users can authenticate to services such as Azure Files without on-premises domain controllers.

A cloud infrastructure entitlement management (CIEM) solution that discovers permissions of all identities across Azure, AWS and Google Cloud, compares granted with actually used permissions and helps right-size and monitor them.

Logs in the Microsoft Entra admin center that record user and application sign-in attempts with status, error codes and Conditional Access results; they are the starting point for troubleshooting failed sign-ins.
A Microsoft Entra capability for discovering related tenants, establishing governance relationships between tenants, monitoring configuration and controlling secure tenant creation.
Microsoft service for issuing and verifying digital credentials that prove specific facts about a person, held in a wallet such as Microsoft Authenticator.

Microsoft Graph activity logs record the HTTP requests that the Microsoft Graph service receives and processes for a tenant, giving visibility into which applications call which endpoints. They can be exported through Azure Monitor diagnostic settings.
Microsoft Graph Data Connect extracts Microsoft 365 datasets in bulk on a schedule into Azure storage for analytics, after admin approval of each request.

Microsoft Graph permissions, also called scopes, define what an app may access; delegated permissions let an app act for a signed-in user, while application (app-only) permissions let it act with its own identity, often requiring admin consent.
PowerShell SDK that wraps the Microsoft Graph APIs and replaces the retired Azure AD PowerShell and MSOnline modules for managing Microsoft Entra ID and other Microsoft 365 services.
Schema extensions are a Microsoft Graph mechanism for adding strongly typed, discoverable custom data to supported Graph resources, defined once and then usable by authorized apps in a tenant.
The Microsoft Graph security API provides a single programmatic interface that connects multiple Microsoft security providers, for example to retrieve alerts or stream them to SIEM tools.
A set of reusable, framework-agnostic web components and authentication providers for working with Microsoft Graph, usable in web apps, Teams tabs and SharePoint web parts.
Microsoft HoloLens is a mixed reality headset developed by Microsoft that overlays holograms on the physical world and was used in enterprise scenarios such as training and field work.
Microsoft's annual conference for developers, IT professionals and partners, formerly known as TechEd.
Microsoft's framework for classifying, labeling and protecting sensitive data, now known as Microsoft Purview Information Protection.
Microsoft's free learning platform with modules and learning paths on Microsoft products; its content can be turned on as a source in Viva Learning.
Microsoft Lync was Microsoft's unified communications platform for instant messaging, presence, voice and meetings; it was rebranded as Skype for Business, which Microsoft Teams later replaced.
The Microsoft Most Valuable Professional (MVP) award, which Microsoft gives to independent technology experts who share their knowledge with the community.
Microsoft Partner Center is Microsoft's portal where partners manage their relationship with Microsoft, including membership, benefits, incentives, customers and support.
Microsoft partner incentives are funding and reward payments Microsoft makes to partners for eligible activities and sales, which partners can reinvest in pre-sales, co-marketing and events.

Microsoft's dedicated security processor built into the chip that provides a hardware-based root of trust, secure identity, attestation and cryptographic services; it is the security subsystem of the Azure Sphere MCU.

The Microsoft Product Terms are Microsoft's published licensing terms that are incorporated into customer agreements and govern the use of Microsoft software and online services. The episode describes them as part of the contractual baseline for Microsoft 365 Copilot, alongside the Data Protection Addendum.
Microsoft Purview Audit records user and administrator activity from Microsoft 365 services in a searchable unified audit log, offered as Audit (Standard) and Audit (Premium).
Search capability in Microsoft Purview for quickly checking whether terms appear across Microsoft 365 locations, often used for early fact finding before a formal eDiscovery case.

Microsoft Purview solution that helps organizations decide how long Microsoft 365 content is kept and whether it is deleted or reviewed at the end of its lifespan, mainly through retention policies and retention labels.
Microsoft Purview solution for managing official records in Microsoft 365, using retention labels, record declaration, disposition review and audit history across their lifecycle.

Microsoft Scout is an always-on desktop AI agent for Windows 11 and macOS, described by Microsoft as its first Autopilot, that works proactively across Microsoft 365, local files and the web under its own identity.

Microsoft's generative AI security assistant that integrates with products such as Defender, Entra and Intune; in the episode it is described as the Copilot used for Intune, separate from Microsoft 365 Copilot.
Microsoft security solution in the Defender portal that gives security teams a unified view of exposure and security posture across Microsoft security products and connected data sources.
A low-cost storage tier for Microsoft Sentinel that separates storage from compute, mirrors ingested logs automatically and allows long-term retention of security data that can still be queried.
Microsoft's cloud-native SIEM and security operations platform that collects security data into a Log Analytics workspace, detects threats with analytics rules and supports hunting with KQL.
Microsoft Sway is a web-based presentation and storytelling app in the Microsoft 365 family; in the episode it is used to share information externally.
Microsoft's public site for security, privacy and compliance information about its cloud services, hosting documentation and resources that customers can use for audits and assessments.
Open-source PowerShell module that uses Desired State Configuration to export, configure, compare and monitor Microsoft 365 tenant configuration as code, including drift detection.

Software that sits between applications and systems to connect them; the episode argues that schedule-based, polling middleware creates a hidden cost and should dissolve into event-driven platform services.
A migration phase in which the old and new environments, for example two Microsoft 365 tenants, run side by side and are linked so mail and collaboration keep working while users move in batches.
The moment in a migration when users stop working in the old system or tenant and switch to the new one, typically scheduled for a quiet window such as a weekend.

A migration factory is a repeatable delivery model for large cloud migrations that moves workloads in waves using shared standards, runbooks, validation gates and rollback patterns instead of one-off projects.
A migration wave is a group of applications and workloads migrated together, so a large estate moves in sequenced batches and each wave's lessons carry into the next.
Minecraft is a 3D sandbox video game developed by Mojang Studios, owned by Microsoft, in which players build and explore persistent worlds; it is also used for learning and team-building scenarios.
Minimal APIs are a simplified approach in ASP.NET Core for building HTTP APIs with minimal code and configuration, without controllers.
Mistral OCR is an optical character recognition API from Mistral AI that converts documents, including scans and tables, into structured Markdown; in the episode it runs in Azure AI Foundry.
A free, public knowledge base of adversary tactics and techniques based on real-world observations, maintained by MITRE and used as a shared language to describe how attacks are carried out.
Mixed reality blends digital content such as instructions and 3D objects with the physical environment so both can be seen and used together.

Mixture of experts is a model architecture in which a gating mechanism activates only a subset of expert sub-networks for each input, so a model can have many parameters while using fewer per inference.

desc.hi: मशीन लर्निंग मॉडल के परीक्षण, डिप्लॉयमेंट और मॉनिटरिंग को स्वचालित पाइपलाइन के ज़रिए दोहराने योग्य और भरोसेमंद बनाने की प्रैक्टिस।

desc.en: Mobile Application Management (MAM) in Microsoft Intune protects corporate data at the app level, for example on personal devices, without managing the whole device, and allows selective wipe of work data.
A short documentation artifact for an AI model or use case that records its purpose, intended use, data sets, performance and known limitations, used as evidence in AI governance reviews.

A model gateway is a single entry point for all AI model traffic: agents call the gateway instead of models directly, so authentication, policy enforcement, routing, cost attribution and logging can be applied centrally.
Storing model weights in a lower-bit numerical format, for example four-bit NF4, to cut memory needs; combined with LoRA (QLoRA) it allows fine-tuning large models on a single GPU.
Model router is a deployable chat model in Microsoft Foundry (formerly Azure AI Foundry) that selects an underlying large language model in real time to respond to each prompt.

Umbrella term for the modern digital workplace, covering both the technical side (cloud identities, security, infrastructure) and the end-user side (collaboration tools, generative AI and new ways of working).

An architecture with a single deployable unit that is divided into modules with clear internal boundaries, typically by business capability, so that parts can be extracted into services later if needed.
A version control strategy in which multiple projects or systems are kept in one shared repository while still being deployable independently.
A usage metric that counts the unique users who actively use a product within a month; used here to track whether Copilot adoption sticks.
MQTT delivery levels that govern acknowledgement and retry between client and broker: QoS 0 (at most once), QoS 1 (at least once) and QoS 2 (exactly once); Azure IoT Hub supports QoS 0 and 1.

A lightweight publish-and-subscribe messaging protocol in which producers publish messages to topics on a broker that forwards them to subscribed consumers, with quality of service levels for delivery.

MTTR (mean time to resolution or recovery) is an operational metric for the average time it takes to restore a service after an incident; it is a key measure for incident response and DevOps performance.

Multi-access edge computing places compute, storage and application hosting physically close to where data is generated, typically alongside a 5G network. It enables real-time processing without round trips to a distant cloud region.
An AI solution design in which several agents each have their own scope, instructions and tools, typically with a front agent that routes requests to specialized agents.
An architecture in which several AI agents work together, typically with one orchestrating agent delegating tasks to specialized child agents.

Multi-cloud is a strategy of running workloads across more than one public cloud provider, such as Azure, AWS and Google Cloud. It promises portability and less vendor lock-in but adds operational complexity.
A repository strategy in which services, libraries or products live in separate, independently versioned repositories, with teams coordinating through APIs, contracts and versioning.

Azure Backup feature that requires a second authorization, via a Resource Guard owned by a different person, before critical operations on a vault such as disabling soft delete or reducing protection.
Multimodal AI refers to models and applications that process more than one input type, such as text, images, voice and video.

Multistage approvals, formerly called advanced approvals, are an agent flow capability in Microsoft Copilot Studio that chains AI approval stages and human (manual) stages with conditions in a single approval process.
Multitenancy is a software architecture in which a single instance of an application serves multiple customers (tenants) whose data is kept isolated from each other.
British AI entrepreneur, co-founder of DeepMind and Inflection AI, and CEO of Microsoft AI.
n8n is a fair-code workflow automation platform that connects apps, APIs and AI models through nodes on a visual canvas and can run as a cloud service or self-hosted.
A natural language processing technique that identifies and classifies entities such as people, organizations, locations and dates in text, often used to enrich documents with metadata for retrieval.
A naming convention is a consistent format for naming cloud resources, encoding information such as workload, environment and region so resources can be identified, governed and automated.
Nearshoring is the outsourcing of business processes, especially IT work, to companies in a nearby country, typically one or two time zones away.

Software vendor whose Nerdio Manager platform helps IT teams and MSPs deploy, manage and cost-optimize Azure Virtual Desktop, Windows 365 and Intune environments; the guest leads a team building a new platform there.
Nested groups are groups that are members of other groups, so a user's effective access can come indirectly through several layers of group membership.
In the episode, the depth of trusted relationships with operators and experts, as opposed to the size of a passive audience, which speeds up learning and opens lower-friction paths to collaboration.
NFS is the standard network file system protocol for Linux and Unix systems; Azure Files supports it alongside SMB.
An Azure networking control that filters inbound and outbound traffic between resources in an Azure virtual network using security rules.

Network slicing lets multiple logical networks with their own performance characteristics and security boundaries run on the same physical 5G infrastructure. It is used to isolate safety-critical traffic from video or guest traffic.
A specialized processor that accelerates AI and machine learning workloads, running repetitive AI math with much lower power draw than a CPU or GPU.

The new commerce experience (NCE) is Microsoft's commerce model for CSP subscriptions, with monthly, annual or three-year term commitments and limited options to reduce seats after a short cancellation window.

NIS2 is the EU directive on cybersecurity for essential and important entities in sectors such as energy, transport, health and digital infrastructure. It requires risk management measures and timely incident reporting.
A voluntary framework from the US National Institute of Standards and Technology for managing AI risks, organized around governing, mapping, measuring and managing risk.
Cross-platform, open-source JavaScript runtime that runs JavaScript outside the browser on Google's V8 engine, commonly used for web back ends.

A non-disclosure agreement (NDA) is a legal contract between two or more parties that defines confidential information the parties agree not to disclose; NDAs can be unilateral, bilateral or multilateral.

A non-human identity is a digital identity used by software rather than a person, such as a service principal, managed identity or AI agent identity, that authenticates and acts on resources and therefore needs its own ownership, permission scoping and revocation path.
In quality management, a nonconformance is a failure to meet a stated requirement, documented against an identifiable requirement and handled through containment, correction and corrective action.

Generative AI models sample across possible answers, so the same input can produce different outputs on different runs, unlike deterministic rule-based automation; this variability has to be managed with monitoring and governance.

Now Assist is ServiceNow's generative AI capability embedded in Now Platform workflows such as IT service management, customer service and HR service delivery, offering features like case and incident summarization.
JavaScript package manager and public package registry, the default package manager for Node.js; projects pull third-party libraries and their transitive dependencies from it.
An NTLM relay attack forwards a victim's NTLM authentication to another server to gain access as that user, typically where SMB or LDAP signing is not enforced.
NT LAN Manager (NTLM) is a suite of Microsoft security protocols for authentication in Windows networks, still required by some legacy applications and supported by Microsoft Entra Domain Services.
NuGet is the package manager for .NET, used to create, publish and consume reusable code packages, including their transitive dependencies.

An MFA push-notification safeguard in which the sign-in screen shows a number that the user must type into the authenticator app to approve the sign-in. Microsoft enforces it for Microsoft Authenticator push notifications.
NVIDIA's GPU microarchitecture that succeeds Hopper; the Grace Blackwell GB200 superchip pairs an Arm-based Grace CPU with Blackwell GPUs for large-scale AI training and inference.
NVIDIA's platform for 3D simulation and industrial digital twins; the episode mentions Microsoft working with NVIDIA to link Fabric twins into Omniverse.

desc.he: NVIDIA היא יצרנית מעבדים גרפיים (GPU) ותוכנות כמו CUDA, TensorRT ו-NVIDIA Container Toolkit, המשמשות להרצת הסקת AI על GPU.

desc.en: NVIDIA's high-bandwidth interconnect that links GPUs and CPUs, used in GB200 NVL72 racks to let 72 GPUs share one NVLink domain.
NVM Express is an interface standard for accessing non-volatile storage, typically SSDs attached over PCI Express, designed for highly parallel input/output.
A product from the Nx team that acts as a meta harness for AI coding agents, letting one session work across multiple dependent Git repositories.
An open-source build system and task orchestration tool chain for monorepos, with generators, project graph, caching and the commercial Nx Cloud service.
An open authorization standard that decides what an app can reach on a user's behalf using scoped access tokens; it is not a login system on its own, which is why OpenID Connect adds sign-in on top.

OAuth 2.0 is an authorization standard in which an app obtains a short-lived access token (bearer token) that stands in for the signed-in user when calling an API, instead of sending a password or a long-lived API key.
Object-level security (OLS) secures specific tables or columns in a semantic model so that they do not exist for users without permission.
The ability to understand what is happening inside a system or integration from its outputs, using tracing, correlation IDs, dashboards, alerts and replay capabilities rather than plain logs alone.
Open Data Protocol, a standard way for systems to expose and query data over the web; Dataverse includes a virtual table provider for OData version 4.
A manufacturing metric for how effectively equipment is used, combining availability, performance and quality.

A Microsoft API that delivers user, admin, system and policy events from Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Entra audit logs as content blobs by record type, used to stream unified audit log data into a store you control.

desc.es: Superficie de scripts basada en TypeScript para automatizar Excel en la web y tareas de Microsoft 365, también desde Power Automate.

desc.en: Identity and access management company based in San Francisco whose cloud platform provides single sign-on to many applications; cited in the episode as a separate identity system to consolidate into Microsoft Entra ID.
Ollama is an open-source tool for downloading and running large language models on a local machine or server, exposing them through a local REST API.
An OAuth 2.0 flow in which a middle-tier service exchanges the token of the signed-in user for a token to a downstream API, so the downstream call is made with the user's identity and permissions.

The on-premises data gateway (often called the Power BI gateway) is a Windows application installed inside a private network that carries data between on-premises sources and Microsoft cloud services such as Power BI, Power Apps, Power Automate and Microsoft Fabric, using outbound connections only. It runs in standard or personal mode.
The EU VAT One Stop Shop lets a business declare and pay VAT due in several member states through its home tax authority; the episode notes that local input VAT cannot be deducted in the OSS return.
The OneCopy principle in Microsoft Fabric means data is stored once in OneLake and read directly by multiple engines such as Spark, SQL and Power BI instead of being duplicated between tools.
A OneDrive sync feature that shows all cloud files in File Explorer as online-only placeholders and downloads them only when opened, saving local disk space.
A OneDrive sync app setting (Choose folders) that controls which OneDrive folders are synced to a device; unchecked folders stay only in the cloud.

A OneDrive feature that adds a cloud-managed shortcut to a shared SharePoint library or folder in the user's OneDrive instead of syncing a replica. The episode warns that deleting or renaming such a shortcut can affect the shared source.
The OneDrive sync software on a computer that detects local and cloud changes and keeps files in both places identical, including chunked, resumable and differential uploads.
OneLake security lets organizations define role-based access, including row-level and object-level restrictions, once on data in OneLake so it applies across Fabric engines and endpoints.

Pointers in Microsoft Fabric's OneLake that reference data stored elsewhere, inside Fabric or in external storage, without copying it. The data stays at the target path while the shortcut appears in a lakehouse or other item.
The single, organization-wide logical data lake that comes with Microsoft Fabric; shortcuts let workloads reference data in other locations without importing a duplicate copy.

desc.pt: Motor de inferência multiplataforma da Microsoft para modelos ONNX, com provedores de execução como CUDA e TensorRT.

desc.en: A design philosophy holding that the things people design and create in turn shape the people who use them.
A formal set of shared definitions for a domain that specifies the types of things and the relationships that may connect them, so that people and systems interpret data the same way.

OPC Unified Architecture, an industrial communication standard for exchanging data in a structured information model, with typed values, status codes, client-server subscriptions and certificate-based application security.
OpenAI is an AI research and product company known for ChatGPT and the GPT models; the episode discusses its partnership with Microsoft, including its commitment to run workloads on Azure.
An open specification for machine-readable descriptions of web APIs, used by Semantic Kernel and Microsoft 365 Copilot to describe what plugins and extensions can do.
OpenClaw is an open-source, self-hosted AI agent framework that connects to multiple large language models and acts as the harness around them.

OpenFGA is an open source fine-grained authorization engine inspired by Google Zanzibar and hosted as a Cloud Native Computing Foundation project; it answers checks such as whether a user can access a given object.
An authentication protocol built on top of OAuth 2.0 that uses compact JSON tokens to handle sign-in; Microsoft recommends it as the default for new cloud apps.
OpenRewrite is an open-source automated refactoring ecosystem that applies recipes to source code. In the episode its recipes drive the migration of Java APIs during the upgrade.
A vendor-neutral, open-source observability standard and framework for instrumenting applications to emit traces, metrics and logs.

OpenTofu is an open source infrastructure-as-code tool forked from Terraform after HashiCorp moved Terraform to the Business Source License. It is governed by the Linux Foundation under the MPL 2.0 license.
An open-source framework and file format, originally developed by Pixar, for describing, composing and exchanging 3D scenes between tools and engines.

Hardware, software and work involved in monitoring and controlling physical production processes and equipment, as distinct from information technology (IT) that covers business, computing and data services.
A Teams Phone connectivity option in which a Microsoft-certified carrier provides PSTN connectivity, numbers and the session border controllers, with numbers managed in the Teams admin center.
Technology that reads the characters visible in an image or document and turns them into machine-readable text, without by itself knowing what that text means.

Organism as a Service is a concept described by Sonny Gillissen in which AI, for example through agent loops in Azure Logic Apps, lets integrations interpret context, react to unexpected situations and respond instead of only executing predefined workflows.
A context layer described by Rishi Sapra with five layers (data, logic, tools, skills and governance) that grounds AI agents in an organization's certified knowledge.

The accumulated cost of unresolved decisions, unclear ownership and inconsistent processes in an organization, paid as ongoing coordination overhead; distinct from technical debt, which lives in the code.
An organizational unit (OU) is a container, like a labeled folder, inside Active Directory used to group accounts and to scope tasks such as synchronization.
An origin group in Azure Front Door is a set of backend origins that receive traffic; it defines health probes and load balancing based on priority, latency and weight.
Power Automate flows whose owner has left, is disabled or was never a real person, so nobody is accountable for them while they may keep running or silently fail.
SharePoint or Teams sites that no longer have an active owner, typically because the original owner left the organization, while their content and permissions remain in the tenant.
A Microsoft 365 collaboration space such as a team, group or SharePoint site that is still active but no longer has a current owner responsible for membership, sharing and lifecycle decisions.
A pricing model for consulting and IT services in which clients pay for measurable business results, often as build fees plus recurring retainers or licences, instead of billable hours.
Actionable messages extend email in Outlook so recipients can take quick actions or fill in fields in an Adaptive Card without leaving Outlook.
A manufacturing metric that combines availability, performance and quality to show how well equipment is used relative to its planned production time.
Content in Microsoft 365 that is shared more broadly than intended, for example through organization-wide or anonymous links, which AI assistants like Copilot can surface to users.
The Open Worldwide Application Security Project, a public community project that maintains shared resources on common web attacks; its Core Rule Set is the basis of managed WAF rules.
PAC validation checks the Kerberos Privilege Attribute Certificate in a ticket against the KDC signature, so forged or tampered group claims such as silver tickets are rejected.
A packaging machine standard from the Organization for Machine Automation and Control (OMAC) that defines a common set of machine states and modes, such as stopped, execute, held or complete.
Fixed-layout, print-oriented reports in Power BI and SQL Server Reporting Services, defined in RDL, with precise control over page size, margins, headers, footers and page breaks.

Behavior of SQL Server-style engines that compile a plan for the parameter values seen at compile time and reuse the cached plan, which can perform poorly for very different parameter values; also called parameter sensitivity.

Azure capability that links a partner's Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program ID to the credentials used to manage a customer's Azure resources, so Microsoft can recognize the partner's influence on Azure consumption.

Composite score in the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program that measures a partner's performance, skilling and customer success per solution area; it determines eligibility for Solutions Partner designations.
A partner development manager (PDM) is the Microsoft role that manages a partner relationship, helping the partner navigate programs and connect with Microsoft field sellers.
Pass-the-hash is a lateral movement technique in which a captured NTLM password hash is reused to authenticate to other systems without knowing the clear-text password.

Pass-through authentication is a hybrid identity sign-in method in which Microsoft Entra ID validates a user's password against on-premises Active Directory at sign-in time via local authentication agents.
A historical record of which IP addresses domain names resolved to over time, used in threat intelligence to connect attacker infrastructure.
A phishing-resistant sign-in credential based on a public/private key pair defined by the FIDO2 standards; the private key stays on the user's device and is unlocked with a biometric or PIN.

Password hash synchronization is a hybrid identity sign-in method that syncs protected hashes of on-premises Active Directory passwords to Microsoft Entra ID, so users can sign in to cloud services with the same password without the readable password being sent to the cloud.
Password writeback is an optional, deliberately configured feature that sends a password changed or reset in the cloud back to on-premises Active Directory, so both accounts keep the same password.
The default cloud billing model in which you are billed after the fact for the resources you actually consumed.

Payables Agent is a Microsoft-built AI agent in Dynamics 365 Business Central that reads vendor invoice PDFs received by email, extracts the details and prepares purchase invoices for human review before posting.
PBIX is the Power BI Desktop report file format that bundles report pages, data model, queries and visuals in a single file; the episode argues that emailing PBIX files around is not version control.
An iterative four-step improvement method (plan, do, check, act) used in lean and continuous improvement to test a change against expected results before making it standard.
In master planning, pegging is the automatic link the planning calculation creates between a demand transaction and the supply expected to cover it.

A per-tenant extension is a Business Central extension built for one customer's own environment rather than published for all Business Central customers, typically to support a process unique to that company.

A risk metric in Microsoft Entra Permissions Management that compares the permissions an identity has been granted with the permissions it actually uses; a higher score means more unused, excessive permissions.
The accumulated backlog of overly broad, inherited or outdated access rights, such as content shared with everyone, that stays latent until AI tools like Copilot surface the data at machine speed.

Permission drift is the gradual divergence of an access model from current business reality as access keeps evolving through local decisions, role changes, leftover groups and exceptions that are never removed.

desc.es: Mecanismo de SharePoint por el que bibliotecas, carpetas y archivos heredan los permisos del sitio padre; romper la herencia permite asignar permisos únicos a contenidos sensibles.

desc.en: A Microsoft Entra Permissions Management feature that lets identities request narrowly scoped cloud permissions for a limited time, optionally with approval, after which they expire automatically.

Design approach for Microsoft 365 Copilot in which reusable intent (instructions, constraints, definitions) and a curated, governed set of sources persist beyond a single conversation instead of being re-entered in every prompt.
An approach that starts analytics and AI work from defined personas, their decisions, pain points and business questions before building semantic models, reports and agents.

A persona represents the goals, responsibilities and working environment of a specific user group. In the episode, personas such as a field engineer or finance analyst define what a Copilot Studio agent must know and do.
Personal branding is the practice of deliberately shaping how a professional is perceived, for example through content, speaking and social media, so that they are known for specific expertise.

Information that can be used to identify a specific person, such as names, contact details or identification numbers; in customer service it must be protected, for example by redaction and access controls.
Pester is the open-source test and mock framework for PowerShell; it runs unit and integration tests for scripts and modules and is commonly used in CI/CD pipelines.

Phi-3 is a family of small language models from Microsoft, including Phi-3-mini, Phi-3-small, Phi-3-medium and Phi-3-vision, designed for low-latency, cost-sensitive and on-device or local deployment.
Microsoft's family of small language models released under the MIT license, including Phi-4-mini and Phi-4-multimodal, designed to run efficiently on local devices and edge hardware.

Multifactor authentication methods, such as security keys and passkeys, that cannot be relayed through a fake login page because no reusable secret is exchanged and the credential only signs for the genuine site.
Social engineering attack in which fake emails or websites that look legitimate trick people into revealing credentials or other sensitive information or into installing malware.

An OAuth extension defined in RFC 7636 in which the client creates a one-time secret at the start of sign-in and must present it when redeeming the authorization code, protecting against code interception.
A Power Platform feature where makers describe a business need and AI proposes a solution design with apps, pages, reports and automations, then helps create them.
Planning Optimization is the engine Microsoft uses to run master planning in Dynamics 365 cloud environments; it calculates requirements outside the main application and runs regenerative plans.

A software engineering discipline focused on building standardized, self-service toolchains, services and processes that development teams can use without depending on a central team, often in the form of an internal developer platform.
Playwright is a browser automation framework that lets software launch a browser, navigate websites, fill out forms and click buttons; Scout uses it for web tasks.

Open-source, community-maintained .NET SDK from the Microsoft 365 PnP community that offers a graph-first, fluent API for SharePoint and Teams and handles throttling; it is not supported by Microsoft.
Open-source set of SharePoint Framework web parts from the Microsoft 365 community (PnP) for building search-driven pages in SharePoint Online, such as search boxes, results, filters and verticals.

Community-maintained open-source library of reusable, SharePoint- and Microsoft 365-aware React controls for SharePoint Framework solutions, such as people picker, taxonomy picker, list view and file picker.
Open-source community JavaScript library that wraps the SharePoint and Microsoft Graph REST APIs, handling requests and authentication so developers write less boilerplate code.
A point of presence is an edge location in a provider's global network where user requests first connect; Azure Front Door uses PoPs to route traffic, cache content and apply security close to users.
Policy as code is the practice of expressing governance, security and compliance rules as versioned code that is evaluated automatically, for example during deployment, to allow or block changes.
A policy decision point is the component of an access control architecture that evaluates an authorization request against defined policies and returns a deterministic permit or deny decision.
Architectural component that evaluates a request against policy synchronously and allows or denies the action before the state change commits; the counterpart to a policy decision point.
A short notice shown to the sender, for example in Outlook, telling them that a rule or policy applies to the message they are composing.
Cryptographic algorithms designed to resist attacks by quantum computers, such as the NIST-standardized lattice-based ML-KEM and ML-DSA and the hash-based SLH-DSA.
A Power Apps canvas app control that opens the device's native scanner to read barcodes and QR codes; Microsoft has since retired it in favor of the barcode reader control.
A Microsoft framework that lets developers build their own code components with HTML, CSS and TypeScript and use them inside model-driven apps, canvas apps and Power Pages.
A component library is a special type of canvas app in Power Apps that holds reusable canvas components, such as headers and buttons, which other canvas apps in the environment can import.

Containers are layout controls in Power Apps canvas apps that position their child controls automatically, either manually or in horizontal or vertical auto-layout, so screens can respond to different sizes without X and Y formulas.

Delegation in Power Apps canvas apps means a query is processed by the data source instead of the app; non-delegable queries only evaluate a limited number of records, which can silently return incomplete results on large SharePoint lists.
Figma plugin created by Microsoft MVP Lukas Pavelka that moves designs, components and design systems between Figma and Power Apps canvas apps, with a free and a pro version.

The browser-based Power Apps maker portal is where makers build apps, flows and solutions with a point-and-click experience. It is well suited to prototyping but offers limited control over moving work between environments.

Per-user Power Apps license that lets users run apps using premium capabilities such as Dataverse, model-driven apps and premium connectors, which are not covered by the Power Apps rights included in Microsoft 365.

The open-source Node.js package used by Power Apps code apps that generates typed model and service files for data sources and connects custom code to Power Platform services such as connectors and authentication.
An AI-native, prompt-driven experience in Power Apps (in preview) where makers describe what they want and AI generates the plan, data model and app.

A role or cross-functional responsibility, framed in this episode, for designing how decision rights, data ownership, access and escalation paths flow through an organization so that a transformation actually changes how work moves.
A Power Automate setting on triggers and Apply to each loops that lets independent items run in parallel instead of sequentially, with a configurable degree of parallelism.

A Power Automate licensing option that licenses an individual automated process (flow) instead of each user, so one licensed flow can serve many users in high-volume scenarios. It was formerly known as the per flow plan.
The list of past runs of a Power Automate cloud flow, kept only for a limited retention period; the episode stresses that it is a debugging aid rather than a permanent audit record.
The event that starts a Power Automate flow, such as a new email, a submitted form, a button click or a schedule; every flow has one trigger followed by one or more actions.
Notifications in the Power BI service that fire when a value on a dashboard tile crosses a threshold; they are limited to tiles pinned to dashboards, such as cards, gauges and KPIs.

name: Org apps (Microsoft Fabric and Power BI)

desc.en: Org apps are a Microsoft Fabric item type that content creators use to package Power BI reports and other items for consumers, allowing multiple apps per workspace. The episode presents them as the single governed doorway for report distribution.
Performance analyzer is a Power BI Desktop pane that records how long each report visual takes to load, broken down into categories such as DAX query and visual display time.

Power BI Premium Per User is a per-user license that gives individual users access to most Power BI Premium features; it does not provision a Fabric capacity, and users of content in a PPU workspace also need a PPU license.

Power BI Premium is a capacity-based Power BI offering that provides dedicated resources and lets content be distributed to viewers without per-user Pro licenses; Microsoft now steers new customers to Fabric capacity.
Power BI Pro is a per-user Power BI license that lets users create, publish, share and collaborate on Power BI content.

A Power BI Desktop project (PBIP) saves report and semantic model definitions as plain-text files in a folder structure instead of a single binary PBIX file, enabling source control with tools like Git.
Model relationships in Power BI connect two tables through a shared column and act as filter pathways, defined by cardinality, cross filter direction and an active or inactive state.
Microsoft's desktop authoring tool for paginated reports (RDL) that are published to the Power BI service.
Power BI report themes are JSON-based theme files that apply colors, fonts and visual formatting consistently across a Power BI report, and can be distributed centrally as organizational themes.
Power BI Desktop preview visual that colors predefined regions such as countries, states or custom TopoJSON boundaries by a measure, instead of plotting points on a map.
A slicer is a Power BI visual that filters the other visuals on a report page; its selected, unselected, hover and disabled states can be styled through the report theme.

A Power BI feature in which semantic model authors define approved responses to common questions, so that Copilot returns a consistent, prevalidated answer when a user prompt matches a trigger phrase.
A Power BI workspace app is a curated bundle of reports and dashboards published from a workspace, with audiences that control which content each group sees.
Named, reusable Power Fx functions defined at app level in Power Apps canvas apps, used to centralize repeated logic such as model normalization, type coercion and payload assembly.
Server logic in Power Pages lets makers run JavaScript on the server, close to Dataverse, for operations that should not run in the browser, with access controlled by web roles and table permissions.

Table permissions in Power Pages control which Dataverse records site users can access and what they can do with them, scoped for example globally, by contact or by account and assigned through web roles.

The Power Pages Web API lets site pages create, read, update and delete Dataverse table records from client-side JavaScript; access is controlled by enabled tables, allowed fields and table permissions.

Power Pivot provides advanced data modeling in Microsoft Excel, letting users relate multiple tables in a data model and write calculations in DAX; it was introduced in 2010 and later became one of the building blocks of Power BI.
The practice of managing Power Platform apps through development, testing and production, typically by moving solutions between environments.

A Power Platform Center of Excellence (CoE) is a team and set of practices that supports makers and administers, governs and nurtures Power Platform adoption across an organization, beyond tooling and dashboards.
Dataflows in Microsoft Power Platform use Power Query to ingest, transform and load data into Dataverse or other destinations, on demand or on a schedule.

A container in Microsoft Power Platform where business data, apps, chatbots and flows are stored and managed together. Each environment belongs to a Microsoft Entra tenant, is bound to a region and can hold at most one Dataverse database.
The native deployment pipelines built into Power Platform that move solutions between environments such as development, test and production, aimed at simplifying ALM for smaller teams.

A container in Power Platform that carries an app and all of its customizable components (such as apps, flows, tables and connectors) between environments. It holds metadata and configuration, not business data.

A Power Platform admin setting that blocks cross-tenant connections through Microsoft Entra ID-based connectors unless the external tenant is on an explicit allow list. The episode describes it as enforced by default, breaking undocumented cross-tenant flows.

name: Power Platform Tools extension for Visual Studio Code

desc.en: Power Platform Tools is a Visual Studio Code extension that brings the Power Platform CLI into VS Code and supports downloading, editing and uploading Power Pages site content.
Power Query M is the functional, case-sensitive formula language used to express data mashups in Power Query across Power BI, Excel and other Microsoft services.
Power usage effectiveness (PUE) is the ratio of a data center's total facility energy to the energy used by its IT equipment; values above 1.0 reflect overhead such as cooling and power conversion.

The @powerpages participant in GitHub Copilot Chat for Visual Studio Code, part of the Power Platform Tools extension, provides Power Pages-aware code generation and explanations, for example for Liquid and form validation (preview).
A package of PowerShell commands for a specific job or service that is installed once and loaded when needed.
The PowerShell mechanism, written as a vertical bar, that passes the output of one command as input to the next so small commands can be chained.
Microsoft's command-line shell and scripting language for Windows and other platforms.

A knowledge graph based on the product-process-resource (PPR) model that links ERP, MES, historian and maintenance records so people and AI can trace how a product, process and resource came together in production.
Predictive analytics uses historical and current data with statistical or AI models to forecast likely future outcomes, such as supply delays, pipeline conversion or customer churn.
Predictive lead and opportunity scoring in Dynamics 365 Sales uses a model trained on historical sales outcomes to score leads and opportunities by their likelihood to convert or close.
Predictive maintenance uses condition evidence such as sensor measurements to warn about developing equipment faults early enough for maintenance to plan an intervention before functional failure.

Power Platform connectors classified as premium, such as connectors to specialized or external systems and custom connectors, which require additional licensing beyond the standard connectors included with Microsoft 365.
A Power BI feature that lets model authors simplify the schema and add instructions so that Copilot gives more accurate answers.
Hidden SharePoint and OneDrive library that stores preserved copies of content that is edited or deleted while a retention policy, retention label or hold applies.

A conflict of interest that arises when one party (the agent) acts on behalf of another (the principal) while their goals and information diverge. The episode applies it to AI agents that follow literal instructions rather than business intent.

Private 5G is a dedicated cellular network operated for a single enterprise site, such as a factory, port or hospital. It uses scheduled access, SIM-based device identity and network slicing to deliver predictable latency for operational technology workloads.
A private branch exchange (PBX) is a private telephone system that connects internal extensions within an organization and links them to the public telephone network.
Microsoft Teams channels visible only to invited members of the team, each backed by its own separate SharePoint site.
Privileged access management (PAM) refers to solutions and practices for controlling, brokering and monitoring access to privileged accounts and administrative permissions.
A privileged access workstation (PAW) is a dedicated, hardened device used only for administrative tasks, so that sensitive administrator credentials are exposed on as few systems as possible.
Microsoft Entra service that replaces standing admin rights with eligible assignments that are activated just in time, with time limits, MFA, justification and optional approval.
Pro-code development is traditional software development by professional developers writing custom code, usually contrasted with low-code development on platforms such as Power Platform.
Process criticality describes how much damage a business process causes when it fails, slows down or produces wrong outcomes, typically assessed by frequency, dependency and consequence.

Process debt is the accumulated cost of unresolved process shortcuts, such as unclear decision rights, unretired exceptions and temporary fixes that became permanent, which automation can hide and scale.
A plant system (operational historian) that stores time-stamped process records from production equipment and is often an existing source for machine data.
In Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management, product dimensions (color, size, style, configuration and version) identify the specific variant of a product master.
Records that describe how input materials contribute to manufactured outputs through assembly, transformation, rework and component replacement.
Product information management keeps one central, shared product definition, including numbers, names, units, categories, attributes, images and translations, that other business processes use.
Engineering software and practice (PLM) that manages product design intent such as drawings, CAD models, material requirements, tolerances and approved revisions.
In Dynamics 365, a product master is the parent record for a product family that holds shared details and the rules from which individual product variants are created.
A product owner is the single accountable role that ranks the backlog, decides what gets built next and accepts delivered changes, a role known from Scrum and agile product development.
A manufacturing modeling structure that links the product to be built, the process required to build it and the resources such as machines, tools and people that can perform the work.

In manufacturing, a routing defines the sequence of operations a product passes through and the work centers or resources that can perform each operation, including approved alternate routes and their rules.
Productized services are consulting offerings standardized into named programs with a fixed scope, defined deliverables, a fixed timeline and a set price.
An industrial controller that runs the local machine sequence of production equipment, handling its steps and conditions in response to inputs.
Design pattern for AI agent skills in which only each skill's name and description stay in context, and the full instructions, scripts and resources load only when a request matches the skill.

A project management office is an organizational unit that sets standards, oversees projects and reports across them; an enterprise PMO provides a portfolio-wide view of all projects in an organization.

Project Online is Microsoft's SharePoint-based cloud project portfolio management service (Project Web App), which works with Project desktop and is being retired on September 30, 2026; Microsoft points customers to Planner, Project Server or Dynamics 365 Project Operations.

Project portfolio management is the discipline of managing projects, programs and portfolios together, including resources, finances, risks and strategic alignment. It provides an enterprise view above individual project schedules.

The Project schedule APIs in Dynamics 365 Project Operations perform create, update and delete operations on scheduling entities such as projects, tasks and resource assignments through the Project Scheduling Service, typically batched in operation sets; they are used, for example, for bulk project migrations.
Microsoft Project Server is Microsoft's on-premises enterprise project management server, the predecessor platform to Project Online. It offered enterprise features such as enterprise custom fields.

Projectum xPM is a project, portfolio and resource management solution from Context& built on the Microsoft Power Platform and Dataverse. It was formerly known as Power PPM and is positioned as a Project Online replacement.
A prompting technique in which the output of one AI prompt feeds the next, linking several steps into one workflow, for example across Excel, Word, Outlook and Teams with Microsoft 365 Copilot.
Prompt engineering is the practice of crafting and refining instructions to get better outputs from a generative AI model.

Protected health information (PHI) is information about an individual's health, medical care or payment for care that can be linked to that individual; in the US its use and disclosure are governed by HIPAA.
Global Active Directory security group designed to protect privileged accounts against credential theft; members cannot use NTLM, are limited in Kerberos delegation and get shorter ticket lifetimes.
Protocol Buffers (protobuf) is a language-neutral mechanism from Google for defining and serializing structured data, used as the interface definition language of gRPC.

Provision on demand is a Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync feature that lets administrators test the synchronization of a single selected user and see the resulting decisions before enabling broad synchronization.
Provisioned throughput units are the normalized unit used to reserve dedicated model processing capacity for Azure OpenAI deployments, as an alternative to pay-as-you-go token billing.

An open-source PowerShell module created by Reza Niroomand that brings the Dataverse Web API to PowerShell 7+, with piping, batching and parallelism for moving large amounts of data in and out of Power Platform.
De-identification technique that replaces personal identifiers with artificial ones while a key to re-identify still exists; under GDPR pseudonymized data remains personal data.
PSReadLine is a PowerShell module that customizes the command-line editing experience, including a searchable command history and suggestions based on previously run commands.

The public switched telephone network (PSTN) is the global infrastructure of interconnected public telephone networks; Teams voice connects to it through options such as Calling Plans or Direct Routing.
A shared belief in a team that people can speak up, ask questions, admit mistakes or challenge decisions without social penalty.
The system of roles, services and processes that creates, distributes, renews and revokes digital certificates based on public and private key pairs.
Publisher verification is a Microsoft Entra program that marks an application's publisher as verified, so consent policies can restrict user consent to apps from verified publishers.
A request to merge one branch into another that provides a place for reviewers to comment on and approve the change before it is merged.
A formal document from a buyer to a vendor stating the items or services, quantities, agreed prices, delivery dates and payment terms of a purchase.
An internal request to buy goods or services that states what is needed, how much and where, before any commitment is made to a vendor.
Technical layer of Microsoft Purview that scans connected data sources and stores metadata about data assets, which the Unified Catalog builds on.
A Microsoft Purview solution for investigating data security incidents such as data leaks, helping teams find where sensitive data is and what was exposed.
Business-facing data catalog in Microsoft Purview where people discover, understand and request access to data, organized by governance domains, data products and glossary terms.

desc.es: Lenguaje de programación muy usado en ciencia de datos, aprendizaje automático y análisis; en Microsoft Fabric se ejecuta en cuadernos.

desc.en: Q# is Microsoft's open-source, high-level programming language for writing quantum programs, included in the Quantum Development Kit and usable with Azure Quantum.

Hybrid quantum-classical algorithm for approximate solutions to combinatorial optimization problems: layers of a cost operator and a mixer are applied with tunable angles that a classical optimizer adjusts in a loop.
Qdrant is an open-source vector database and similarity search engine written in Rust, used to store embeddings with payload metadata for filtered semantic search and retrieval-augmented generation.

Containment is the set of defined steps that prevent suspect material from being used or shipped while a quality team establishes which material shares a problem; it can begin before the cause is known.
A system for managing quality investigations, non-conformance records and approval workflows, including product disposition decisions.
The Quantum Development Kit (QDK) is Microsoft's free, open-source toolkit for developing quantum programs, with a VS Code extension, local simulators and a direct connection to Azure Quantum.
A qubit is the basic unit of quantum information; unlike a classical bit it can be in a superposition of zero and one until it is measured.
Query diagnostics is a Power Query feature that records traces of query evaluations, showing where time is spent and which queries are sent to the data source.

Power Query optimization that pushes supported transformation steps back to the data source, such as a database, instead of evaluating them in the Power Query engine. Flat files like CSV and Excel cannot fold.
A customizable toolbar in Office apps such as PowerPoint, Word, Excel and classic Outlook where users pin frequently used commands.
Quiet hours (quiet time) are scheduled periods in which Microsoft Teams and Outlook mobile apps silence notifications, so work alerts do not reach users outside working time.
R is a free, open-source programming language and environment for statistical computing and graphics. In SQL Server it can run in-database through Machine Learning Services.
A RACI matrix is a responsibility assignment chart that defines for each task or decision who is Responsible, Accountable, Consulted and Informed.
A Ralph loop (Ralph Wiggum technique) repeatedly re-runs an AI coding agent on the same goal until a completion criterion is met, so agents keep working instead of stopping early.
Ransomware is malware that encrypts or locks an organization's data and demands payment; attackers typically also try to delete backups to prevent recovery.
Technique that limits how many requests a client can make to an API or service within a given time period, protecting backends from overload and abuse.
An agent reasoning pattern that alternates between reasoning about what is needed and acting, for example retrieving data or calling a tool, until the model decides it has enough to answer.
React is an open-source JavaScript library for building user interfaces from components; PCF offers a React-based template that uses the React runtime already loaded by the platform.
An asynchronously updated copy of a primary database that serves read queries and can support failover, billed as a separate server.

A rank-merging method used in hybrid search that combines result lists from several retrievers, such as BM25 keyword search and vector search, by summing reciprocal rank scores so that documents ranked well by multiple methods rise to the top.

name: Recovery time objective (RTO) and recovery point objective (RPO)

desc.en: RTO defines how fast a system must be back online after a failure, and RPO defines how much data loss is acceptable; both are business requirements that drive resilient design.

Database rule that every reference to another record must point to a record that exists, so links between tables cannot break; Dataverse enforces it for lookup relationships while SharePoint lookup columns do not.

Software testing practice of re-running tests after changes to confirm that previously working functionality still behaves correctly; in this episode, AI agents expand the regression suite with tests generated from observed failures.

Regular expressions (regex) are character sequences that specify text match patterns; in data classification they are used for fast, pattern-based detection of structured sensitive data such as ID numbers.
Ready-made blueprints in Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager containing the controls and improvement actions for a regulation, standard or certification, used to create assessments.
A cloud migration path in which an existing server or application is moved to Azure with few changes, typically running on a virtual machine instead of on-premises hardware.

Relationship analytics in Dynamics 365 Sales shows communication activity and a relationship health score for contacts, accounts, leads and opportunities to highlight relationships that need attention.
Relationship intelligence is a Dynamics 365 Sales feature set, made up of relationship analytics and who knows whom, that turns customer communication into relationship signals.
In Dynamics 365, a released product is a shared product definition that has been approved for use in a specific legal entity, which then adds its own local settings.
Remaining useful life is an estimate of how long a component can continue to meet its required function under assumed future operating conditions, ideally stated with its uncertainty.
Microsoft's proprietary protocol for connecting to the graphical desktop of a remote computer, listening on port 3389 by default; open RDP ports on the internet are a frequent attack target.
The XML-based file format that defines paginated reports in SQL Server Reporting Services and Power BI.
A single-click data exfiltration attack on Microsoft Copilot disclosed by Varonis that injected prompts through a URL parameter and chained follow-up instructions to leak data over multiple turns.

name: Request for information (Copilot Studio agent flows)

desc.en: A human review action in Copilot Studio agent flows that pauses the flow and asks a person to supply missing or critical data through a form, such as an Outlook actionable message, before execution continues.
A request sent to several vendors to bid on the same requirement, so the buyer can compare prices, delivery dates and terms before choosing a supplier.
Reranking is a retrieval step in which a second model rescores the top candidates returned by a search so the most relevant results are passed on, for example to a language model in a RAG pipeline.

Any change to infrastructure managed by Terraform that Terraform did not make, so that the real environment no longer matches the configuration and state. It is detected with a plan or a refresh-only plan.
The Responsible AI dashboard in Azure Machine Learning brings together tools such as model explanations and error analysis to help assess and debug models for responsible AI.

desc.nl: Principes en praktijken voor eerlijke, transparante, veilige en verantwoordelijke AI; bij Microsoft vastgelegd in de Responsible AI Standard en ondersteund door tools zoals het Responsible AI-dashboard.

desc.en: A REST API is a web interface through which one program requests data or actions from another using an address (URL), an HTTP verb, headers and a response with a status code. The term REST comes from Roy Fielding's 2000 dissertation.
SharePoint Advanced Management site-level control that limits access to a SharePoint site and its content to members of specified groups, regardless of existing sharing links.
SharePoint Advanced Management site-level control that keeps a site's content out of organization-wide search and Microsoft 365 Copilot results without changing who can access it.

desc.it: Impostazione di SharePoint che limita la ricerca a livello di organizzazione e Copilot a un elenco selezionato di siti, per ridurre l'esposizione di contenuti condivisi in eccesso.

desc.en: Microsoft Purview labels applied to individual items such as documents or emails that define when retention starts, how long the item is kept and what happens at the end of the period.
Microsoft Purview policies that keep or delete content such as Teams channel messages, chats and site files for a defined period, independently of what users delete.
A resilience pattern in which a failed call to a remote dependency is automatically attempted again, ideally bounded and with jitter, to recover from brief transient faults.

Return on security investment (ROSI) compares the reduction in expected loss achieved by security controls with their cost, calculated as exposure before minus exposure after minus security cost, divided by security cost.

RevoScaleR is a Microsoft R package with rx-prefixed functions for importing, transforming and analyzing data at scale. It is used in SQL Server Machine Learning Services to set compute contexts and define SQL Server data sources.
A software delivery metric that measures what share of recently written code is rewritten, deleted or rolled back shortly afterwards, used as a signal of code durability.
Rightsizing is the cost-optimization practice of matching provisioned cloud resources or license tiers to measured actual usage, for example moving underutilized virtual machines to smaller sizes.

A safe deployment practice that releases a change to successive cohorts (rings) of users or environments, from an internal team to pilot users to broad production, with validation and exit criteria before each expansion.
A risk register is a record used in risk management to track identified risks along with their likelihood, impact and status. It is a core input for governance, risk and compliance (GRC) reporting.
Security company known for internet-scale threat intelligence and attack surface data, acquired by Microsoft in 2021; its technology underpins Microsoft Defender Threat Intelligence.

desc.pl: Model kontroli dostępu oparty na rolach, który decyduje, jaki poziom dostępu ma dana tożsamość; w Microsoft 365 wyznacza też, jakie dane może pokazać Copilot.

desc.en: ROT data is content that is redundant, obsolete or trivial; outdated documents of this kind can muddy the answers of AI tools that are grounded on company content.
A unified routing feature in Dynamics 365 Customer Service that records the intake, classification and assignment stages of each work item so administrators can see why it was routed where it went.
Row-level security filters which rows of a semantic model or warehouse table each user can see, based on roles and filter rules.
In Azure Automation, a runbook is a script, usually PowerShell or Python or a graphical workflow, that the service runs on demand, on a schedule, from an alert or via a webhook.

The SaaS fulfillment APIs are Microsoft commercial marketplace APIs that publishers integrate to manage the subscription lifecycle of transactable SaaS offers, such as activation, plan changes and cancellation.
A Microsoft Defender for Office 365 feature that opens email attachments in an isolated sandbox and judges them by behaviour before or while delivering them.
A Microsoft Defender for Office 365 feature that rewrites URLs and checks them at the moment of click in email, Microsoft Teams and Office apps.
A pattern for distributed transactions that splits a process into local steps across systems, each with a compensating action that undoes earlier steps if a later step fails.
An attack or fraud technique that achieves a large effect through many small, individually inconspicuous steps, such as transfers that drain accounts one tiny piece at a time.
Sales forecasting in Dynamics 365 Sales projects expected revenue from open opportunities, using fields such as estimated revenue, close date and forecast category.
A lead in Dynamics 365 Sales stores an early signal of interest from a person or company; once qualified, it is closed and an opportunity is created from it.

An opportunity in Dynamics 365 Sales is a record for a potential sale linked to a customer account or contact, holding estimated revenue, close date, probability, products and activities until it is closed as won or lost.
Sales Order Agent is a Microsoft-built AI agent in Dynamics 365 Business Central that reads customer order emails, checks stock and creates draft sales quotes or orders for human review and approval.
The Sales Qualification Agent is an AI agent in Dynamics 365 Sales that autonomously researches leads and prepares qualification information for sellers.
Cloud software company known for its customer relationship management (CRM) platform.
An older XML-based federation standard widely used for corporate single sign-on, in which an identity provider sends signed assertions about a user to an app.

Sandboxing is a security mechanism that runs programs in an isolated environment with restricted access so failures or compromised code cannot spread; the episode applies it to OS-level isolation of AI agents.
SAP ERP Central Component, the predecessor ERP system to SAP S/4HANA, whose mainstream maintenance ends in 2027.
SAP's role-based, tile-oriented user experience for SAP applications, first used with SAP S/4HANA and replacing the transaction-code-driven SAP GUI for many tasks.
SAP HANA is SAP's in-memory database; it keeps its data in RAM but still needs very fast storage for logs, backups and snapshots.
SAP's ERP suite released in 2015 as the successor to SAP ECC, running only on the in-memory SAP HANA database.
SAP SuccessFactors is SAP's cloud-based human capital management software suite, delivered as software as a service and offering country-specific localization for global HR processes.
SAP is a German enterprise software company best known for its ERP systems. In the episode it is cited as a typical ERP source whose data is unified with CRM data through Fabric connectors.
Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition systems collect controller values for supervision of industrial processes and often already hold data paths to production equipment.
A game in which individuals or teams search for and collect items from a list; used in the episode as a first, low-effort Minecraft team challenge.

The schedule board in Dynamics 365 Field Service is a live planning board where dispatchers see resources, time slots, unassigned work orders and map views, and assign bookings to the right technician.

Schema drift occurs when the structure of source data changes, for example when columns are added, removed, reordered or change data type, which can break data pipelines and dataflows that are not designed to handle it.
Greenhouse gas accounting categories: Scope 1 covers direct emissions from sources an organization owns or controls, Scope 2 the energy it buys, and Scope 3 all other emissions in its value chain.
The continuous or uncontrolled growth of a project's scope after it has started, for example adding new metrics, data sets or features without formal change control.
The practice of improving content, such as a website or marketplace listing, so that it ranks higher and is found more often in organic search engine results.
SEC Rule 17a-4 is a US Securities and Exchange Commission regulation under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 that sets record retention and accessibility requirements for broker-dealers.
Secrets management is the practice of storing API keys, passwords, tokens and connection strings centrally with controlled, logged access instead of hardcoding them in scripts or configuration files.
Secure by design is the principle of treating security as part of a system's initial design rather than an afterthought, so that security gaps are identified before an application is built.

Secure key release (SKR) is a capability of Azure Key Vault Premium and Managed HSM that releases an HSM-protected key only to a trusted execution environment whose attestation claims satisfy a release policy defined by the customer.

Preconfigured groups of recommended security settings for products such as Windows, Microsoft Edge or Microsoft 365, which can be deployed through Microsoft Intune to harden devices including Cloud PCs and session hosts.

Security Compute Units are the provisioned capacity units consumed by Microsoft Security Copilot when prompts, agents and reports run; Microsoft 365 E5 includes a monthly allotment and extra units can be purchased.

A single setting in Microsoft Entra ID that enables baseline identity protections such as MFA for all users and admins and blocking legacy authentication; the episode recommends it for small businesses not using Conditional Access.

A category of security tools that collects logs from many systems such as servers, firewalls, applications and identity systems and correlates them to detect attacks that single log entries would not reveal.

desc.ja: セキュリティ運用センター（SOC）。組織のセキュリティ イベントやアラートを監視・調査・対応するチームおよび機能。

desc.en: Security tooling that automatically responds to detected threats, for example by disabling accounts or revoking sessions, typically through automated workflows called playbooks.

Security service edge (SSE) is a cloud-delivered security model that moves access checks for web, cloud services and private applications from a central network into the cloud, typically combining secure web gateway and Zero Trust Network Access capabilities.

Security trimming filters search or retrieval results so that each user only receives documents they are permitted to access, typically by storing user and group identifiers with indexed content and filtering on them at query time.
Seedance is ByteDance's AI video generation model family; Seedance 2.0 accepts text, image, video and audio references and is used for character-consistent, multi-shot video generation.
Internal control principle that requires more than one person or role to complete sensitive tasks, so that the same actor cannot both request and approve an action.
A pane in PowerPoint and other Office apps that lists all objects on a slide, letting users select, rename, reorder, group, show or hide them, including objects hidden behind others.
An architecture pattern in which a system defines a desired state, detects drift from it, decides what the drift means and remediates it automatically, instead of relying on manual reviews.

Self-service business intelligence is an approach in which business users build their own reports, dashboards and data models instead of relying on a central BI team; without governance it can lead to duplicated content and rising costs.

Self-service password reset in Microsoft Entra ID lets users change or reset their own password without administrator or help desk involvement. Attackers have abused password reset flows to flood users with reset requests.

A customer-facing self-service site where customers search approved knowledge articles to solve simple issues, such as updating contact details or finding an invoice, without opening a support request.

Semantic caching returns a stored LLM response for prompts that are similar in meaning to an earlier prompt, avoiding a new model call. Azure API Management offers semantic cache lookup and store policies for Azure OpenAI APIs.
Semantic drift is the gradual divergence of business definitions such as metrics, measures and entity meanings across copied or forked data models, while names, schemas and security stay unchanged.

desc.he: שכבת אינדקס סמנטי ב-Microsoft 365 שמדרגת תוכן לפי רלוונטיות והקשר מעבר להתאמת מילות מפתח, ומבססת את התשובות של Microsoft 365 Copilot על נתוני Microsoft Graph שלמשתמש יש הרשאה אליהם.

desc.en: Microsoft's free, open-source (MIT) development kit for C#, Python and Java that connects application code to AI models through a kernel, plugins, function calling, memory and connectors.
A shared business layer that defines what terms, measures and records mean and how they relate, so reports, people and AI tools use the same definitions.

Semantic link is a Microsoft Fabric feature that connects Power BI semantic models to data science workloads; its Python library SemPy lets notebooks read tables, evaluate measures and run DAX queries.

Pattern-based detectors in Microsoft Purview that recognize data such as credit card or passport numbers using patterns, keywords, checksums, proximity and confidence levels. Built-in and custom types serve as conditions in DLP policies.
