Sentiment analysis estimates whether a conversation appears positive, neutral or negative; in customer service it gives agents a signal to listen more carefully, not a verdict.

An internal control principle, also called segregation of duties (SoD), that requires more than one person or identity to complete a sensitive task so that no single actor can both perform and approve it.
SMB is the standard Windows network file sharing protocol; Azure Files supports it, and SMB 3.0 and higher encrypt data in transit.

A cloud execution model in which the provider runs and scales the servers while you supply only code or workflows that run in response to events. You pay for executions and resources used rather than for idle machines.

A service account is a shared non-human account used to run automation under one set of credentials; for AI agents it lacks per-agent attribution, ownership, lifecycle and policy enforcement, which is why dedicated agent identities are recommended instead.
A central record of the software services a company runs, showing for each service its owner, documentation, dependencies, status and support links.
A provider's written uptime commitment for a service; in Azure, missing the SLA results in service credits rather than restored availability.
An infrastructure layer, often based on sidecar proxies such as Istio or Linkerd, that manages service-to-service traffic, mTLS and policy enforcement in distributed applications.
The identity an application uses to sign in within a Microsoft Entra tenant. Agent identities are built as a special kind of service principal.
Software company whose cloud platform is widely used for IT service management and ticketing.
A network element at the edge of a SIP-based voice network that translates signaling, handles media and protects the voice path; Teams Direct Routing requires a certified SBC.
AI tools and agents that employees install or sign up for on their own, running outside the view and control of the IT team.

Automation that runs without explicit ownership or oversight, for example flows on personal connections that outlive their purpose; unlike shadow IT it executes actions such as moving data or changing records.

Shadow data is any unknown, hidden or overlooked copy of sensitive information that exists outside an organization's IT security and governance frameworks, for example in forgotten storage accounts, personal drives or AI training data sets.
IT systems, services or tenants created by departments or employees without the knowledge or administration of central IT.
A cryptographic, time-limited token derived from a secret tied to an identity, used for example by devices to authenticate to Azure IoT Hub.
Microsoft Teams channels that can include people from outside the team or tenant, for example through B2B direct connect, with their own SharePoint site and membership.
A mailbox in Exchange Online that multiple users can access and send from, used here as the consistent sender identity for an internal newsletter.

The shared responsibility model describes how security duties are split between a cloud provider and its customer; in SaaS the provider runs the platform while the customer keeps responsibility for its data, identities, devices and access.
Software vendor of Microsoft 365 migration, consolidation and governance tools.
SharePoint 2013 workflows are the legacy workflow engine for SharePoint; Microsoft is retiring them in SharePoint Online and recommends Power Automate as the replacement.
Copilot agents grounded on a specific SharePoint site or document library that answer questions about that selected content.

Autofill columns are a pay-as-you-go SharePoint feature (part of Microsoft Syntex / SharePoint Premium document processing) that uses natural-language prompts to extract or generate metadata from files and populate library columns automatically.
Reusable SharePoint definitions that bundle site columns and settings for a category of documents or items, such as a policy or contract, so metadata stays consistent across libraries and sites.
A legacy Microsoft desktop application for customizing SharePoint sites and building SharePoint workflows.
Document libraries are the SharePoint containers for storing, organizing and co-editing files, with columns for metadata, custom views and permissions at library, folder or file level.
Microsoft's client-side development model for extending SharePoint and Microsoft 365 with web parts, extensions and form customizers, typically built with React and TypeScript.
Global navigation is the tenant-wide navigation layer in SharePoint, shown in the SharePoint app bar once a home site is set, that gives users consistent top-level links across all sites.
A SharePoint site set as the organization's home site; it is the foundation from which Viva Connections pulls its news, dashboard and resources.
SharePoint feature that groups related sites into a flat cluster with shared navigation, branding and search scope; associating a site with a hub does not change its permissions.

desc.pt: Agente com IA no SharePoint (SharePoint Premium, Microsoft 365 Copilot) que sugere colunas de metadados, cria regras em linguagem natural, monta visualizações e responde perguntas sobre o conteúdo das bibliotecas.

desc.en: The SharePoint limit, 5,000 items by default, on how many list items a single database operation such as a view query can process at once; it does not cap how many items a list can store.

Managed metadata in SharePoint lets organizations define centrally managed term sets in the term store and use them in managed metadata columns across sites, giving consistent vocabularies for tagging, navigation and search.

Quick steps are custom commands for a SharePoint or Microsoft Lists list or library that appear in the command bar and run an action, such as moving a file or setting a status, on the selected item in one click.

Links created with the Share option in SharePoint and OneDrive that grant access to a file or folder, with scopes such as anyone, people in the organization, people with existing access or specific people.

The governed process of creating SharePoint sites and Teams workspaces through a request and approval step and standard templates, so that ownership, naming, sensitivity and lifecycle settings are applied from the start.
Subsites are SharePoint sites nested beneath a parent site; modern SharePoint guidance favors flat, standalone sites connected through hub sites instead of deep subsite hierarchies.
A FinOps practice of showing teams the costs attributed to them without transferring the amount out of their budgets, building cost awareness before any chargeback.
Shure is an audio equipment manufacturer known for microphones; it also builds conferencing audio such as the MXA ceiling microphones and IntelliMix room kits certified for Microsoft Teams Rooms.
SID filtering on Active Directory trusts strips SID history and foreign security identifiers from authentication data crossing the trust, preventing privilege escalation across forests.
Sign-in frequency is a Conditional Access session control in Microsoft Entra ID that defines how long a user can access a resource before being asked to sign in again.
A protocol that managed devices use to request certificates from a certificate authority; Intune and Microsoft Cloud PKI use it to deliver device certificates.
A single point of failure is a part of a system whose failure stops the entire system from working; in organizations it can be one person or approval path that all decisions depend on.
An authentication approach where a user signs in once with one set of credentials at a trusted identity provider and can then open every app they are allowed to use without signing in again.

The principle that each piece of business information has one authoritative source; the episode frames it less as one storage location and more as one trusted decision reality that defines which source governs which decision.

A SharePoint Advanced Management feature that lets administrators delegate the review of overshared sites, found in data access governance reports, to the site owners, who confirm who should keep access.

Skype for Business was Microsoft's enterprise unified communications product for instant messaging, presence, calling and meetings, offered as an on-premises server and as Skype for Business Online; Microsoft Teams replaced it.

The part of a PowerPoint theme that holds the slide layouts, colors and fonts of a presentation; a well-built slide master is the basis of a corporate template and of good Copilot and Designer results.
A small language model is a compact AI language model with far fewer parameters than a large language model, so it needs less compute and can be focused on a narrow domain or run on local devices.

A Microsoft 365 feature in PowerPoint, Word, Excel and Outlook for creating diagrams such as lists, timelines and hierarchies from text; text can be converted to SmartArt and SmartArt back to text or shapes.
SMB signing adds a cryptographic signature to Server Message Block traffic so that relayed or tampered messages are rejected.

A snowflake schema is a dimensional data model in which dimension tables are normalized into further related tables (for example product category and subcategory) instead of connecting directly to the fact table as in a star schema.
SOAP is an earlier, XML-based protocol for building web services that was largely displaced by simpler REST-style APIs over plain HTTP.

SOC 2 is a System and Organization Controls audit report based on the AICPA Trust Services Criteria, commonly requested by enterprise customers to evaluate the security controls of service and SaaS providers.
Social capital is the value created by networks of relationships, trust and shared norms that let people cooperate and make decisions efficiently.
An event-driven JavaScript library for real-time, two-way communication between web clients and servers, mainly over WebSockets with polling as a fallback.
Interpersonal and social skills such as communication, collaboration, learning and leadership that complement technical hard skills in any profession.
Software as a service is a cloud delivery model in which a vendor hosts and runs an application and customers use it on a subscription basis, traditionally priced per user seat.
Microsoft Software Assurance is a program sold with volume licensing agreements that gives organizations rights to newer software versions and additional benefits for on-premises products.
A software bill of materials (SBOM) is a machine-readable inventory of the components and dependencies that make up a piece of software.
The gradual increase of disorder, complexity and unpredictability in software systems as undocumented changes, exceptions and dependencies accumulate over time without active maintenance.
A software design principle of building systems so that new functionality can be added or parts swapped later through plug-ins, hooks and abstractions without rewriting the core.
Software supply chain security protects applications against risks introduced through third-party packages, transitive dependencies, build pipelines and deployment artifacts.

Relationships in which one Power Platform or Dynamics 365 solution component, such as a flow, form or business rule, relies on another component like a table or field. Missing dependencies are a common cause of failed solution imports into another environment.

The component-level stacking of definitions in Dataverse, with a system layer at the bottom, managed solution layers above it and a single unmanaged layer; the top layer usually determines runtime behavior.
The owner label of a Power Platform solution; it controls which components other publishers may change and defines the prefix added to the names of custom tables and columns.

Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program designation per solution area, such as Modern Work, Security or Data & AI, earned by reaching the required Partner Capability Score; it replaced the former Silver and Gold competencies.

In hybrid identity, the source of authority is the directory that has final say over an object's identity attributes. Microsoft Entra ID can take over the source of authority for synced groups and users from on-premises Active Directory.
sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint is a system stored procedure in Azure SQL Database and SQL Server 2025 that lets the database call external HTTP REST endpoints directly from T-SQL.

A specification that adds industrial conventions on top of MQTT, defining a topic structure, a typed binary payload based on protocol buffers, and birth and death messages for edge node lifecycle state.
Spatial audio renders voices according to where speakers are positioned in a virtual space, so nearby people sound louder and distant ones quieter, enabling natural side conversations in 3D meetings.

Spec-driven development is an approach in which work starts from a written specification of the intended feature, which is then turned into a code scaffold and refined; AI coding agents can generate that scaffold from a plain-language spec.

GitHub's open-source toolkit for spec-driven development with AI coding agents, built around a constitution, specifications, plans and tasks. In the episode it is used as the enforcement layer that binds architectural intent to executable rules.
An email authentication record in DNS that lists the servers allowed to send mail for a domain.

Software for searching, monitoring and analyzing machine-generated data, used for log aggregation and SIEM; in the episode a security operations stack is consolidated from Splunk into Microsoft Sentinel.

A pejorative term for a spreadsheet- or desktop-based reporting setup that individuals or teams build on their own instead of a governed data mart or warehouse. In BI it stands for duplicated datasets and inconsistent metric logic.

A read-only T-SQL surface over Delta tables that Microsoft Fabric provisions for items such as lakehouses; in the episode, using it as the default path for every workload is a major driver of capacity unit consumption.
A transactional SQL database that runs inside Microsoft Fabric on the same engine as Azure SQL Database. Its data is automatically mirrored into OneLake for analytics.
SQL injection is a code injection attack in which malicious SQL statements are inserted into an application's input fields; it is one of the most common attacks that web application firewalls block.

A JOIN clause in SQL combines columns from two or more tables based on a related column; common variants include inner joins, which return only matching rows, and left joins, which keep every row of the left table.
SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) is Microsoft's free integrated environment for managing SQL Server and Azure SQL databases, including writing queries and inspecting execution plans.
Microsoft's server-based report generation platform for paginated reports defined in RDL, authored for example with Reporting Services projects in Visual Studio.
Microsoft's relational database management system that uses T-SQL. Its engine also underpins Azure SQL Database and Azure SQL Managed Instance.
Structured Query Language, the standard domain-specific language for querying and managing data in relational database systems.
SQLBI is a Business Intelligence training and consulting company founded by Marco Russo and Alberto Ferrari, known for its DAX and data modeling content and books.
German aluminium extrusion manufacturer and part of the ST Extruded Products Group (STEP-G), cited in the episode as a multi-year Microsoft 365 adoption and intranet case.

desc.pt: Modelo de IA generativa de difusão para criar imagens a partir de texto.

desc.en: Standard channels are the default Microsoft Teams channel type that all members of the parent team can see and access; their files are stored in the team's SharePoint site.
Permissions, especially administrative rights, that are permanently active even when they are not being used, which enlarges the attack surface if an account is compromised.
Static code analysis examines source code without running it to find bugs and security issues, often automatically on every commit in a CI/CD pipeline.
Store Commerce is the point-of-sale app of Dynamics 365 Commerce for in-store staff, running on Windows, iOS, Android and macOS across desktop, tablet and phone form factors.
A modernization pattern in which a facade routes requests between a legacy system and its replacement, so functionality can be moved over piece by piece until the old system can be retired.
A behavioral software design pattern that encapsulates interchangeable algorithms behind a common interface so one implementation can be swapped for another at runtime.

Streamable HTTP is the remote transport of the Model Context Protocol that uses standard HTTP POST and GET requests, with optional server-sent events for streaming. It replaced the earlier HTTP+SSE transport.

A part of Dynamics 365 Finance that tracks the detail of a specific kind of activity, such as accounts payable, accounts receivable, inventory, fixed assets or tax, and feeds accounting entries into the general ledger.
A 32-bit value that marks which part of an IPv4 address identifies the network and which part identifies the host; its number of one bits is written as the slash prefix length.
The practice of dividing a larger IP address block into smaller logical networks (subnets) to reduce noise, separate devices and keep address management manageable.

Subscription vending is an Azure landing zone pattern that automates the creation of new Azure subscriptions, placing them in the right management group with policies, access and logging preconfigured, typically through infrastructure as code such as Bicep.

Suggestion acceptance rate measures how often AI outputs such as Copilot drafts or summaries are used without heavy rewriting or rejection, serving as a signal of trust, context quality and workflow fit.
Sulava is a Finnish consultancy working on modern work, AI and Microsoft 365.

The supervisor-worker pattern is a multi-agent architecture in which one supervisor agent owns the overall goal, breaks it into tasks for specialised worker agents and makes the final decision, keeping accountability in one place.

name: Supplier Communications Agent (Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management)

desc.en: The Supplier Communications Agent is an AI agent in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management that automates routine procurement communication with vendors about purchase order changes.
A surrogate key is a system-generated unique identifier, often a sequential number, that is not derived from business data and is used to relate tables such as fact and dimension tables.
Sysmon (System Monitor) is a Windows Sysinternals service that logs detailed process, network, file and handle activity to the Windows event log for security monitoring.

A system of record is the authoritative information storage system for a given data element or business process, for example an ERP or HR system that holds the governed, auditable version of the data.
A system prompt is the set of instructions given to a language model up front that defines how it should behave, for example to answer only from provided context and cite sources.

Systems engineering is an interdisciplinary approach to designing and managing complex systems as a whole, including planning for component failure through redundancy, monitoring and fallback procedures.
Systems thinking is a way of analysing problems by looking at flows, dependencies, incentives and feedback across a whole system instead of isolated events or individuals.
T-shaped skills describe professionals who combine broad knowledge across many topics with deep expertise in one or a few specialist areas.
Tabular Editor is a tool for building, managing and scripting tabular semantic models for Power BI, Microsoft Fabric and Analysis Services, including C# script automation.

In information architecture, a taxonomy is a governed, standardized classification scheme of business terms (for example regions, products or departments) used to tag content consistently, such as through a SharePoint term store.
A collective term for interventions that aim to improve team effectiveness and clarify roles, often through collaborative tasks.

Team Topologies is an organizational design model by Matthew Skelton and Manuel Pais with four team types (stream-aligned, platform, enabling and complicated-subsystem) and three interaction modes, designed around team cognitive load.
The admin portal for Microsoft Teams, used for usage reports, team templates and Teams policies.
JSON file that describes a Microsoft Teams app and tells the Teams client how and where to surface it, for example which URL a tab loads.
A Teams Phone feature that acts as a virtual receptionist, greeting callers and routing them to the right person or call queue based on menu choices, time of day or holidays.
Call queues in Microsoft Teams route incoming callers to groups of people in an organization who can help with a particular issue or question, sharing the incoming call volume.
Microsoft's PSTN offering for Teams Phone in which Microsoft acts as the carrier, supplying numbers and per-user minute bundles in a limited set of countries.

Certified for Microsoft Teams is Microsoft's certification program for headsets, cameras, phones, displays and Teams Rooms systems that pass Microsoft's requirements and quality testing; certified devices are the supported option for Teams meetings and calls.
Channels are the topic- or workflow-based spaces inside a Microsoft Teams team where members post conversations, share files and add tabs and apps.
Microsoft's tool (formerly App Studio) for configuring, distributing and managing Microsoft Teams apps, including editing the app manifest.

Custom Microsoft Teams apps that run inside a meeting, for example as an in-meeting side panel, a meeting tab or on the shared meeting stage. They use the meeting context, the app manifest and Teams single sign-on to surface data and actions next to the conversation.

Event notifications that Microsoft Graph sends for Teams online meetings, such as call started, call ended and participant join or leave. Services subscribe to them via change notifications (webhooks) to trigger automation at key moments of a meeting.
The Microsoft Teams feature that creates a live, speaker-attributed transcript of a meeting; Microsoft 365 Copilot in Teams relies on it to produce meeting summaries and action items.
Teams app capability that lets users query or act on an external web service from the compose area and insert the results, usually as cards, into a conversation.
A Microsoft Teams app surface that loads a web page for a single user, typically an existing web app embedded in the Teams client.
Predefined or custom Microsoft Teams structures with channels, tabs, apps and settings, managed in the Teams admin center, from which new teams can be created.
Microsoft SDK for building custom Microsoft Teams apps that has been deprecated; existing TeamsFx solutions need to be migrated, for example to SPFx or Power Apps as discussed in the episode.
A metric that expresses the cost to fix existing technical debt as a percentage of the total investment; in the episode it is applied to automation portfolios such as Power Automate flows.
Technical debt is the future cost of rework caused by choosing quick or ungoverned solutions instead of sound, maintainable ones.
A time-ordered record of repeated measurements sent by devices, such as machine sensor readings, whose meaning comes from the sequence rather than any single value.
Short-lived, time-limited passcode in Microsoft Entra that lets a user sign in for the first time and register passwordless methods such as the Authenticator app or a security key.

Tenant restrictions in Microsoft Entra prevent users from signing in to other, external Microsoft 365 or Entra tenants with corporate devices or networks, reducing the risk of data exfiltration; universal tenant restrictions enforce this through Global Secure Access.

desc.pt: SDK da NVIDIA para otimizar e executar inferência de deep learning de alto desempenho em GPUs.

desc.en: A plugin that teaches Terraform how to talk to a single platform through its API, such as Azure, AWS or GitHub. Providers are distributed separately from Terraform and listed in the Terraform Registry.

The record Terraform keeps of the infrastructure it manages, mapping resources in the configuration to real remote objects. Terraform uses it to decide which changes to make; it can contain sensitive values and is best kept in a remote, locked and access-controlled backend.
A thin client is a simple computer optimized for connecting to a desktop or computing environment that runs remotely on a server or in the cloud.
A person or group carrying out cyberattacks; Microsoft tracks threat actors in profiles and names them by weather-themed families, using temporary Storm labels for groups still in development.

Threat analytics is the threat intelligence capability in Microsoft Defender XDR that provides reports by Microsoft security researchers on active threat actors, campaigns and attack techniques, including organization-specific exposure and recommended mitigations.
A Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 tool for searching email detections, delivery actions and campaigns across a tenant.
Threat hunting is the proactive search through security data for threats and suspicious activity that automated detections have not flagged, for example with queries in Microsoft Defender XDR.

Continuously updated information about known malicious IP addresses, domains and attack patterns that security tools use to alert on or block threats; Azure Firewall can filter traffic based on Microsoft threat intelligence.

Threat modeling is a structured security exercise in which developers and security experts review an application's design to identify what can go wrong and where security gaps are, ideally early in development.
An accounts payable control that compares the purchase order, the product receipt and the vendor invoice before an invoice is paid.

desc.uk: Обмеження кількості запитів, яке Microsoft Graph застосовує до застосунків, що надсилають забагато викликів, наприклад через надто часте опитування.

desc.en: The Time Entry agent, part of the Time and Expense Agent in Dynamics 365 Project Operations, drafts weekly time entries from resource assignments and Outlook calendar data, reminds users in Microsoft Teams to submit them and can support approvals.
Time to decision is a metric that measures how long it takes from an identified issue to a committed action, used to show whether decision authority is flowing or pooling in a specific workflow.
A latency metric for generative AI systems that measures the time between a user submitting a request and the first token of the answer appearing.
TLS inspection lets an organization decrypt and inspect selected encrypted web traffic under its policy so that content-based checks such as file filtering can be applied.

Ending the encrypted TLS connection at a proxy or load balancer such as a gateway, so back-end servers receive plain requests and certificates are managed in one place; also called TLS or SSL offloading.

TMDL is a human-readable, text-based syntax for defining tabular semantic models, including tables, measures and relationships, and can be used to store Power BI semantic models as a folder of text files.
Toil is repetitive, manual operational work, such as recurring alert triage or log analysis, that creates no lasting value and that site reliability and DevOps teams aim to reduce through automation.
Token protection is a Microsoft Entra Conditional Access session control that binds sign-in session tokens to the device they were issued to, reducing token theft and replay attacks.

Token theft is an attack in which an adversary steals and replays a user's session or access token, for example after adversary-in-the-middle phishing, to act as the user without needing the password or passing MFA again.

Standardized, versioned definition of an action an AI agent may call, specifying allowed inputs, structured outputs, executing identity, provenance logging and approval gates for irreversible steps, similar to an API contract.
Total cost of ownership (TCO) is the full cost of a system over its lifetime, including operations, maintenance, staffing and infrastructure, not only the initial purchase or migration cost.
The ability to follow the recorded history of material and products through receipt, production and delivery, for example to support recall and containment decisions in manufacturing.

Machine-learning classifiers in Microsoft Purview that learn to recognize a kind of document, such as contracts or source code, from example documents, and can be used as conditions in DLP and labeling policies.
Transact-SQL (T-SQL) is Microsoft's extension of SQL used by Microsoft SQL Server and related SQL products and services.

An integration pattern in which a change to a record and a matching entry in a dedicated outbox table are written in the same transaction, so a downstream service can reliably pick up and process every event.
The triple peak workday is a pattern described in Microsoft research in which knowledge work activity peaks not only in the morning and afternoon but again in the late evening.
Troy Hunt is an Australian security researcher best known as the creator of the data breach notification service Have I Been Pwned.
Truesec is a cybersecurity company providing services such as penetration testing, incident response and proactive security.
A source-control practice in which developers commit small changes to one shared branch, the trunk, at least daily, with branches living for hours rather than weeks.
A security chip on a device's motherboard; Windows Autopilot pre-provisioning and self-deploying modes require TPM attestation to prove the device's identity.
A programming language from Microsoft that builds on JavaScript with static types to catch mistakes early; it is used to write Power Apps code components.

A desktop flow run mode in which the bot signs in to a free machine without a user present; it requires a paid unattended license and cannot run while any user session is open or with elevated rights.

Unconstrained delegation is an Active Directory Kerberos setting that lets a service cache users' TGTs and request tickets to any service on their behalf, which attackers can abuse if the host is compromised.

A unified customer profile combines matched and de-duplicated records about the same person from several source systems into one profile, sometimes called a golden record, while keeping track of where each detail came from.

An architecture pattern providing a governed, shared event space, typically on an MQTT broker, where machine data and other current factory events are published once and consumed by any approved system.

Unified routing in Dynamics 365 Customer Service and Contact Center sends incoming cases and conversations to the most suitable queue or service representative based on rules, skills, presence and capacity, using push or pick assignment.
Set of Microsoft Graph APIs, introduced in preview in 2026, for taking baseline snapshots of Microsoft 365 tenant configuration and monitoring the live tenant for configuration drift.
Measuring costs (and value) per unit of work rather than in aggregate; in this episode applied to AI as cost per decision, cost per insight or cost per automated workflow.

A software testing practice that checks small, isolated pieces of code such as a single method or function against expected behavior; fast and cheap, but blind to integration and user-interface failures.
The governance layer of Databricks that provides centralized access control, auditing, lineage and discovery across workspaces.
Information that does not follow a predefined data model, such as chat messages, meeting transcripts and documents, which large language models can now analyze for patterns.

Custom routes in an Azure route table, associated with a subnet, that override Azure's default system routes, for example to send outbound traffic through a firewall or virtual appliance as the next hop.

User experience design is a user-centered approach to designing products around usability, accessibility and how people perceive and use them; in the episode it is applied to Power Apps business applications.
A lean method for visualizing how material, information and decisions flow through a product family, including process steps, queues and handoffs.

VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) is an EU legislative package that modernises the VAT system with three pillars: digital reporting and e-invoicing, platform economy rules and single VAT registration. The episode treats it as a shift to continuous transaction controls.
Microsoft event-driven programming language built into most desktop Microsoft Office applications, used for example to automate tasks in Excel.
Vector search finds data by similarity of embeddings rather than exact matches and is a foundation for retrieval-augmented AI applications; Azure SQL Database and SQL Server 2025 support it natively.
A database optimized for searching embeddings by meaning rather than exact words, used as memory for retrieval-augmented generation.
Veeam is a vendor of third-party backup and recovery software for hybrid and multi-cloud environments.
In Dynamics 365, a vendor posting profile defines which general ledger accounts vendor transactions post to, based on rules set for a vendor or vendor group.
Digital credentials based on W3C open standards that let an issuer make a claim about a holder, which the holder can present and a verifier can check, optionally disclosing only what is needed.
VertiPaq is the in-memory columnar storage engine used by Power BI import models, which compresses data column by column for fast queries.
Term for disciplined, AI-assisted software and agent development in which experienced engineers own setup, security and governance, contrasted in the episode with casual vibe coding.
Virtual desktop infrastructure hosts desktops on central servers or in the cloud, and users connect to them remotely; user profiles and app data must load quickly from central storage.
A complete computer simulated inside another computer, with its own operating system, memory and storage; it offers stronger isolation than a container but is larger and slower to start.
A Microsoft-managed data gateway that connects Power BI and Microsoft Fabric to data sources inside an Azure virtual network, without installing gateway software on a machine.

Azure feature that connects two virtual networks so traffic between them flows privately over the Microsoft backbone; global peering connects virtual networks across Azure regions. Peered networks need non-overlapping address spaces, and peering is not transitive.
An Azure Virtual Network feature that restricts access to Azure services so only traffic from a chosen virtual network subnet is allowed, while the service keeps its public endpoint.

A virtual private network (VPN) creates an encrypted tunnel from a remote device into a private network over an untrusted network such as the internet, traditionally used for remote access to company resources.

Component that translates Dataverse requests for a virtual table into calls to an external system and returns the results as Dataverse rows; Dataverse includes an OData v4 provider and supports custom providers.

desc.ar: بيئة التطوير المتكاملة من Microsoft لبناء تطبيقات .NET وغيرها، وتتضمن تكامل GitHub Copilot.

desc.en: Microsoft Viva app for corporate communicators that centralizes campaign management, publishing and reporting across channels such as Outlook, Teams and SharePoint.
Microsoft Viva app that serves as the employee experience front door, bringing company news, resources and tools into a dashboard inside Microsoft Teams.
Microsoft Viva app for organization-wide employee engagement surveys with benchmarking and analytics.
A virtual local area network divides a switched network into separate logical networks; enforcing access between VLANs still requires routed controls such as firewalls.
VMware is a virtualization vendor whose vCenter-managed virtual machines are one of the main on-premises sources that Azure Migrate discovers, assesses and replicates.
In Dynamics 365 Finance, a shared reference that links a source document, its subledger accounting entries and the resulting general ledger entries, so amounts can be traced back to their origin.
Vulnerability management is the ongoing process of identifying, prioritizing and remediating security weaknesses in software and systems, closely tied to patch management.
Weak ties are looser relationships with people outside one’s close working circle; they connect different groups and let information, help and innovation travel across an organization.
Web resources are files such as JavaScript, HTML or CSS stored in Dataverse and used to extend model-driven app forms; PCF code components are the more governed, modern alternative.

Web roles in Microsoft Power Pages are sets of permissions assigned to site users, such as authenticated or anonymous users, that control access to site pages and, together with table permissions, to Dataverse data.
Web Authentication (WebAuthn) is a W3C web standard that gives websites an API to authenticate users with public-key credentials such as passkeys instead of passwords.
WebSocket is a communications protocol that provides a persistent, two-way channel over a single TCP connection; the episode contrasts it with polling-based connectors.
Who knows whom is a Dynamics 365 Sales relationship intelligence feature that suggests colleagues who have previously communicated with a lead or contact, enabling warm introductions.
A version of Windows 365 for shift and part-time workers in which one license serves Cloud PCs used by several people at different times, so organizations pay for concurrency rather than headcount.
Windows 365 Link is a Microsoft hardware device built to connect users directly to their Windows 365 Cloud PC, without local apps, user files or a local admin account.

Windows App is Microsoft's client app for connecting to Azure Virtual Desktop, Windows 365, Microsoft Dev Box, Remote Desktop Services and remote PCs from Windows, macOS, iOS, Android and web browsers.

A Microsoft managed service that sits on top of Intune and Windows Update for Business, creating update rings, monitoring rollouts and pausing them when health signals turn bad. Policy decisions, exclusions and accountability stay with the organization.

The newer, simpler flavor of Windows Autopilot that groups and configures a device the moment it enrolls, without pre-registering a hardware hash; it supports Microsoft Entra join only and runs on Windows 11.

A collection of Microsoft technologies used to set up and pre-configure new Windows devices and enroll them into Microsoft Intune, with deployment modes such as user-driven, self-deploying and pre-provisioning.

A Windows 10/11 Enterprise edition for Azure Virtual Desktop that lets multiple users hold interactive sessions on one virtual machine at the same time. Its use depends on eligible Windows Enterprise or Microsoft 365 licenses.

The managed business version of Windows Hello that replaces passwords with a device-bound key pair, unlocked by a PIN or biometrics, to sign users into Microsoft Entra ID or Active Directory work accounts.
Windows Local Administrator Password Solution (LAPS) gives every device a unique, regularly rotated local administrator password stored in the directory with restricted read access.
An opt-in Windows feature on Copilot+ PCs that saves encrypted snapshots of the screen locally and lets users search their past activity in natural language.
A Windows Server role for downloading, approving and distributing Microsoft updates from an internal server; Configuration Manager uses it for patch management.
Microsoft's server operating system, whose licensing can be applied at the physical host level and, where eligible, used in Azure via Azure Hybrid Benefit.

A Windows feature that runs a Linux environment directly on a Windows PC without a separate traditional virtual machine or dual-boot setup; WSL 2 uses a real Linux kernel in a lightweight virtual machine.
A set of policy controls built into Windows that lets organizations defer updates, set installation deadlines and control restarts, with devices downloading updates directly from Windows Update.
WinUI is Microsoft's native XAML-based UI framework for Windows desktop apps and part of the Windows App SDK.
Work in progress is material or product that has started its production route but is not yet finished; too much WIP ties up material and space and hides problems in the flow.
Work IQ is Microsoft's intelligence layer that grounds Microsoft 365 Copilot and agents in an organization's work context and data.
A job record that follows a maintenance or repair task from the first report to completion, holding tasks, assigned workers, required parts, status and costs.
Workday is a cloud-based enterprise application suite from Workday, Inc. for human capital management and finance, built around configurable business processes, routing and approvals.

desc.de: Agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot, der aus natürlicher Sprache Automatisierungen für Outlook, Teams, SharePoint und Planner erstellt (Frontier-Status).

desc.en: Workload identity federation lets workloads outside Azure, such as GitHub Actions pipelines, exchange a trusted external token for a short-lived Microsoft Entra access token without storing secrets.
Workplace loneliness describes low connection, thin trust and weak relational redundancy among people at work, which can persist even in highly connected and productive teams.

Elected body of employee representatives that, in Germany and other EU countries, holds information, consultation or co-determination rights over workplace changes such as technical monitoring systems.
A workstream in Dynamics 365 unified routing defines how one kind of incoming work, such as chat, voice, messaging or records, is taken in, classified, routed to queues and assigned to agents.
Dutch Microsoft partner where Femke Cornelissen works as Chief Transformation Officer.
Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF) is Microsoft's XAML-based UI framework for building Windows desktop applications on .NET.
The programming language used to develop and customize Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations (formerly Dynamics AX/Axapta).
A standard digital certificate format; devices can prove their identity with an X.509 certificate and private key, for example during the TLS handshake with Azure IoT Hub.
A Visual Studio extension created by Reza Niroomand that lets developers define and register Power Platform (Dataverse) plug-ins and custom APIs as code, for example through C# attributes.
A free, open-source unit testing framework for .NET languages such as C#, F# and Visual Basic, also used for integration tests.
YAML is a human-readable text format for configuration files that relies on spacing and indentation; GitHub Actions workflows are written in it.
YubiKey is a hardware security key made by Yubico that can store passkeys and serve as a phishing-resistant backup credential.
A Microsoft email protection capability that re-evaluates delivered messages and moves them to junk or quarantine when their verdict later changes to phishing or malware.

Applications or flows that were created and then abandoned but never retired, so they keep their data connections and permissions, consume resources and create attack surface without delivering value.
A governance model that groups environments into risk zones, often green, yellow and red, with increasing restrictions and IT approval from personal experimentation to production agents.
